tools.name: 1Code
tools.tagline: Orchestration layer for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex)
tools.valueProp: A Cursor-styled Electron client that wraps Claude Code and Codex behind a shared kanban board, worktree-per-chat isolation and a REST API for firing agents from CI. Sunset after two months of releases; its GitHub-triggered PR-review automations and phone PWA for background agents were unusual among actively maintained tools.

pricing.notes: Building from source and running locally with your own Claude/OpenAI login or API keys was free. A paid 1code.dev subscription (reported on Show HN as $20/mo, with a $200/mo 'Max' tier) unlocked pre-built releases, cloud background agents and Automations. Pricing page is no longer reachable; figures are from HN commenters, not the vendor site.

featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: README: 'Git Worktree Isolation - Each chat session runs in its own isolated worktree'; a dedicated 'Run coding agents the right way' section repeats this as the mechanism for branch safety (no accidental commits to main). Confirmed by a third-party guide (verdent.ai, June 2026) describing per-session worktrees as optional-but-core to how parallel agents avoid colliding.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False, agent-side only. src/main/lib/plugins/index.ts shows the README's 'Plugin Marketplace' is a reader for Claude Code's own plugin format: it scans ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/*/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json and surfaces each plugin's commands/skills/agents and bundled .mcp.json MCP servers in a settings tab (agents-plugins-tab.tsx). It manages Claude Code plugins already installed via the CLI ecosystem; there is no first-party API for third-party code to add panels, views, commands or providers to 1Code's own Electron UI. Documented in src/main/lib/plugins/index.ts (github.com/21st-dev/1code).
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Local mode (build from source, BYOK, local execution, 'no cloud sync required' per README) has no vendor-server dependency. Background agents, the Automations engine and the public API run in 1code.dev's vendor-managed cloud sandboxes with no documented self-hosted alternative, so the product as a whole is only partly independent of vendor infrastructure.
featureNotes.pricing.model: README installation section frames two paths explicitly: 'Build from source (free)' vs. 'Subscribe to 1code.dev (recommended)' for pre-built releases plus background-agent support; the README also states 'Automations require a Pro or Max subscription'. Dollar figures ($20/mo, $200/mo 'Max') come from Show HN commenters (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46637723), not a live pricing page.

top.title: Show HN: 1Code – Open-source Cursor-like UI for Claude Code

editorial.reachRationale: a 75-point/49-comment Show HN launch, ~5.6k GitHub stars and 612 forks over a ~7-week public life, but only 19 contributors, no npm/registry download signal, an expired Discord invite, and zero commits or releases in the 90 days before the repo was archived, evidence of an early-adopter audience that never reached an established user base before shutdown. Stars discounted somewhat as a viral-launch artifact typical of Show HN posts.
editorial.polishRationale: A full Electron/React desktop app (Monaco editor, node-pty terminal, Radix UI) with diff previews, a built-in git client, PWA companion and a documented API shipped in under two months, but it never left v0.0.x, the public repo lagged the private desktop source (one release commit reads 'Manual sync from private repo desktop source'), and the marketing site redirected into the archived repo as of September 2026, with no lasting docs site.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes beyond a terminal wrapper with worktree isolation, a kanban session board, chat forking, plan mode, an automations rule engine (GitHub/Linear/Slack triggers) and a programmatic task API, but merge-conflict handling and cross-agent messaging are undocumented and the plugin surface is a reader for Claude Code's own plugin format rather than a native extension system.
editorial.feelRationale: Standard Electron/Chromium stack (electron-vite, React, Monaco, node-pty) per package.json; no maker performance claims or first-party benchmarks found, and a targeted search for user reports of 1Code's own UI speed turned up nothing specific (only generic Claude Code/Codex agent-latency complaints unrelated to this client). Scored as a typical, unremarkable Electron app with no evidence of jank or of standout speed.

status.overrideReason: GitHub repository banner: 'This repository was archived by the owner on Jul 7, 2026. It is now read-only.' The last commit was 2026-02-24 and the last release (v0.0.84) 2026-03-06; the 1code.dev marketing site redirects to the archived GitHub repo and the project's Discord invite has expired.

tools.name: Agent of Empires
tools.tagline: Run your AI coding agents in parallel, and manage them from one place.
tools.valueProp: One local Rust service drives the same tmux and worktree sessions from a TUI or browser. Its phone PWA adds live terminal control, ACP approval cards, and QR-paired HTTPS access through your own tunnel.

maker.name: Agent of Empires community
maker.funding: Supported by Mozilla.ai

pricing.notes: AoE is free and open source; users supply their coding-agent installations and subscriptions.

featureNotes.platforms.windows: The README supports Windows only through WSL2; no native Windows release exists.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: Phone access is an installable web PWA, not an App Store or TestFlight app.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Phone access is an installable web PWA, not a Play Store or APK app.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Run aoe serve on a machine you control and connect by LAN/VPN or HTTPS tunnel; agents stay on that machine.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Custom agent commands can be configured in AoE rather than requiring one of the named agents.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: The diff view marks unmerged files and shows conflict changes, but documented merge and conflict resolution remains in external git/editor tools.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: The HTTP API lets an external orchestrator create, prompt, and read sessions as controlled subagents; the docs do not describe automatic delegation by an agent in the default UI.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Plugin workers can react to events and create structured sessions, but scheduling requires an installed plugin or external orchestrator.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: aoe send and the HTTP API can address another session; there is no documented agent-to-agent mailbox or conversation layer.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: A separate experimental CityHall v0.1.0 control plane adds accounts, roles, and SSO; the core aoe dashboard uses shared token/passphrase access.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: The TUI and web dashboard drive the same live sessions; the web dashboard offers authenticated and read-only links for another viewer.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: The server and agents run on the user machine; remote HTTPS uses optional user-controlled Tailscale/Cloudflare tunnels, while LAN/VPN access works without them.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Third-party code extends AoE itself: documented aoe-plugin.toml manifests and JSON-RPC workers add commands, keybindings, themes, settings, dockable panes, notifications, and session automation. See docs/plugins.md, docs/development/writing-plugins.md, and docs/plugin-api.md; install from GitHub or a local directory.

github.description: Manage multiple Claude Code, OpenCode agents from either TUI or Web for easy access on mobile. Also supports Mistral Vibe, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Pi.dev, Copilot CLI, Factory Droid Coding.

top.title: Show HN: Agent-of-empires: OpenCode and Claude Code session manager

activity.changelogCadence: weekly: 16 releases in 90 days, including 7 in September 2026

editorial.reachRationale: 120 contributors, 264 Homebrew installs in 30 days, 1,847 downloads from five release assets, and a 118-point Show HN support an established user base. I discounted 3,294 stars as attention and the 5,567-member Discord because it belongs to Mozilla Open Source AI, not AoE.
editorial.polishRationale: My call from hands-on use: it is just fine, not a standout. Stable 1.17.2 releases, broad platform and agent docs, token-protected remote access, push notifications, mobile layouts and a documented plugin SDK show a well-maintained product, but the finish stops at solid.
editorial.depthRationale: It reaches beyond tmux through managed worktrees, containers, ACP structured views, diff comments, API control, remote phone access, and plugin workers; the separate CityHall team layer remains experimental.
editorial.feelRationale: The TUI is native Rust, and the live VT path streams tmux output through a persistent channel with near-attach latency instead of polling. The web terminal falls back to 50 ms capture-pane polling on older tmux or unsupported panes, and release notes record mobile scroll and repaint fixes, so performance is strong with known edge cases.

tools.name: Agent Orchestrator
tools.tagline: Stop babysitting agents. Start merging real work.
tools.valueProp: Closes the GitHub loop itself: it watches every worker’s pull request and pushes CI failures, review comments and merge conflicts back to the agent that owns the branch. Free on desktop and phone, but single-user and local only.

maker.name: Untrivial.ai (Prateek Karnal)
maker.funding: No announced round. Started inside Composio (packages renamed from @composio to @aoagents in April 2026), under founder Prateek Karnal's Untrivial.ai; revenue is paid design-partner pilots at $500-2,000/month.

pricing.notes: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); no plans, accounts or pricing page. Agents run on the provider CLIs and subscriptions you already have; AO does not proxy API calls. A design-partner program sells paid pilots at $500-2,000/month for teams of 10-100 engineers, and 'AO Cloud' (shared sessions, hosted runs) is waitlist-only.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Electron app, Apple silicon and Intel DMG/ZIP from GitHub Releases or `brew install agentwrapper/tap/agent-orchestrator` (own tap, not homebrew-core). tmux required for Terminal UI sessions.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: x64 installer; Terminal UI runs through a ConPTY host, no tmux needed.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: x64 AppImage, .deb and .rpm; tmux required for Terminal UI.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: 'AO Mobile' on the App Store (changelog 0.13.0: 'went live on both app stores'). Companion only: it pairs with a desktop-run daemon and cannot run agents itself.
featureNotes.platforms.android: 'AO Mobile' on Google Play; same companion role as iOS.
featureNotes.platforms.web: No browser UI ships. The desktop app is Electron-only; the Next.js 'Cloud UI' in the repo is flag-gated behind the AO Cloud waitlist.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: Optional Go `ao` CLI (spawn, send, session, pr, review, preview, browser) that talks to the desktop-owned loopback daemon; docs say the desktop app 'requires no global ao command'. The npm `@aoagents/ao` package is frozen at 0.10.0 and only launches the desktop build.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: The 'Terminal UI' mode is the agent's own TUI (Claude Code, Codex...) hosted inside the Electron app over tmux/ConPTY; AO has no full-screen terminal interface of its own.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Only the phone attaches remotely: the mobile app connects over LAN or Tailscale to the daemon your desktop app runs. Docs say the desktop daemon is loopback-only, 'do not expose AO on a remote server', and AO 'does not turn the local desktop product into a hosted multi-user service'.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: AO Cloud (shared sessions, hosted runs) is a waitlist. Changelog 0.13.0: the cloud control plane is in the monorepo but 'everything is flag-gated; nothing changes for local-only users yet'.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: The Go daemon and its opt-in 'Connect Mobile' LAN listener are the only server; the phone connects to it directly and there is no vendor relay. Mobile push notifications transit Expo's push service.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Terminal UI plus structured Chat (via claude-agent-acp); one of two harnesses that can hand off between Chat and TUI in the same session.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Terminal UI plus native app-server Chat; Chat/TUI handoff supported. Settings manage multiple Codex accounts.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Not in the daemon's 27-harness catalog (docs/plugins/agents). A Gemini icon appears in the homepage mockup only.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Listed as `copilot` in the catalog; Terminal UI only.
featureNotes.agents.opencode: Terminal UI plus native ACP Chat; also a supported reviewer harness.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Cursor Agent CLI in Terminal UI; a Cursor ACP chat driver landed in 0.13.0.
featureNotes.agents.pi: Terminal UI; Pi Chat via the pi-acp adapter is admitted only with a per-session bypass-permissions fallback (docs/STATUS.md).
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Adapters are compiled into the daemon: 'There is no plugin marketplace or ao plugin install command' and no custom-command adapter. The marketing FAQ's 'if it runs in a terminal, it runs in AO' is not backed by the docs.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: The per-project 'orchestrator' is a role, not an agent: it runs on whichever installed harness you configure (e.g. `--orchestrator-agent claude-code`). AO ships no model routing of its own.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: One worktree and branch per Git-backed session, base branch resolved from the remote's default; `postCreate` hooks, `symlinks` and `env` per project; cleanup never force-deletes a dirty worktree.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: No per-task container or sandbox. Reviewer docs state 'native modes, autonomous settings, and prompts are not OS or network containment'.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Branch created with the worktree; `ao spawn --branch` overrides the name. Scratch sessions get an AO-managed branchless directory.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Changed-files inspector with a virtualized diff viewer (0.13.0), file explorer, image before/after; diffs recompute their merge base after rebases.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: The worker agent opens the PR through your `gh` login; AO then claims it (`ao session claim-pr`) and observes it. No AO-side 'create PR' action is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: `ao pr merge` / desktop merge action plus `resolve-comments`; when the observer sees a merge conflict it 'asks the eligible session to rebase and resolve it'. Merge is never automatic.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Chat sessions carry conversation 'compaction and rollback state' (provider-level rewind); no file or worktree snapshot feature is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Homepage and llms.txt claim 10+ concurrent workers per repo; every session appears on one live board.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: The Kanban is the primary screen: Working / Needs you / In review / Ready to merge columns derived from session, PR, CI and review facts. GitHub issue intake can feed it (opt-in, assignee-scoped).
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: The project orchestrator session 'can break [a plan] into focused tasks, spawn or redirect workers, pass each worker the relevant context, follow their progress'.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: No cron. Event-triggered only: opt-in GitHub issue intake creates a worker when an issue is assigned to the configured user, and the SCM observer sends CI-failure / review / conflict nudges to the owning session. llms.txt mentions cron-like 'automations' but the docs do not.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Durable notification center plus Electron toasts, attention sound and macOS Dock bounce for needs-input and merge-ready; mobile push (via Expo/APNs/FCM) when an agent is waiting for input. Slack/Discord/webhook notifiers from the legacy release are 'not supported in the rewrite'.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: `ao send --session <id>` works from inside a session (sender identity is prefixed when AO_SESSION_ID is set); the orchestrator redirects workers the same way.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Hold-to-talk dictation in the mobile app only, on-device STT (iOS SFSpeechRecognizer / Android SpeechRecognizer). Nothing documented for desktop.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Architecture docs: 'a local, single-user system'. No accounts. Shared sessions and team handoffs are the AO Cloud waitlist pitch.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Anyone with the Connect Mobile password sees the same daemon, but that is one person's phone, not a collaboration feature; 'shared agent sessions' are waitlist-only.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: No self-serve team plan. A design-partner program sells paid pilots ($500-2,000/month, month-to-month) with founder-led onboarding.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Apache-2.0 on the whole monorepo (desktop, daemon, CLI, mobile, and the flag-gated cloud control plane).
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: No vendor server in the local path; the only third-party hops are Expo/APNs/FCM for mobile push and PostHog for telemetry.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Uses the agent CLIs and logins already on your machine; 'AO doesn't proxy any API calls' and bundles no provider CLIs.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Desktop/daemon PostHog telemetry is documented and disabled with AO_TELEMETRY_RENDERER/EVENTS/REMOTE=off (or a build with an empty PostHog key). The mobile app has no in-app opt-out, and the privacy page's 'no analytics SDKs' claim for mobile contradicts docs/telemetry.md and the 0.13.0 changelog (PostHog + Sentry on mobile). Telemetry also records the GitHub owner of each project, which for personal repos is your username.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False, nothing of the sort for the app itself. /docs/plugins states AO's harness/runtime/tracker/notifier/workspace 'adapters' are compiled into the Go backend, are 'not npm plugins and cannot be installed through a marketplace', and the legacy agent-orchestrator.yaml plugin/notifier/runtime/workspace/tracker/SCM config blocks are inactive in the rewrite. There is no documented way for third-party code to add a panel, command, provider or theme to AO's own dashboard/CLI. Documented at https://orchestrator.inc/docs/plugins and /docs/cli ('no plugin marketplace').
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Loopback REST API with a generated OpenAPI spec plus an SSE event stream and WebSocket terminal mux, driven by the `ao` CLI; unauthenticated and pinned to 127.0.0.1. No MCP server or SDK is documented.

github.description: Open-source (Apache-2.0) orchestrator for Claude Code, Codex & 30+ coding agents. Plan, run and supervise agent teams from task to merged PR. Desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux) + iPhone & Android apps.

hn.query: Agent Orchestrator local-first Harness Engineering control plane

top.title: Show HN: Agent Orchestrator, a local-first Harness Engineering control plane

editorial.reachRationale: 112 contributors and 10,372 release-asset downloads show real development traction, but the product-specific Discord (2,317 members) and X (2,725 followers) are small and the one Show HN landed at just 15 points, so this reads as early attention rather than an established community.
editorial.polishRationale: The product is mid-rewrite from TypeScript to Go and the docs say so on almost every page ('not all available in the current daemon rewrite'), the site cannot agree on how many harnesses it supports (23, 24, 25 and 27 on different pages), llms.txt advertises cron automations the docs do not, the privacy page and telemetry doc contradict each other about mobile analytics, 0.12.0 shipped a macOS file-descriptor leak, and 0.13.0 lists 409 fixes. Against that: three desktop platforms plus two app stores, stable and nightly channels with in-app updates, a Homebrew tap, eight UI languages, and a dated changelog. Rated from docs and release notes, not hands-on use.
editorial.depthRationale: This goes well beyond a session switcher: A persistent per-project orchestrator agent plans and spawns workers, a live Kanban derives each card from session, PR, CI and review facts, a GitHub observer routes failing checks, requested changes and merge conflicts back to the owning agent, reviewer agents run against worker PRs, each worker gets an isolated agent-drivable browser, Chat and the agent's native TUI can swap inside one session, and native iOS/Android apps pair with the daemon. Rated from docs and release notes, not hands-on use.
editorial.feelRationale: Architecture doc: 'The Electron/React desktop app, optional CLI, and Expo mobile app are thin clients over the daemon's HTTP, SSE, and terminal interfaces' run by a long-running Go daemon (tmux/conpty terminal mux) -- a typical Electron-over-backend stack. No maker performance claims and no user reports of lag or notable speed turned up in the docs or a targeted web/GitHub search.

tools.name: Agent Teams
tools.tagline: You're the boss, agents are your team.
tools.valueProp: An AGPL Electron app built around a live five-column kanban where Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Cursor agents plan, claim, message each other and review their own tasks, with hunk-level accept/reject before anything lands. The unit of work is a card, not a session.

pricing.notes: The desktop UI itself is free OSS with no account. A bundled free model works with no signup, API key or card; connecting Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, SuperGrok, GitHub Copilot, Z.AI, MiniMax or Kiro uses subscriptions/API keys the user already has. No team/billing tier exists.

featureNotes.platforms.web: Roadmap/docs (as of September 2026) note 'the desktop app is the main product; the web version is currently in active development.' A shipped 'limited standalone dashboard for local or trusted-network use' exists, but the docs explicitly say it has no built-in auth and isn't meant for public exposure.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Same standalone HTTP dashboard: reachable over a trusted network, but the docs explicitly warn it lacks authentication and is not intended for exposing to the public internet.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: No cloud backend exists ('there is no Agent Teams cloud backend for storing your code'), but the only server-style surface is the unauthenticated local/trusted-network dashboard above, so this is short of a full self-hostable server product.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Ships a bundled free model reachable with no signup, API key or card, in addition to the named third-party runtime connectors.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Docs (Git worktree strategy guide) and FAQ confirm worktree isolation is available per teammate at launch, but it's an opt-in choice, not the default for every team.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Agents create and manage their own tasks and can message/delegate to teammates, but team composition (which agents exist) is set up by the human, not spawned autonomously by an agent, a softer form of the subagents pattern than a single agent recursively spawning others.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Auto-resume after Claude rate limits (nudges the lead once the cooldown passes) is already shipped; the roadmap's '24/7 autonomous teams in the cloud' item is explicitly listed as in progress, not shipped.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: The maker's own written vision describes future phone/voice control of the lead agent, but this is aspirational roadmap language, not a shipped feature.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False, nothing shipped yet for the app itself. The README's roadmap section lists 'a secure universal plugin system regardless of the type of agents' as an unchecked, not-yet-built checkbox item, separate from the MCP/agent support that already ships (see apiOrMcp). No panels, commands, providers or themes can be added by third-party code; there is no plugins/extensions folder or SDK in the repo. Documented at https://github.com/777genius/agent-teams-ai#readme (Roadmap section).

You just watch the kanban board and give high-level commands. top.title: Show HN: VS Code Agent Kanban: Task Management for the AI-Assisted Developer

activity.changelogCadence: near-weekly (13 releases in the trailing 90 days)

editorial.reachRationale: A real, active Discord (218 members, 23 online) and 35 GitHub contributors (unusually high for a solo-founder project whose repo was created in February 2026) show genuine community pull beyond the founder, but there's no product-specific HN thread (the top HN hit for a broad query is an unrelated 'VS Code Agent Kanban' Show HN, and a direct 'agentteams.live' query returns zero stories) and no registry/download data since it ships only as GitHub Release binaries. Stars (2.2K, smallest of the three researched tools) are discounted. This lands as emerging: more product-specific traction than a one-person niche tool, but well short of an established community with its own visible online discourse.
editorial.polishRationale: A dedicated multi-language docs site (docs.agentteams.live) with guided walkthroughs, a maintained release-notes reference, and a professionally structured README with an explicit competitor comparison table, all consistent with the unusually high contributor count and commit velocity for the repo's age.
editorial.depthRationale: Its kanban board with 5 real-time columns, hunk-level diff review, per-teammate worktree isolation, cross-team messaging, a notification/badge system, and MCP support, going well beyond a thin CLI wrapper.
editorial.feelRationale: Electron 40 + React 19 + Zustand 4 desktop shell (typical Electron territory, not native/GPU-rendered). The maker documents an `AGENT_TEAMS_DISABLE_GPU=1` workaround for 'Linux app freezes or shows a blank window over RDP' caused by virtual GPU drivers breaking Electron rendering, real but scoped to a specific remote-desktop/virtual-GPU edge case rather than a general slowness report, so this sits at the standard Electron baseline rather than being marked down further.

tools.name: AionUi
tools.tagline: One desktop. Your AI agents, actually coworking.
tools.valueProp: An office-document app first: built-in assistants turn a prompt into an editable PPT, Word or Excel file, on top of 20-plus wrapped CLI agents reachable from Telegram, Lark and WeChat. No worktrees, containers or PR flow; coding agents are guests here.

pricing.notes: App and its Multi-Agent Mode are free and open source; BYOK Mode (your own API keys) has no AionUi fee and is not routed through AionUi's servers. An optional Prepaid Mode routes requests through AionUi's backend and deducts token usage from a purchased Balance at 'AionUi's then-current token pricing'; no public price list or tiers page was found.

featureNotes.platforms.android: Terms of Service describe 'the AionUi desktop application for macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, etc.' and the WebUI guide documents running the desktop build under Termux/proot on Android, but there is no Play Store app or APK; this is a workaround, not a shipped mobile client.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: `AionUi --webui` / `--resetpass` are flags on the desktop binary, and a standalone `aionui-web` CLI tarball (or `bun run webui`) starts the headless WebUI server; neither is a CLI for creating or steering agent tasks.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: WebUI Configuration Guide documents cross-network access via Tailscale, LAN access with `--remote`, and systemd server deployment on a machine you control; the desktop app and the standalone `aionui-web` server share the same feature set.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: The WebUI (desktop-bundled `--webui` flag or the standalone `aionui-web` package) is a self-hostable server component with its own SQLite data dir, admin password, and Docker deployment shown by a third-party image on Docker Hub.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Wiki: 'other ACP backends with mcpCapabilities.stdio are auto-supported' for Team Mode; there is no documented generic 'point at any executable' adapter outside that ACP compatibility path.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: The Preview Panel renders `.diff`/`.patch` files among its 10+ supported formats (README, and a third-party review calls it a 'diff viewer'), but no first-party page describes a dedicated review flow (approve/reject, inline comments) tied to a git diff.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Team Mode gives Teammates 'a shared task board' during a run (README), but there is no persistent kanban/queue feeding tasks into the app generally.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Sidebar badges show pending permission approvals per agent (README), and Scheduled Tasks/FAQ mention reminder notifications, but no page documents a general 'agent is blocked on input' alert across channels.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: BYOK Mode runs entirely on-device with no AionUi server in the path (Privacy Policy: 'AionUi does not see, route, or log' BYOK interactions); Prepaid Mode, if used, depends on AionUi's backend.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False, agent-side only. AionUi's 'Extension SDK' contributes only 'Extension' skills, one of three Markdown SKILL.md sources (Built-in, Custom, Extension) attached to backend assistants from Settings → Skills; the wiki states Skills are 'Markdown only, no code execution unless the Skill explicitly invokes a tool.' This is skill bundling for the agent, not extension of AionUi's own Electron/React interface, no documented way to add panels, views, commands or providers to the app itself (a repo code search for an Extension SDK/code directory turned up none). Documented at https://github.com/iOfficeAI/AionUi/wiki/AI-Assistants-Ecosystem-Guide.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: AionUi is an MCP client (imports/manages external MCP servers per agent) and ships an internal 'Team MCP Server' for Leader/Teammate coordination, but no public API or externally-callable MCP server for controlling AionUi itself was found.

top.title: Show HN: AionUi – Open-Source Cowork for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex and More

activity.changelogCadence: near-daily (35 releases in the trailing 90 days)

editorial.reachRationale: 33.1k stars (Trendshift trending) are discounted, but 930 open issues and 115 contributors on a repo created in August 2025 corroborate a genuinely large, actively-complaining user base rather than a star-bombed launch, and 35 releases in 90 days shows a maintainer keeping pace with it. Discounted heavily: X (46 followers), Discord (714 members) and its own Show HN (2 points) are all thin, and the loudest third-party coverage (a personal blog, a low-engagement Reddit thread) reads as early-adopter, not mainstream.
editorial.polishRationale: Signed installers for macOS/Windows/Linux plus a Homebrew cask, a professional bilingual marketing site, and a 21-assistant/skills system that clearly got design attention, but a filed bug (#534) describes 15-30s startup and the UI becoming 'unusable' after a few turns, and a first-party reviewer notes there's no official Fedora package and a ~330MB Electron footprint. These are real rough edges on a product whose repo dates to August 2025.
editorial.depthRationale: Team Mode gives teammates a shared task board, subagents and cross-agent messaging; scheduled tasks and a self-hosted WebUI extend it beyond parallel sessions. Diff review is limited to previewing .diff and .patch files, and no dedicated PR or merge flow is documented.
editorial.feelRationale: Electron app (TypeScript is 10.4M of the repo's language bytes per `gh api .../languages`, versus far smaller JS/CSS) with no native-rendering claims from the maker. GitHub issue #534 ('AionUI is very slow to open and very very laggy to use in general... becomes impossible to use') describes multi-second startup and typing lag after several turns; no first-party performance claims or user praise for speed were found to offset it.

tools.name: Amp
tools.tagline: Amp is the frontier agent and development environment that lets you build from anywhere.
tools.valueProp: An agent that brings its own fleet: every thread gets a vendor cloud machine that sleeps for free and wakes on a Slack message or schedule, and teammates can join the same terminal. Runs only its own agent and rejects worktrees on principle.

maker.name: Amp Frontier Corporation (spun out of Sourcegraph, Dec 2025)
maker.funding: Spun out of Sourcegraph on 2025-12-02 as an independent company; says it is profitable. Investors listed on /about: Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia, Felicis, Redpoint, Craft Ventures, Goldcrest Capital.

pricing.notes: Hobby tier is free (since 2026-09-13 'Free Agent'): all product features, bring your own keys or ChatGPT/other subscriptions with no Amp token fees, orbs pay-as-you-go by the minute, or run agents free on your own runner machines. Individual tiers Megawatt ($20/mo, 45,000 orb minutes) and Gigawatt (price shown behind a toggle, not captured); education discount $10/mo. Teams: no extra charge, members mix tiers, pooled credits, SSO when one member is paid. Enterprise: custom pricing, pooled credits only, SCIM, audit logs, MCP allowlist, self-hosted orbs. Model inference through Amp credits is billed at provider API prices with no markup for non-enterprise.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Native Mac app (beta, direct .dmg download, requires macOS 26 or later) plus the CLI/TUI.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: CLI only, and only through WSL; docs recommend WezTerm or Alacritty over Windows Terminal. No Windows desktop app.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: CLI/TUI only (curl install script or Homebrew tap). No Linux desktop app; the web app covers the rest.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: iPhone and iPad app is a public TestFlight beta (iOS 26+); docs say an App Store release will come later.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Docs list Mac, iPhone and iPad apps only; Android users get the responsive web app.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: The interactive `amp` CLI is a full-screen TUI with a command palette (Ctrl+O); the sidebar was removed in Aug 2026.
featureNotes.execution.local: `amp --executor local` (the default) runs the agent on your own machine from the CLI.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Runners: start `amp --no-tui --runner-id <id>` on any machine you own and create threads on it from ampcode.com, the apps or other agents; one runner can serve many directories. Portals, desktop and multiplayer are orb-only.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Orbs: Amp creates a sandboxed cloud machine per thread (sizes tiny to xxlarge), pauses it when idle at no cost and wakes it on the next message, webhook or schedule.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Enterprise-only 'self-hosted orbs' run the compute in your own GKE/EKS/AKS cluster, but ampcode.com still runs the conversation and relays file contents and command output. Nothing else is self-hostable.
featureNotes.agents.amp: This is Amp itself; it does not wrap other agents.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Plugins can define custom modes and subagents for Amp's own loop, but there is no adapter for running a third-party CLI agent as a thread.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Multi-model: modes low/medium/high/ultra route to GPT, Claude and other models; specialist subagents Search, Oracle, Librarian and Read Thread; Puck is a meta-agent that starts and steers threads.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: The homepage says 'Forget worktrees'. Isolation is one orb (machine) per thread instead; threads on a runner share that machine's checkout.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Each orb thread gets a fresh, isolated vendor-managed machine with the repository, setup script results and plugins; project snapshots are reused for up to 72 hours.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Default Ship behaviour is trunk-based (commit, rebase, test, push to main). The 'Push to Branch' project setting makes the agent create a short descriptively named branch per thread instead.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Changes pane with Review (walk the diff), Restack (rewrite into cleaner commits) and Sync (pull the orb's branch locally); the CLI got in-thread diff review and staging in June 2026.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: With 'Push to Branch' the agent pushes and reports a pull-request URL; the GitHub App connection lets the agent open pull requests itself. There is no dedicated PR button; the default Ship flow pushes straight to the base branch.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Default Ship rebases onto the latest base branch, resolves conflicts in the orb, re-pushes if the base moved, and checks with you before continuing on a substantive conflict.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Thread sidebar and Activity feed list every running thread across orbs, runners and local CLI; Puck can fan one request out to several agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: No kanban or queue. The Activity feed filters threads by status, author, label and project, and threads can be pinned, coloured, labelled and snoozed.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Agent to Agent: a thread can start other threads (in orbs, other projects or on runners), send them instructions and files, and collect results; Puck coordinates parallel agents from the web, apps or Slack.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Per-thread schedules set in natural language (once or repeating) plus plugin-registered webhooks that wake an orb on outside events such as GitHub pushes or Linear issues.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Mac and iOS apps notify when a thread is ready for your next message; Slack via Puck; CLI has an amp.notifications.enabled setting.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Agents in the same workspace can message each other and transfer files between threads.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Dictation on web and in the apps; 'Talk to Puck' realtime voice, exposed as a Siri/Shortcuts action; Space adds voice/video calls between people in a thread.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Workspaces with member/admin roles, invite links, SSO; Enterprise adds SCIM, groups and narrower roles.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Multiplayer: workspace members can prompt the same orb thread and use its terminal, portals and files for up to a week; @-tagging a teammate invites them. Space adds a voice/video/screen-share call per thread. Not available on runner threads.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Teams tier at no extra charge with pooled credits, per-member tiers, usage analytics; Enterprise with pooled credits only.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Closed source. Only side projects (amp.nvim, official-plugins, SDK demo, Homebrew tap) are public under github.com/ampcode.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Threads, auth and orchestration always go through ampcode.com; even Enterprise self-hosted orbs only move the compute.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Link a ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription or bring your own Anthropic/OpenAI keys with no Amp token fees on all non-Enterprise tiers; OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure Foundry, Vercel/Cloudflare gateways and custom endpoints in early access.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: The security page says telemetry is stored on Amp Server alongside threads; the CLI settings reference has no telemetry switch. Minimal Data Retention only covers model-provider inference.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: True, extends Amp's own app surface, not just the agent. The documented plugin API (loaded from .amp/plugins/ or ~/.config/amp/plugins/) exposes amp.registerCommand(...) to add entries to Amp's own command palette (with availability states) and ctx.ui.notify/confirm/input/select(...) to render real UI dialogs inside the app, plus registerLinkPattern(...) to change how the transcript view renders text, alongside the agent-side amp.registerTool/registerSkill and amp.on(session.start|agent.start|tool.call|tool.result|agent.end) hooks, which alone would not count. Documented at https://ampcode.com/docs/customize/plugins (component APIs) and https://ampcode.com/docs/customize/global-plugins-and-skills (distribution/sharing).
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: External REST API v2 with OAuth scopes (threads, workspace data), TypeScript and Python SDKs, and MCP servers configurable per user, workspace or orb.

top.title: Amp, Inc. – Amp is spinning out of Sourcegraph

tools.authorNote:
The polish is incredible, and it’s thoughtful and very good in its execution. They’re consistently three to six months ahead of the curve: sometimes they do things that don’t make sense to me, and then three months later I realize what they were up to. Probably the most AI-pilled team out there.

It’s worth keeping installed and trying, just so you understand what everyone else is going to be doing soon enough, even if it doesn’t fit your personal workflow just yet.

editorial.reachRationale: No GitHub signal (closed source), but @ampcode/cli alone shows ~109k npm downloads/month (plus older @sourcegraph/amp and @ampcode/sdk installs) and a 26k-follower product X account; a name known among practitioners of agentic coding tools from its Sourcegraph pedigree, but no Discord and modest HN (49 stories, 90-point launch) keep it below 'major'.
editorial.polishRationale: Native Mac and iPhone apps, a web app, a TUI and Slack all open the same thread; SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SCIM, a documented external API and SDKs; the news page ships several dated entries a week and the docs are unusually specific (timeouts, rate limits, billing rules). The apps are labelled beta as of September 2026, and Windows is WSL-only.
editorial.depthRationale: Per-thread cloud machines with pause/wake, live app portals, a shared tmux terminal, agent-to-agent delegation across orbs and runners, natural-language schedules and webhooks, multiplayer threads with voice/video, a meta-agent (Puck), workspace-published plugins and skills, and enterprise controls. What it deliberately lacks is a task board, worktrees and any way to run other vendors' agents.
editorial.feelRationale: Docs state 'Amp runs as a native app on your Mac, iPhone, and iPad,' sharing the same threads/orbs as the web app, and a search for slow/fast/laggy reports turned up no jank or lag complaints about the interface itself (only unrelated hits about dev-server load times and model/pricing gripes). Held back because the native-app claim is unverified against an actual rendering stack and the apps are labelled beta as of September 2026.

tools.name: Aperant
tools.tagline: Software that builds itself
tools.valueProp: A fixed Planner, Coder and QA pipeline that runs entirely on the Claude Code CLI you already pay for, then opens an AI-resolved merge from its worktree back to main; it wraps no other coding agent. The 14.6k-star open-source app is in maintenance mode, per its README, while the maker rebuilds it from scratch as a separate, unreleased paid cloud product.

pricing.notes: The desktop app is free; you bring your own Claude Pro/Max subscription and the Claude Code CLI, which do the actual model spend. Team and Enterprise plans (custom guardrails, audit trail, SSO/SAML) were added as 'Aperant Cloud' per the changelog, but no price list is published; the current aperant.com is a waitlist for a separate, unreleased Aperant 3.0 cloud product.

featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: 'Aperant Cloud' (changelog v2.4.0, Feb 2026) adds real-time team dashboards and shared issue queues, but the README describes agent execution as up to 12 local agent terminals; no page documents the vendor provisioning agent sandboxes.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: No relay/daemon/server component exists in the 2.x architecture to self-host in the first place, the app and its Claude Code CLI dependency both run entirely on the user's machine.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Requirements section: a Claude Pro/Max subscription and the `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` CLI are prerequisites; the app orchestrates that CLI rather than shipping its own model access.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Ships its own fixed three-role pipeline (Planner, Coder, QA agents) on top of the Claude Code CLI; README and feature table name no other coding-agent CLI as supported.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Changelog v2.2.0 (Jan 2026): 'Improved branch naming conventions from planner output', confirming automatic per-task branch creation inside each worktree.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: The Kanban board and agent-terminal screenshots in the README don't show a dedicated diff viewer, and no docs page (all return 404) confirms one either way.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Feature table: 'GitHub/GitLab Integration, Import issues, investigate with AI, create merge requests.'
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Feature table: 'AI-Powered Merge, Automatic conflict resolution when integrating back to main.'
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: No snapshot/rollback feature is named in the README, changelog or blog.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: README: 'up to 12 agent terminals'; changelog v2.1.0 (Dec 2025) originally shipped this as 'run up to 4 sessions simultaneously', so the cap has grown over time.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: README Interface section leads with 'Kanban Board, Visual task management from planning through completion.'
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: The Planner/Coder/QA roles are a fixed built-in pipeline stage sequence, not a documented mechanism for an agent to spawn or steer arbitrary other agents at runtime.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: No scheduled or event-triggered runs (cron, webhooks) are described anywhere read; the closest is GitHub/GitLab/Linear issue import, which is user-triggered.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Changelog: role-based access control and team management (v2.4.0), SSO/SAML for Enterprise (v2.3.0).
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Changelog v2.4.0 lists 'real-time team dashboards' and 'shared issue queues with priority ordering', which show team-wide progress but don't document two people steering the same live agent session.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Changelog v2.3.0: 'Custom guardrail rules (Team and Enterprise plans)'; no public price list found.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: The 2.x desktop app has no vendor server in its path at all (BYO Claude subscription, local-only execution). The optional 'Aperant Cloud' team tier is vendor-hosted with no self-host option documented.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Requirements: 'Claude Pro/Max subscription' plus the Claude Code CLI; Aperant does not resell model access.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: aperant.com/telemetry returns 404 and the privacy policy covers only the marketing/waitlist site, not the desktop app; no in-app telemetry documentation was found.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False, nothing of the sort. No plugin, extension, SDK, `plugins/` or `extensions/` directory, or third-party-code loading mechanism is mentioned anywhere in the README (features table, security model, interface descriptions), CONTRIBUTING.md, changelog or aperant.com marketing/waitlist page. There is no documented way to add a panel, command, provider or theme to Aperant itself. See https://github.com/AndyMik90/Aperant#readme.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: No API or MCP server is documented; /docs returns 404 site-wide.

github.description: Autonomous multi-session AI coding

top.title: Auto Claude - Autonomous multi-agent coding framework

activity.changelogCadence: roughly biweekly from Dec 2025 to Feb 2026 (v2.1.0 -> v2.4.0), no entries since

editorial.reachRationale: 5.1M release-asset downloads across the last five releases and 14.6k GitHub stars are real product-specific usage signals for a 25-contributor indie project, and the README/changelog document a mature feature set (SSO, audit trails, team plans) that implies paying customers existed. Discounted: stars and downloads accumulated during a 2025-2026 viral period and the Discord (2,307 members) is a general 'AI That Works' community, not Aperant-exclusive; its own Show HN post got 3 points and 0 comments, and the only self-reported user count ('10,000 users', a Jan 2026 blog post) is unverified and seven months stale, with no update since.
editorial.polishRationale: The README and changelog show a mature release process (SHA256 checksums, VirusTotal scans, macOS code signing, staged betas), but this rating is from docs alone (no hands-on use), and the public storefront (aperant.com) has been reduced to a bare early-access waitlist with every docs/pricing/download page returning 404 while the product sits mid-rebuild.
editorial.depthRationale: Beyond parallel worktree terminals, the app documents a three-role Planner/Coder/QA pipeline, a Graphiti knowledge-graph memory layer, GitHub/GitLab/Linear issue import, AI-resolved merges, an audit trail, and product-adjacent features (AI-assisted roadmap with competitor analysis, an 'Ideation' vulnerability/improvement scanner, auto-generated changelogs) that go well past a terminal wrapper; it lacks documented automations/scheduling, cross-agent messaging or checkpoints, which keeps it below the deepest tools in this set. Rated from docs, not hands-on use.
editorial.feelRationale: Electron app (CONTRIBUTING.md: Node.js 24+, node-pty native dependency for the terminal panes); no first-party performance claims or user reports of jank or speed were found in README, changelog, blog or a targeted web search, so this is a default Electron rating rather than an informed one.

tools.name: Atlas
tools.tagline: Install any coding agent. Run them everywhere.
tools.valueProp: Links every commit back to the agent session that produced it, prompts, tool calls, and reasoning stay queryable months later, and gives Claude Code, Codex, and its own agent a shared on-device memory so switching mid-task doesn't lose the thread; despite the tagline, agents only run on your local machine, never remote or vendor-managed.

pricing.notes: No pricing page exists (tryatlas.cc/pricing and /download both 404 as of 2026-09-25); the app is distributed free via GitHub releases and the homepage while in alpha (latest tag alpha-0.3.3). A separate web app (app.tryatlas.cc, 'Now in preview' as of September 2026) exposes an org-scoped 'AI broker' with per-organisation spend caps and a per-request usage ledger, implying some model usage may be billed through Atlas rather than purely bring-your-own, no public plan or price was found for this.

featureNotes.platforms.linux: README: 'macOS 13+ and Windows 10+ (x64) are the supported platforms. Linux builds from the same Tauri codebase but is untested', build-from-source only, no prebuilt binary.
featureNotes.platforms.web: Homepage references 'the web app' for calls/canvases; app.tryatlas.cc is a separate 'planning surface' (issues, knowledge, chat, calls) labeled 'Now in preview' as of September 2026, not a full equivalent of the desktop app.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Local organisations run fully offline with zero server dependency, but team/cloud-sync features (org sync, chat, AI broker) only run on Atlas's own Cloudflare-hosted backend (US-only), no self-hosted relay is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: app.tryatlas.cc (web, labeled preview as of September 2026) adds an Issues/Roadmaps board agents read for context, but it's a planning backlog, not a queue that auto-dispatches tasks into agent sessions.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Shared memory propagates decisions between agents automatically, and `@thread:name` mentions let a user pull a prior session's reasoning into a new prompt, but there is no live agent-to-agent messaging channel.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Conversations/canvases ('Spaces') and issues sync in realtime across teammates and agents via app.tryatlas.cc (web, 'Now in preview' as of September 2026), but this is shared planning/chat context rather than two people steering the same live agent session.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Same split as execution.selfHostServer: local/solo use needs no server at all, but team sync and the AI broker are only available through Atlas's own hosted cloud.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: External agents (Claude Code, Codex) authenticate with your own subscription or key; Atlas Agent can instead run through Atlas's org-scoped 'AI broker', which brokers model access and bills through Atlas rather than a key you supply.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: No plugin system for Atlas itself. Themes are a single declarative .toml of colour tokens (docs.tryatlas.cc/docs/themes), which restyles the app but adds nothing to it; Packs (skills, subagents, commands, hooks from skills.sh) and the ACP registry extend the agents Atlas runs, not Atlas. Documented at docs.tryatlas.cc/docs/agents and /docs/themes.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Atlas exposes its shared memory as MCP tools to any connected agent that advertises HTTP MCP support; no general public API is documented beyond that and the AI broker's OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

github.description: Source control for agents. Use multiple coding agents, track their changes and query them in one place

editorial.reachRationale: Created in May 2026, with a 402-member Discord, no product X account, and zero HN stories; 6,440 stars were discounted as attention rather than use, leaving genuine but early usage signals (40 contributors, steady commits) as the basis for 'emerging'.
editorial.polishRationale: Ships a working editor, terminal, git client, timeline, shared memory, knowledge base and a native browser tab, actively trending on GitHub, but tagged alpha (alpha-0.3.3) as of September 2026, and the README flags 'QA on the long tail of registry agents is ongoing.'
editorial.depthRationale: It goes beyond parallel sessions: checkpoints link commits to full session reasoning, memory is shared across agents, and the web app adds issues/knowledge/calls on top.
editorial.feelRationale: Tauri app (Rust backend, native WebView, not Electron) with an explicit 'true concurrency, Rust-owned session state' claim for running multiple agent threads at once; homepage tagline 'Compact, AMOLED, fast' and the founder's own LinkedIn description of Atlas Agent as 'pretty fast.' A targeted search for user sentiment ('Atlas tryatlas coding agent slow OR fast OR laggy') surfaced no independent reports of lag or slowness.

tools.name: bb
tools.tagline: The IDE that builds itself
tools.valueProp: The self-modifying one: most features are plugins, and you ask an agent in a thread to write the next one. One server dispatches threads across machines you own; Windows is WSL-only and the phone apps are TestFlight and an APK, not store releases.

pricing.notes: Free and MIT-licensed; no pricing page or paid tier exists. Agents run on the provider subscriptions you already pay for ('billed by them, not bb'). The optional bb connect relay is free with a GitHub login and has a per-account machine-slot limit. Product Hunt lists it as Free.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Electron desktop app for Apple Silicon only (arm64 dmg/zip; Homebrew cask `bb`). Intel Macs run `npx bb-app` and use the browser.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: No native app. Windows support means the Linux stack inside WSL2 via `npx bb-app`; native PowerShell, CMD and drive-letter paths are explicitly unsupported.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: x64 AppImage shipped since 0.38 (2026-08-15) but labelled alpha ('expect problems'); `npx bb-app` on Linux is a fully supported path.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: TestFlight build linked from Settings → Mobile: a native shell around the server’s web app that adds pairing, saved servers and push. No App Store release, and it runs no agents itself.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Android APK linked from Settings → Mobile, the same shell as the iOS app (docs/platform-support.md). No Play Store release.
featureNotes.platforms.web: `npx bb-app` serves the web app on localhost:38886; reachable remotely via bb connect, Tailscale Serve, or `--server-bind-host 0.0.0.0`.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: `bb` CLI ships in the npm package and is described as a first-class surface with the same capabilities as the app; agents use it too.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: The CLI is command-oriented (`bb thread spawn/tell/wait/output`); no full-screen terminal UI is documented.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Settings → Machines generates a one-line installer that enrolls a host daemon on any macOS/Linux/WSL2 box; one server dispatches threads across enrolled machines. Reach the server via the vendor-run bb connect relay or your own Tailscale Serve route.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: bb operates no compute. The experimental Modal sandbox plugin (0.43, 2026-09-11) provisions pausable cloud machines on your own Modal account; community plugins do the same for Vercel Sandboxes.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: The bb server is the product and runs on your machine. The optional bb connect relay (yourhandle.getbb.app) is vendor-operated, terminates TLS, and is not self-hostable; Tailscale Serve is the documented alternative.
featureNotes.agents.opencode: Shipped ACP provider (`acp-opencode`), listed when `opencode` is on PATH; no native harness. Cannot `/compact`.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Shipped ACP provider (`acp-cursor`, always listed); README calls it 'Cursor via ACP'. Cannot `/compact`.
featureNotes.agents.amp: Not a shipped provider. docs/configuration.md uses `amp acp` as the example for the ACP `customAgents` setting, and a community marketplace plugin ('Amp', bundled ACP bridge on @ampcode/sdk) exists.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: ACP providers plugin `customAgents` accepts any command that speaks ACP; marketplace plugins can also register providers via the provider-bridge API. A plain non-ACP CLI is not supported.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: No coding agent of its own. A server-side 'helper' model (default `codex/gpt-5.6-luna` via your Codex credentials) does thread titles, transcription and similar chores.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Built-in Worktree plugin creates `git worktree` per thread under the bb data dir, copies `.worktreeinclude` files, runs `.bb-env-setup.sh`/`.bb-env-teardown.sh`, kills processes in it, and removes it after a five-minute grace when the last thread is archived.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: No local Docker-per-task mode. Experimental Modal sandbox plugin gives each machine a cloud sandbox with a Dockerfile-defined image; community CoW-copy (Btrfs/reflink) and Vercel Sandbox plugins exist.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Each managed worktree gets its own branch; prefix configurable with `managedBranchPrefix`.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Working-tree diff view in the thread panel (homepage mockup shows 'Uncommitted · 6 files, +124 -18'; changelog references the diff toolbar and diff code themes).
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: The GitHub plugin (gh CLI auth) lists issues/PRs, spawns agent threads on them and shows the thread's PR in `bb thread show`, but no in-app 'open PR' action is documented; the agent creates the PR.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Nothing documented beyond `bb environment branches`; no merge or conflict tooling found in docs or changelog.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Editing a sent message rewinds the conversation and re-runs the turn (Codex, Claude Code, Pi) but 'your workspace keeps its changes'; no file snapshot or restore.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Built-in Tasks plugin with List or Board view per project and `bb tasks` CLI; it can dispatch work to threads (`bb tasks detach`, dispatch outside a git repo).
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Threads can be 'manager' threads that coordinate child threads; `bb thread spawn --parent-self`; homepage: 'have one agent spawn and manage another, each in its own thread'.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Built-in Automations plugin (`bb automation create --script-file`, scripts may call the bb CLI), Workflows plugin (off by default), Send later (scheduled sends) and Concurrency limit plugins.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Built-in Push notifications plugin with independent mobile, web and desktop delivery, plus a notification center. Mobile push goes through Expo's exp.host, which a self-hosted server must reach.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: `bb thread tell <thread-id> "..."` steers another thread immediately; queue lists show a Sender for agent threads; the CLI reference covers an agent editing another thread.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Voice input with a microphone picker; transcription runs through your Codex credentials (`codex/gpt-transcribe`) or an OpenAI API key, not locally. Community 'Handsfree' plugin adds a voice operator.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: One server, no user accounts; the HTTP API is unauthenticated and bb connect binds a server to a single GitHub-login owner ('require the paired account owner's session').
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Any browser or paired device that can reach the server sees and steers the same threads, but there is no per-person identity, presence or roles.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: No plans, billing or org features exist.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Everything runs on your machines; bb connect is optional (Tailscale route documented). Only third-party server in a default path is Expo's push API for mobile notifications.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: 'bb uses the provider CLI you already have authenticated'; Account Pooler rotates several of your own Claude/Codex accounts as they hit limits.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Anonymous usage telemetry (app starts, thread/message counts, plugin installs) with a random per-install id; off via Settings → Privacy or `BB_TELEMETRY=false`; never sent from source runs.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: True, extends bb's own interface and core directly. `@get-bb/plugin-sdk` documents seven extensible app surfaces (app window, command palette, composer, home page, plugin settings, Plugins page, plugin backend); the repo's own first-party plugins built on it add agent providers (provider-claude-code, provider-codex, provider-acp, provider-pi), environments/machines (environment-git-worktree, environment-modal-sandbox, etc.), panels/views (monaco-editor, side-chat, thread-list, navigation, pdf-preview), and theming (theme-preview), matching the true bar's own canonical example. Documented at plugins/plugin-api-docs/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md and the plugins/ directory tree (github.com/get-bb/bb).
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: HTTP + WebSocket API, Node SDK (`BBSdk` in bb-app) and CLI. No MCP server of its own is documented.

github.description: The agent IDE that builds itself

top.title: Bb: The IDE that builds itself

tools.authorNote: This is my current daily driver, primarily because of its incredibly robust and thoughtful plugin system. Not necessarily as extensive as DeepSeek Harness’s, but the attention to UX and usability makes it stand out. It’s a novel mental model for extensibility, and I can’t recommend it enough.

editorial.reachRationale: 297,787 release-asset downloads over the last five releases and 962 commits/30d in 30 days point to a real and active install base and dev velocity, comparable in magnitude to peers scored established (cmux, emdash, superset); the product-specific Discord (657) and X (1,049) are modest and the HN reception thin (23 points), so this lands at established rather than major.
editorial.polishRationale: My call from daily use: a slick app, and the plugin system is unusually well thought through; the product's own features are built on it. It ships a dated changelog every week and roughly 1,000 commits a month. Short of finished: the README says workflows and surfaces are evolving, the Linux app is alpha, Windows is WSL-only, the iOS and Android apps are TestFlight and a sideloaded APK rather than store releases, several plugins are marked experimental, and the 0.43 notes list many reliability fixes.
editorial.depthRationale: Managed worktrees with setup/teardown hooks, multi-machine dispatch from one server, manager/child threads, thread-to-thread steering, a Tasks board, automations, workflows, scheduled sends, concurrency limits, push notifications, account pooling, a GitHub plugin, a browser-automation plugin, an SDK and a plugin system that the product's own features are built on; that is as deep as anything in this dataset.
editorial.feelRationale: My call from daily use: it feels quick. Under the hood it is an Electron shell around a React web app served from a local Node daemon, a typical web stack, so this rests on use rather than architecture.

tools.name: Berd
tools.tagline: a desktop app for getting work done with any model
tools.valueProp: Block's open-source (Apache-2.0) desktop app switches between Goose, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Pi through ACP, giving each session a named agent identity with visible subagent delegation. It adds voice conversation (Siri/OpenAI speech) and per-project git worktrees, plus enterprise distribution seams so companies can layer private providers onto the same public build.

pricing.notes: Free, open-source app; users configure and pay their own model provider (Claude, OpenAI, etc.). No Berd-specific paid tier found. Enterprise distributions can add managed provider settings and private resources, but that is a build-time overlay, not a published pricing plan.

featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Project workspaces have a 'worktree' startup mode (vs. 'branch') backed by native git_create_worktree/git_remove_worktree Tauri commands (src/shared/api/git.ts, src/features/projects/lib/projectChatWorkspaces.ts); Berd creates, names and tears down the worktree, not just tolerates one you made yourself.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False, agent-side only, nothing for Berd's own interface. 'Extensions' in Settings -> Connections are directly-configured MCP-style tool integrations (stdio, SSE, streamable HTTP, ACP, or builtin) that extend what the agent can call, and 'Agent Skills' under skills/ are portable SKILL.md packages installed via `npx skills add block/berd --skill <name>` into any compatible harness, both are agent-side additions that don't count (MCP registration, SKILL.md bundles). Berd's own internal design doc confirms there is no plugin framework for the product itself: 'It should not become a plugin framework before the product needs one' (docs/composable-capabilities.md). No documented way to add a panel, view, command or provider to Berd's own UI. Documented at distro/skills/berd-help/references/connections-and-extensions.md and docs/composable-capabilities.md (github.com/block/berd).
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: CHANGELOG v0.6.2 lists 'Experimental, Remote SSH sessions': opt-in sessions on an SSH host you already control, with the Berd UI staying local; marked experimental, not the default path.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: A 'PR Inbox' (docs/work-status-platform-surfaces.md) tracks and opens existing pull requests from Berd projects; PR creation itself is done by the agent (e.g. Claude Code/Codex) shelling out inside the session, not a dedicated in-app 'create PR' action confirmed from source.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: CHANGELOG v0.6.1 'Clearer subagent activity': chat activity identifies known subagents, their assigned tasks, delegation, waiting and cancellation states inline in the transcript.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Native desktop completion notifications (src/shared/hooks/useCompletionNotifications.ts, src-tauri/src/commands/notifications.rs) plus a planned/partial macOS menu-bar and Windows tray 'Work Status' popover surfacing chats and PRs.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Voice Conversation mode (Apple Speech Recognition/Siri voices, OpenAI STT/TTS, Pocket TTS) lets you talk to an active session, including backgrounded calls while switching chats; extensively iterated across the last several releases.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: TELEMETRY.md: disabled by default in official builds; togglable in Settings at any time; excludes prompts, messages, files, source code and credentials when enabled.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: A changed-files list is exposed via a git-status API (src/shared/hooks/useChangedFiles.ts) inside the workspace widget, but no line-level in-app diff viewer was confirmed from README, changelog or source structure.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Onboarding's CURATED_HARNESS_IDS is a fixed list (goose, claude-acp, codex-acp, cursor-agent, pi-acp) with no generic custom-command harness found in source; not confirmed absent.
