top.title: Show HN: Sandboxed HTML in Markdown (With Doom, Sort Of)

editorial.reachRationale: Repo created August 2026 (2026-08-11) with real launch coverage (VentureBeat, TheRundown, a YouTube review, a Block employee LinkedIn post) and healthy OSS activity for its age (943 stars, 24 contributors, 215 commits/90d, weekly releases). Discounted Block's own scale since Berd is a side project of a bigco, not its flagship; found no dedicated Discord, X account or HN discussion, and no download/install numbers, so it reads as early attention rather than an established user base.
editorial.polishRationale: Signed macOS builds, a weekly-cadence CHANGELOG and real press coverage (VentureBeat) show engineering discipline for a project whose repo dates to August 2026, but several highlighted surfaces are rough: remote SSH is explicitly 'Experimental', PR creation and line-level diff review ride on the agent's own tool use rather than a dedicated in-app flow, and open issues (105) run high relative to its size.
editorial.depthRationale: Worktree-per-agent isolation, visible subagent delegation in the transcript, two real extension paths (MCP Connections/Extensions plus installable Agent Skills), voice conversation, and a PR Inbox go well past a session switcher, but there's no task board, no scheduled or event-driven automations, no cloud sandboxes/computer use, and no team collaboration, so it stops short of a full orchestrator.
editorial.feelRationale: Tauri 2 (Rust backend, native OS webview) plus a React 19 frontend, lighter-weight than an Electron app; no user reports of lag or jank turned up in review/press coverage or the changelog. Held back by: no GPU-native rendering claim and no direct performance benchmarking found.

tools.name: Buzz
tools.tagline: A hive mind communication platform.
tools.valueProp: Humans and agents on the same substrate: every message, review, workflow step and git event is a Nostr event signed by its author’s keypair, so an agent’s identity and audit trail outlive any API key. Git lives inside the workspace, and branches become channels with review and a signed merge.

pricing.notes: Fully free and Apache-2.0 to self-host. Block also runs a hosted version at buzz.xyz (create a community with Block-provided hosting) and is collecting a waitlist for a separate paid 'enterprise version built for company-wide access, support, and agent management' that had not launched as of September 2026.

featureNotes.platforms.ios: A native iOS app ('Buzz - chat with your hive', App Store id6779728271, first released 2026-07-17) exists and is listed as a real product, but VISION.md's status table marks the Flutter mobile client 'in active development' (short of the same feature parity as desktop), matching README's 'Being wired up' column.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Same Flutter mobile client as iOS, same in-progress status per VISION.md.
featureNotes.platforms.web: The relay serves a browser web client, but VISION.md is explicit that it's 'the repo browser at myproject.com' - i.e. git-hosting/repo browsing only. The channels/chat workspace itself requires the desktop (or in-progress mobile) app.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Block hosts communities at buzz.xyz, but that hosts the relay/workspace, not agent compute - agents always run on a laptop, a VM, an edge box, or similar infrastructure the operator points at the relay (VISION_AGENT.md, engineering.block.xyz/blog/buzz). A separate paid 'enterprise' agent-management tier was waitlist-only as of September 2026.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: No git-worktree feature; isolation is at the channel/branch level (see branchPerTask), not the filesystem level.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: README 'Branch as room' story: opening a feature branch creates a channel where patches, CI, review and the merge decision live together. This is channel-per-branch, not automatic branch creation by Buzz.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: buzz-dev-mcp gives agents a shell that 'runs at the operator's trust level, like bash itself' (VISION_AGENT.md) - explicitly not sandboxed/containerized by Buzz itself.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Buzz hosts git itself (smart HTTP, NIP-34 patch events) and the engineering blog shows 'the Buzz Git forge showing a pull request, review status, branches, activity, and comments' - a working PR-equivalent, not just raw patch mailing.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: The same forge screenshot and copy describe a 'signed merge decision' recorded alongside discussion, patches, CI and review in one channel; merge itself is a relay-verified pointer compare-and-swap over content-addressed packfiles (engineering.block.xyz/blog/buzz).
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: buzz-agent summarizes its own history when context fills and continues (VISION_AGENT.md) - this is compaction, not a resumable checkpoint/rewind feature; no explicit checkpoint capability found.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: No kanban/task-board surface; the seven surfaces are Home, Stream, Forum, DMs, Agents (a directory/job-board), Workflows and Search (VISION.md).
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Home Feed aggregates @mentions, action items and agent updates with an explicit zero-notification-by-default model per surface (VISION.md 'Home Feed & Notifications'); push notifications specifically are roadmap ('📋 Developer portal, push notifications, culture features').
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: No telemetry policy or opt-out statement found in README, VISION docs, or SECURITY.md.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial, config-level extension of Buzz's own behavior, not code. The `buzz-workflow` crate is a YAML-as-code automation engine, orchestrated directly by `buzz-relay` (Buzz's own core), triggered via `wf.on_event` on Nostr events (message/reaction/schedule/webhook triggers per README) and producing KIND_WORKFLOW_* events, this is Buzz running user-authored automation config against its own event bus, matching the partial bar's 'custom command/action YAML that the app runs' example. Separately, agent tool access is MCP-based (buzz-dev-mcp, 'works with any agent or client that speaks MCP') and is agent-side, so it does not itself count. No plugin API, hooks, or way to add panels/commands to Buzz's own UI was found. Documented in ARCHITECTURE.md and README.md (github.com/block/buzz).
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: No team billing/seats feature is described anywhere; the product is Apache-2.0 self-hosted with an unlaunched enterprise waitlist, so this is unknown rather than confirmed absent.

github.description: A hive mind communication platform

top.title: Jack Dorsey launches Buzz to combine team chat, AI agents and Git hosting

activity.changelogCadence: near-daily desktop point releases (59 in the last 90 days); no separate changelog doc found, tracked via GitHub releases

editorial.reachRationale: 34,547 stars and 106 contributors sit in the same numeric band as established OSS multiplexers like cmux (~27k) and herdr (~39k), both rated established. Beyond stars, the signals are genuinely product-specific rather than borrowed from Block's brand: 106,153 release-asset downloads across the last 5 releases, a 378-point/339-comment HN front-page launch, dedicated press coverage (Block's own engineering and company blogs, third-party YouTube/LinkedIn coverage), and a live App Store listing. Two things hold it at established rather than major: the repo was created March 2026 and the product openly badges itself 'DEVELOPER PREVIEW' on its own homepage, with a known broken feature (workflow approval gates) and mobile clients in progress. Real, fast-growing, company-backed traction, but it has not reached the multi-year, broad-enterprise-adoption bar of the tier above.
editorial.polishRationale: The core desktop chat/channel/search experience is described as working across seven surfaces, but the project explicitly badges itself a 'Developer Preview,' the Windows build is unsigned alpha, workflow approval gates are known-broken (runs fail instead of pausing, tracked as WF-08), and mobile clients are active work-in-progress - real but visibly early.
editorial.depthRationale: This goes far beyond a tmux wrapper: it is a full team workspace (channels, threads, forum, DMs, voice huddles) with its own git hosting and PR/review/merge flow, YAML workflow automation, a formally-specified (TLA+/Tamarin) multi-tenant and git-storage protocol, per-agent cryptographic identity and delegation, and a compute-sharing mesh for local inference. Few tools in this dataset combine chat, git hosting, and agent orchestration as one substrate.
editorial.feelRationale: No user reports of speed or lag turned up in a targeted 'Buzz Block hive mind slow OR fast OR laggy' search - only launch coverage and store listings. The maker's own engineering post cites concrete responsiveness targets (Redis pub/sub fan-out <50ms p99) and describes agents mentioning each other 'almost instantly without breaking anyone's flow,' backed by a Rust relay/backend with Postgres full-text search and a Tauri+React desktop client - a stack built for low-latency real-time chat rather than a heavier Electron shell. Held back because these are architectural targets and maker claims rather than confirmed field reports, and the product's own 'early, rough edges' framing tempers full confidence.

tools.name: Capy
tools.tagline: The best AI software engineer
tools.valueProp: Capy puts cloud and local threads in one web and desktop queue, with explicit interrupt, queue, and steer delivery plus attention states. Its own agents can split work into isolated VM tasks, while paid plans allow unlimited concurrent threads and connected model subscriptions.

maker.name: Scrapybara, Inc.
maker.funding: Y Combinator-backed, per Capy about page.

pricing.notes: Lite $20/month ($1 first seven days), Pro $100/month, Max $200–$1,000/month, Enterprise custom. Unlimited members and concurrent threads on paid plans. Personal local threads with a connected subscription need no Capy credits; cloud VM and hosted models consume credits. Pro/Max support connected Codex, Copilot and SuperGrok subscriptions; enterprise supports BYOK.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Download page lists an Apple Silicon and Intel desktop app; version 0.3.0 shown.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Download page lists a Windows x64 desktop installer.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Download page and Linux docs list x64/arm64 AppImage, deb and tar.gz builds.
featureNotes.platforms.web: Homepage offers Open in web, and quickstart starts a thread at capy.ai.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: No Capy agent CLI is documented in the docs index; API quickstart uses curl for programmatic control.
featureNotes.execution.local: Download FAQ: desktop pairs a computer and local threads work in a folder there; paired computers can be reached from other devices while online.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Machines docs: cloud threads execute in isolated Capy VMs; each thread has a machine identity.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Enterprise page offers customer-specific infrastructure by agreement, but docs describe the agent loop on Capy servers and no self-hosted server distribution.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Codex subscription and local Codex session import are supported, but Capy runs its own agent loop rather than Codex CLI as a managed agent.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Desktop setup can import Claude Code sessions; docs do not describe launching Claude Code as the managed agent.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Copilot subscription supplies models, not a managed Copilot CLI agent.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Pricing names Captain, Build and Review agents; tasks docs describe Capy child agents.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: No managed git worktree workflow appears in Quickstart, Tasks, Machines or Download: local threads use folders, and fresh child tasks get isolated VMs with clean checkouts.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Machines docs describe isolated cloud VMs per thread and fresh VMs for writing child tasks.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Pull requests docs: Capy creates a fresh capy/ branch named from the PR title when publishing from the target base branch.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Quickstart locates growing diffs and PR review in a thread side pane and dedicated PR page.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Quickstart and pull requests docs: agent commits, pushes and opens a PR.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Pull requests docs document stacked branches and CI/review follow-up, but no merge or conflict assistance; Terms say Capy does not merge PRs by default.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Machines docs describe setup snapshots used for VM boot, not a user checkpoint or rollback of in-progress agent work.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Threads docs describe sidebar and threads page status buckets; pricing lists unlimited concurrent threads; homepage shows web multi-agent split/filter/sort.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Threads page lists and filters work by status, folders and tags; docs do not describe a kanban board or queued task feeder.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Tasks docs: an agent drafts, starts and coordinates child tasks on shared or fresh machines, up to three levels deep.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Automations docs: scheduled, GitHub, Slack, Linear, incoming webhook and on-demand triggers create runs.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Threads docs show a Needs attention bucket and child task blockers notify the parent agent; a user-facing push or desktop alert for blocked threads is not documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Tasks docs: sibling root threads can message each other and a coordinator can read their state.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Threads docs document live microphone dictation in the composer.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Projects docs: enabled organization members can read non-personal project threads; folders can be shared.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Project members can read non-personal threads and the API exposes join and takeover, but concurrent human steering of one thread is not explicitly documented.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Pricing lists unlimited members and shared organization credits.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Open Source Program grants free access to open-source projects; Terms reserve rights in Capy Services, and no product source or OSI license is published.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Machines docs say the agent loop runs on Capy servers; customer-specific enterprise infrastructure does not document self-hosting end to end.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Pricing and download FAQ document Codex, Copilot and SuperGrok subscription connections; Claude subscription sign-in is excluded.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial, the documented API can create and drive threads, manage automations, and file threads in folders from outside Capy, but no documented loader adds code to Capy panels, commands or lifecycle. https://docs.capy.ai/api-reference/overview documents those controls; https://docs.capy.ai/integrations/mcp and https://docs.capy.ai/skills extend the agent only.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: API reference documents create/list threads, messages, task observation, automations and reviews; MCP docs cover external tools consumed by Capy agents.

top.title: Launch HN: Trigger.dev (YC W23) – Open-source platform to build reliable AI apps

tools.authorNote: Very cool for the cloud-managed, I'm-willing-to-pay-to-have-problems-solved kind of solution. Things just work, and they've done a lot of work to make them work. If you don't want to spend all day tinkering with your own setup, fixing bugs, customizing things, dealing with skills and so on, Capy is really good. Devin and Tembo are similar in that way.

editorial.reachRationale: The product homepage claims more than 70,000 engineers, and Capy sells team plans with unlimited seats and concurrent threads. That self-reported reach suggests an established product, but no independent product usage count or download metrics were available, so it does not support a major tier.
editorial.polishRationale: The shipped web and desktop apps, documented status buckets and delivery shortcuts, in-app diff and PR review, and detailed API suggest a finished workflow; this is a documentation assessment, not a hands-on UX test.
editorial.depthRationale: Isolated VMs, nested parallel tasks, cross-thread coordination, PR and CI follow-up, review agent, automation triggers, integrations, and an external control API extend well beyond a session list. This is a documentation assessment, not a hands-on UX test.
editorial.feelRationale: Capy's Linux build ships as an AppImage, .deb and portable tarball alongside a full web app, the standard packaging for a cross-platform web-rendered client; no implementation language was named and no performance claims or complaints were found.

tools.name: Cate
tools.tagline: Tackling terminal overload with one infinite canvas.
tools.valueProp: The spatial one: each worktree becomes a coloured territory of terminals, editors and browser panels on an infinite canvas. No web or mobile client, no automations, and telemetry you cannot switch off.

maker.name: 0-AI UG (haftungsbeschränkt)
maker.funding: not disclosed; two-founder German UG (Paul Horn, Anton Horn) in Stuttgart, commercial-register entry listed as 'in registration' on the Impressum

pricing.notes: Free MIT-licensed download with no paid tier, accounts or seat limits. Agents run with credentials stored on your machine and requests go straight to the provider you configure; Cate does not proxy or resell tokens.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Electron app; DMG and ZIP for arm64 and x64 on GitHub releases, plus a homebrew-core cask `cate`.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: NSIS installer and ZIP, x64 only. WSL hosts are supported as remote workspaces.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: AppImage, DEB and tar.gz, x64 only; the 1.7.0 notes say terminal dependencies were rebuilt for older glibc.
featureNotes.platforms.web: No hosted or self-served web UI; the product is the Electron desktop app.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: `cate` is a CLI that agents (or you) run inside a Cate terminal to open panels, read/type into other terminals, drive browser panels and create, message, wait for and review agent workers. It is not a standalone launcher you run outside the app.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Point a workspace at a host over SSH (system OpenSSH client since 1.6.0) or WSL; terminals, git, search and agents run there while editors, browser and canvas stay local. Cate ships a bundled Node runtime daemon per platform for the remote side.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: No vendor compute; privacy page calls it a local-first tool.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: There is no server or relay product; remote access is a direct SSH connection to a machine you already run.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Native hook bridge for status (working / waiting / finished) and session resume; also available as a T3 chat panel provider.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Native hook bridge for status and `codex resume`; also a T3 chat panel provider.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Not in the agent registry at v2.0.2; the 1.0.4 changelog notes the docs deprecated Gemini CLI in favour of Antigravity.
featureNotes.agents.opencode: Hook-based status via `session.status` / `permission.asked`, follow-ups, `--session` resume; also a T3 chat panel provider.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: `cursor-agent` is in the registry, but Cursor exposes no permission event so Cate does not show a waiting state for it (blog, July 2026).
featureNotes.agents.pi: A July 2026 blog post lists Pi among the six hooked CLIs, but the agent registry at v2.0.2 (src/shared/agents.ts) has only claude-code, codex, cursor, grok, kiro and opencode, and the Pi-based in-app agent no longer appears in package.json.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: README: run 'any agent CLI' in a Cate terminal, but lifecycle status, needs-you notifications, session resume and orchestration only work for the six registered CLIs whose hook APIs Cate bridges; anything else is a plain terminal.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Bundles T3 Code (npm `t3`) as embedded chat panels with streaming, tool calls and approvals, but T3 drives the same vendor agents (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode) with your credentials; Cate ships no agent loop or model routing of its own. The earlier Pi-based 'Cate Agent' with mission orchestration (1.6.0) is not in the 2.0.2 dependencies.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Type what you are working on and Cate creates the worktree under `.cate`, gives it a colour, a territory on the canvas and its own terminals; branch off a local branch, remote branch or open PR. Agent workers can be spawned into isolated worktrees via the CLI.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Worktree creation names and creates the branch from the description you type.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Multi-file Diff Review panel (working tree, staged, commit, branch comparisons; unified or split) plus side-by-side diffs and review notes; agents can record findings with `cate review note add`.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Commit, push and open a pull request from a review across local, SSH and WSL workspaces (1.7.0); a Pull Requests overview lives in the repository overlay (2.0.0).
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: 0.4.6 added a 'merge back' action for worktrees in the Parallel Work tab and 2.0.0 added branch clean-up; no conflict-resolution help is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Agent worker output can be reviewed and then applied, kept or discarded as a unit; no snapshot or rollback of files or agent state is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Work is arranged spatially on the canvas; there is no kanban board or queue feeding agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Recursive orchestration through the Cate CLI (1.6.1-beta.1): terminal agents can create, inspect, message, wait for, review, apply, keep, discard and stop nested workers in isolated worktrees, gated by separate read and control permissions in Settings.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: No scheduled or event-triggered runs are documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: OS notifications on state transitions (working to waiting on permission, finished) driven by each CLI's hook API; clicking one brings the exact terminal forward.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: `cate agent send --panel <id>` delivers a prompt to another agent panel and `cate terminal read` reads another terminal; sessions are isolated per terminal.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Only a macOS microphone entitlement so Claude Code's own voice input works inside a Cate terminal; Cate has no dictation or voice mode.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Single-user desktop app with no accounts or sign-in.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Nothing documented; all state is local JSON files under the project's `.cate/` directory.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: MIT licence on the whole Electron app (LICENSE file, package.json).
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: No vendor server in the working path; the only outbound traffic is always-on crash reporting and usage analytics (Sentry plus 0-AI's analytics) and update checks against GitHub releases.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Privacy page: agent requests go directly from your machine to the provider you configure, using credentials stored locally; Cate does not proxy or log them.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Privacy page and 1.3.1 changelog: crash reporting and anonymous usage analytics in packaged builds are 'always on, are not optional, and cannot be turned off'; the Settings toggle was removed in 1.3.1. Source (src/main/lifecycle/telemetry.ts) confirms the notice is informational only.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: No plugin system: Cate shipped a real third-party extension system (isolated extension panels with permissions and a catalog) and removed it entirely in 1.7.0 (“removed the extension catalog, settings, panels, installation, and server runtime”). What remains is custom editor themes and a hand-edited settings.json, which restyle rather than extend. The agent-skills catalog is agent-side. Documented in CHANGELOG.md (github.com/0-AI-UG/cate).
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: The `cate` CLI is a programmatic surface over panels, terminals, browser automation, reviews and agent workers, but it only works from a terminal Cate spawned (per-terminal session token) and needs CLI permissions enabled in Settings; there is no MCP server or external HTTP API.

top.title: Cate v1.0 is out: The Infinite canvas workspace for developers

editorial.reachRationale: A genuine Show HN launch (65 points, 66 comments) shows some real attention, but brew installs are tiny (23/30d), there's no Discord, and the only X account is a co-founder's personal handle with 113 followers, so usage signals stay at early-adopter scale.
editorial.polishRationale: Signed builds for three platforms, a homebrew-core cask and a dated Keep-a-Changelog entry most weeks, but 2.0 shipped through three betas and two patch releases in one week, 1.7 removed the extension system and 2.0 removed saved layouts, and the only documentation is the README and changelog. Rated from those documents and the source tree, not hands-on use.
editorial.depthRationale: Beyond terminals on a canvas it manages worktrees with branch creation, has a multi-file diff review with PR creation, hook-driven needs-you notifications, agents that spawn and review nested workers through a CLI, and agent-drivable browser panels; it lacks a task board, automations, any team layer and a plugin API. Rated from the documents and source tree, not hands-on use.
editorial.feelRationale: Electron app (electron-vite dev/build scripts in package.json) rendering its infinite canvas in a web view, with no Rust or native GUI layer in the repo's language breakdown. No maker performance claims and no user reports of lag or unusual smoothness turned up across the README, changelog, HN launch thread, or Reddit coverage.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.tagline: Work with Claude directly in your codebase.
tools.valueProp: The harness as its own multiplexer: one account runs the same sessions in the terminal, desktop, web, phone and Slack, teleports them between surfaces, and runs them in Anthropic’s cloud VMs. Only Claude, nothing open, and everything beyond the CLI needs a paid plan.

maker.name: Anthropic
maker.funding: Anthropic, PBC: the model vendor itself; venture-backed AI lab

pricing.notes: Claude Code is a feature of paid Claude plans; the Free plan lists it as 'No'. Pro $17/mo billed annually ($20 monthly); Max 5x $100/mo and Max 20x $200/mo; Team standard seat $20/seat/mo annual ($25 monthly) or premium seat $100/seat/mo annual ($125 monthly, 5x usage); Enterprise $20/seat/mo annual plus usage at API rates. The CLI, VS Code and JetBrains extensions can instead bill per token through an Anthropic Console API key, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry, but the multiplexing surfaces (Desktop, cloud sessions, mobile, Remote Control, routines, voice) require a claude.ai subscription. Cloud sessions count against plan usage with no separate compute charge; on Enterprise they need a premium or Chat + Claude Code seat. Dispatch and computer use are Pro/Max only; Code Review, analytics, SSO and server-managed settings are Team/Enterprise only.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Claude Desktop universal build (Intel and Apple silicon) with a Code tab; the CLI installs via curl, `brew install --cask claude-code` or `claude-code@latest`.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Claude Desktop x64 and ARM64 installers; Code sessions can run natively or inside a WSL 2 distribution. CLI via PowerShell installer or `winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode`. The Bash sandbox is not supported on native Windows.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Desktop app is in beta and only for Ubuntu 22.04+ / Debian 12+ (x86_64, arm64) via Anthropic's apt repo; computer use is not available there and other distros are told to use the CLI. The CLI itself supports Linux generally (curl, apt, dnf, apk).
featureNotes.platforms.ios: No separate Claude Code app: the Code tab in the Claude app (App Store) is a client for cloud sessions, Remote Control sessions on your machine, and Dispatch. Code never runs on the phone.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Same Code tab in the Claude app on the Play Store; same client-only role as iOS.
featureNotes.platforms.web: claude.ai/code ('Claude Code on the web') starts and steers cloud sessions and Remote Control sessions, manages routines and cloud environments, and shares sessions.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: `claude` is the primary product; `claude agents`, `--worktree`, `--cloud`, `--teleport`, `remote-control`, `/schedule`, `/bg` cover the multiplexing flows.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: Agent view (`claude agents`, research preview) takes over the full terminal with sessions grouped under Needs input / Working / Completed, a dispatch input, peek-and-reply and attach/detach. Agent teams can also render each teammate in a tmux or iTerm2 split pane.
featureNotes.execution.local: Terminal, IDE extensions and Desktop 'Local' sessions run on your machine; Desktop's Bash sandbox uses macOS Seatbelt or Linux bubblewrap/seccomp.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Three paths: Desktop SSH sessions run Claude Code on a Linux or macOS host you manage (auto-installed on first connect, admin-distributable via `sshConfigs`); Remote Control publishes a local CLI session to claude.ai/code and the phone app through Anthropic's relay; Team/Enterprise self-hosted environments run cloud sessions on your own runners.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Cloud sessions (research preview) run in isolated Anthropic-managed VMs started from the browser, phone, Desktop, `claude --cloud`, routines, Claude Tag or Projects; they keep running with the laptop closed and can hold multiple repositories.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Self-hosted environments (public beta, Team and Enterprise, off by default) put runners on your Docker/Kubernetes/bare hosts, but the queue, session stream and inference stay on api.anthropic.com; only the checkout and build artifacts stay local. Bypass permissions is unavailable in self-hosted sessions.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: The product is Claude Code; every session, subagent, teammate, background session and cloud thread is a Claude Code process.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: The parallel-agents docs state 'In every approach the workers are Claude sessions. To involve a different tool, expose it to Claude as an MCP server.' No adapter for other coding agents.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Anthropic's own agent loop with Claude models (Sonnet, Opus, Haiku, Fable), permission modes including Auto with safety classifiers, and model routing per session.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Desktop has a per-session worktree toggle, configurable worktree location and branch prefix, and archive-to-remove; the CLI has `--worktree`, the `EnterWorktree` tool, `isolation: worktree` for subagents, `.worktreeinclude`, automatic cleanup on exit and a periodic sweep of subagent and background-session worktrees.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Each cloud session runs in an isolated Anthropic-managed VM with git credentials kept outside the sandbox; local sessions use an OS-level Bash sandbox (Seatbelt / bubblewrap) rather than a container, and a devcontainer reference exists.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: `--worktree <name>` creates branch `worktree-<name>` from the default branch; Desktop prepends an optional branch prefix; cloud sessions push their own branch which `--teleport` then fetches.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Desktop diff view with per-line comments submitted back to Claude and a 'Review code' button that leaves Claude's own comments; claude.ai/code reviews cloud-session changes; the VS Code extension shows inline diffs.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Create a PR from claude.ai/code when a cloud session finishes, from Desktop (a CI status bar then appears), or via `gh` from any session; `/batch` splits a change into 5-30 worktree-isolated subagents that each open a PR.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Desktop's CI status bar has Auto-fix (Claude iterates on failing checks) and Auto-merge (squash once checks pass, needs GitHub auto-merge enabled). Merge conflicts are not detected automatically because GitHub sends no webhook; the docs say to open the session and ask Claude to rebase.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Automatic checkpoint before every prompt; `/rewind` (or Esc Esc) restores code, conversation or both, with snapshots kept for the 100 most recent checkpoints and swept after about 30 days. Documented for the CLI; the Desktop page does not mention it.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Desktop sidebar of sessions filterable by status, project or environment, split view of two sessions, auto-archive when the PR merges; agent view lists every background session across projects; cloud sessions appear at claude.ai/code and on the phone.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: No kanban. Agent view groups sessions into Needs input / Working / Completed with a dispatch input, and a Project's Overview pane lists which threads finished, have PRs ready, or are waiting on you.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Built-in and custom subagents inside a session; dynamic workflows run 'tens to hundreds' of subagents from a script; agent teams (experimental, CLI only, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`) have a lead spawn and message teammates; Projects (public beta, Pro/Max) have Claude start and track cloud threads from one conversation; Desktop's Claude can suggest, rename and archive other sessions.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Routines (research preview) run in the cloud on a schedule, from a per-routine HTTP endpoint, or on GitHub events; Desktop local scheduled tasks run on your machine with an optional worktree per run; `/loop` polls inside a session; channels push MCP events (CI, chat, webhooks) into a running session.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Desktop sends an OS notification when a session finishes while you are elsewhere and when CI finishes; Remote Control sends phone push for 'when Claude decides' and 'when actions required'; Dispatch pushes when a spawned session finishes or needs approval; agent view fires the terminal notification channel when a session needs input.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Cross-session messaging (`ListAgents` / `SendMessage`, on by default from v2.1.224) between sessions on one machine, and through Anthropic's servers to cloud sessions and Remote Control sessions on other machines; Desktop's own surface lets Claude list, read, message and archive other Desktop sessions; teammates in agent teams message each other directly.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: `/voice` push-to-talk or tap-to-record dictation in the CLI, agent view and the VS Code extension, transcribed on Anthropic's servers; needs a claude.ai account and a local microphone, so not in cloud or SSH sessions.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Team (2-150 seats) and Enterprise organizations with an admin console for Claude Code (toggle Desktop, cloud, Remote Control, routines, bypass mode), server-managed settings, SSO, SCIM and audit logs.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Cloud sessions can be shared by link with Team-wide or public visibility; 'Recipients see the latest state when they open the link, but their view doesn't update in real time'. No documented co-steering of one session by two people.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Team plan with standard and premium seats and central billing; Enterprise adds per-user and org spend limits, role-based access, SCIM, compliance API and an analytics API.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: The npm package license reads 'SEE LICENSE IN README.md' and the README points to Anthropic's Commercial Terms. The anthropics/claude-code repository hosts the changelog, plugins and issue tracker, not the product source.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Even self-hosted runners poll Anthropic's queue and stream sessions to api.anthropic.com; Remote Control, cloud sessions, routines and mobile all go through claude.ai. There is no vendor-free deployment.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: You bring a Claude subscription or an Anthropic/Bedrock/Agent Platform/Foundry credential; Anthropic is the token seller either way. Third-party providers work for the CLI and IDE extensions only; Desktop, cloud, mobile, Remote Control and routines require a claude.ai plan.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` (metrics), `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` and `DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND` are documented; telemetry is off by default on Bedrock, Agent Platform and Foundry. Caveat: `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` or `DO_NOT_TRACK` also disables the feature-flag fetch that Remote Control needs.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False: Claude Code's own plugins extend the agent, not the app. A Claude Code plugin is 'a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or other components' (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins): Skills (SKILL.md, run as /my-plugin:review), Agents (subagent definitions), Hooks (commands run at lifecycle points like after every edit), and MCP servers. All four extend the agent, not the multiplexer, so they don't count. The Desktop app has the same model (desktop docs: 'Plugins are reusable packages that add skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers...', installed via a plugin browser/marketplace UI, /plugin command) with no desktop-specific mechanism to add a new panel, view, or command to Claude Code's own chrome beyond the plugin manager itself. Documented at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Agent SDK for Python and TypeScript plus headless `claude -p` with stream-json output; routines expose per-routine HTTP trigger endpoints; MCP client with channels for inbound events; `claude-cli://` deep links.

top.title: Claude Code is steganographically marking requests

editorial.reachRationale: npm shows ~70M/month (though via a deprecated install path) and brew cask claude-code 36.6k installs/30d, with an outsized HN footprint (9,080 stories); discounted the 1.79M X followers and 127k Discord as Anthropic-wide, not product-specific, since the product doesn't need them to clear the bar.
editorial.polishRationale: Judged from docs and the changelog rather than hands-on use: near-daily versioned releases, a weekly what's-new digest and unusually complete docs, but the surfaces are uneven, with Linux Desktop in beta, agent view and cloud sessions in research preview, agent teams experimental and CLI-only, Projects waitlisted and Pro/Max-only, Dispatch absent on Team/Enterprise, and Desktop's cross-session view blind to CLI and cloud sessions of the same project.
editorial.depthRationale: This is the only record where the multiplexer, the agent and the model vendor are one product, and it goes further than any sibling on reach: sessions move between terminal, Desktop, browser and phone (`/desktop`, `--cloud`, `--teleport`, Continue in), message each other across machines and into the cloud, are spawned by a Project or by Dispatch from a phone, run on Anthropic VMs or on self-hosted runners, and are fed by routines with schedule, API and GitHub triggers plus auto-fix and auto-merge on the resulting PRs.
editorial.feelRationale: The CHANGELOG documents a long, recurring pattern of TUI responsiveness bugs rather than one-off jank: fullscreen freezing/blanking on scrolling, keystrokes lagging behind spinner/streaming repaints, sustained high CPU from busy loops, 'TUI lag with many parallel subagents,' the terminal freezing during long streamed responses, and freezes at session start, in the agents list, and after the security dialog, each patched separately across many dated releases.

tools.name: Claude Code Haha
tools.tagline: Give Claude Code somewhere you can watch it work
tools.valueProp: A desktop shell built directly from Claude Code's own CLI source, so subagents, skills, memory, MCP and permissions behave exactly as they do in the terminal, but you swap the model underneath (Claude, ChatGPT or Grok via OAuth; DeepSeek, Zhipu GLM, Kimi, MiniMax or a local Ollama/LM Studio model) instead of swapping which coding agent runs. It stays local-first with no forced account of any kind, and follows you off the desktop through H5 mobile pairing or two-way bot control, not just notifications, across eight chat platforms (Feishu, Telegram, WeChat, DingTalk, WhatsApp, WeCom, QQ, Slack).

pricing.notes: Free and open source (MIT); no pricing page found on the site or in the docs map. You bring your own Claude/ChatGPT/Grok account or a third-party API key (DeepSeek, Zhipu GLM, Kimi, MiniMax and others), or run a local model via LM Studio/Ollama at no cost; the project does not resell or bill for model usage. README: 'maintained in the author's spare time', sponsorships and enterprise/custom-integration work are by direct contact with the author, not a published tier.

featureNotes.platforms.tui: The bundled `claude-haha` CLI (`./bin/claude-haha`) starts an interactive full-screen terminal session by default, inherited from Claude Code's own engine; `--print` runs it non-interactively for scripts/CI instead.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: The local REST/WebSocket server (Bun.serve, default 127.0.0.1:3456) can be started headless on a machine you own and reached remotely via H5 token auth behind your own reverse proxy ('headless deployment' in the internals/server docs), but this is the same local-access server relocated, not a documented SSH/daemon-attach workflow to a separate remote host.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: `bun run src/server/index.ts` runs the same server the packaged app manages automatically; docs cover startup flags, auth modes, a reverse-proxy checklist and a troubleshooting table for self-hosting it.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Not a wrapper around the external Claude Code CLI: the engine (internally `claude-haha`) is built from 'repaired Claude Code sources' and reuses the same tool/permission/subagent/skill/MCP machinery per the docs ('same machinery, just shown as an interface'). Only this one engine ships, you switch the model backend (Claude/ChatGPT/Grok OAuth, third-party API keys, or local LM Studio/Ollama), not the coding-agent CLI itself, so codex/geminiCli/cursorAgent/opencode/amp/pi/anyCli are all false here.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: `-w/--worktree [name]` CLI flag and an 'Isolated worktree' toggle in the desktop composer and in Scheduled tasks create a dedicated Git worktree per session/task; `--tmux` opens it in a tmux pane (iTerm2 pane on macOS).
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Creating a worktree implies a new Git branch, and you can name it, but no separately documented automatic branch-naming/per-task convention beyond the worktree name was found in the pages read.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: The desktop feature map lists 'undoing a turn that went wrong' as a bullet on the sessions page; no broader session-snapshot/rollback system is documented in any page that was read.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Permission requests and 'needs-you' prompts push to native desktop notifications and to any configured IM channel (interactive cards on Feishu/DingTalk, buttons on Telegram, text replies elsewhere); Scheduled tasks can also push a completion summary to the same channels.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Agent Teams: `TeamCreate`, teammates spawned with `name`/`team_name`, `SendMessage` (including broadcast `to:"*"`) and shutdown-request/response coordination, run in-process by default or in a tmux/iTerm2 pane.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Privacy page: the bundled upstream agent runtime may contact diagnostic/analytics/feature-flag services; setting `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` reduces or disables non-essential traffic.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False, mirrors Claude Code's own excluded plugin model exactly, agent-side only. The `--plugin-dir <path>` CLI flag and `plugin`/`plugins` subcommands load bundles of skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers into the agent, and the 'Plugin' source tier in Settings plus the two-source (ClawHub + SkillHub) Skills Market with security-scan badges are all ways of distributing SKILL.md/agent/MCP bundles to the agent running inside cc-haha. Nothing here adds a panel, view, command or provider to cc-haha's own desktop/CLI interface. Documented at https://cchaha.ai/en/cli/reference and https://cchaha.ai/en/desktop/skills.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Local REST + WebSocket server exposes `/api/*` (sessions, agents, tasks, teams, skills, plugins, IM adapters, Computer Use, diagnostics) and `/ws/<session-id>`; full MCP client support via `--mcp-config`, `--strict-mcp-config` and an `mcp` subcommand.

github.description: 本地优先的跨平台 Claude Code / AI Agent 桌面工作台：多 Agent 协作、Git Worktree、代码 Diff、技能市场、多模型、Computer Use、桌面宠物；支持微信、飞书、钉钉及 H5 等远程访问。 | Local-first Claude Code / AI Agent desktop workspace: multi-agent teams, Git worktrees, diffs, skills marketplace, multi-model, Computer Use, task-aware desktop pets; remote via WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, Telegram, WhatsApp & H5.

editorial.reachRationale: Product-specific community signals are flatly absent, no X account, no Discord, 0 Hacker News stories for any query tried, no npm/Homebrew listing, which is more extreme than every comparable desktop-workspace sibling read (e.g. Orca had a 4.4k Discord and 16k X followers as of September 2026). Leaned on the real usage signals that do exist (53,866 release-asset downloads across the last 5 releases, 36 contributors, 189 open issues, near-daily commits for ~6 months) but discounted the 14.7k stars / 8.6k forks heavily: the unusually high fork:star ratio is more consistent with developers forking a 'repaired Claude Code sources' codebase to study or reuse than with a multiplexer's own user community, so this lands as emerging rather than established.
editorial.polishRationale: A fully built three-OS desktop app with 16 settings tabs, an in-app updater with proxy fallback, and detailed docs, but distribution is GitHub-Releases-only (no App Store, no Homebrew/AUR/winget) and both macOS and Windows installers are documented as unsigned, requiring a manual xattr/script workaround on macOS and a SmartScreen click-through on Windows until SignPath onboarding finishes. This is a rough edge Orca and Superset don't share at this same tier.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes well past a tmux wrapper with isolated per-session worktrees with tmux/iTerm2 panes, line-anchored diff review, six built-in subagents plus user-defined ones, full Agent Teams multi-agent coordination (SendMessage broadcast, shutdown handshake, three execution backends), cron-style scheduled tasks that run in their own worktrees, a two-source Skills marketplace, Computer Use screen control, and a local REST/WebSocket/MCP server reachable from H5 mobile or 8 IM platforms with two-way session control. Held back because there's no in-app PR creation, no merge-conflict assist, no task board/kanban, and no voice control, all confirmed absent in the docs read.
editorial.feelRationale: Electron desktop app (repo topic `electron`, DMG/exe/AppImage/deb builds); no GPU-rendering or native-toolkit claims were found in any docs page read, and none of the maker's own pages make a performance claim either way. A web search ('cc-haha Claude Code Haha slow OR fast OR laggy') returned no user reports about this product specifically, only the repo itself, generic Claude-Code-is-slow complaints unrelated to this app, and an Instagram post. Typical unoptimised-but-uncomplained-about Electron app, so rated as fine rather than fast or sluggish.

tools.name: Claude Squad
tools.tagline: Manage multiple AI agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Aider.
tools.valueProp: Its Go TUI puts each CLI agent in a tmux session and managed worktree, with preview and diff tabs. A checkout action commits and pauses an agent so you can take over its branch.

pricing.notes: Claude Squad is free; install and pay for whichever external coding agents you run.

featureNotes.agents.anyCli: The --program flag and named profiles launch an arbitrary local command; no agent protocol is required.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: The s action commits, syncs/pushes the branch, and opens its branch URL; session/git/worktree_git.go does not call gh pr create despite the Submit PR label.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Checkout commits and pauses the session for manual takeover; the repo does not document merge or conflict handling.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Config-only extension of the app: README Configuration documents named profiles and --program for custom agent launch commands. There is no documented loader for third-party panels, commands, or lifecycle code in the TUI.

github.description: Manage multiple AI terminal agents like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Amp.

top.title: Claude Squad – A terminal app that manages multiple Claude Code instances

editorial.reachRationale: 11,007 downloads from the five latest release assets, 127 Homebrew installs in 30 days, and 20 contributors suggest an established user base. I discounted 8,538 GitHub stars because attention is not use and the six matching HN stories had little engagement.
editorial.polishRationale: The stable 1.0.20 release, installers for three desktop operating systems, profile picker, and session recovery show a usable product.
editorial.depthRationale: Its scope stays compact: tmux sessions, worktrees, preview and diff, commit/push and checkout, without a task board or automated merge flow.
editorial.feelRationale: The interface is a Go TUI driving tmux sessions, so input and terminal rendering use the local terminal rather than a browser or Electron layer. The repo contains a lightweight preview and diff view; no measured latency or independent speed reports were found.

tools.name: CLI Agent Orchestrator
tools.tagline: Lightweight orchestration for multi-agent AI workflows
tools.valueProp: The broadest provider roster in the index: a dozen CLI agents run as native processes in isolated tmux windows, so a supervisor on one provider can hand off to a worker on another. AWS-shaped for fleets, with a Kubernetes worker mode and no GUI.

pricing.notes: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); no CAO-specific fee or tier. All cost is whatever the provider CLI you run charges (Anthropic/OpenAI/AWS/Google/etc. subscriptions or API keys), CAO never resells tokens.

featureNotes.platforms.windows: pyproject.toml classifiers list only macOS and POSIX::Linux, with a comment explaining why: the package imports `fcntl`/`termios` at module scope and orchestrates through tmux, neither of which exists on Windows; the package guards the first `cao` command with an explanatory error rather than failing silently.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: The full-screen terminal experience is tmux itself (a prerequisite CAO manages sessions/windows in), not a separate TUI CAO built; `tmux attach` to any `cao-` session gives the tmux-standard full-screen window/pane interface.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Docs/intro: 'Antigravity CLI is the Google-backed provider (formerly Gemini CLI)', the provider was renamed/replaced rather than kept as a separate 'Gemini CLI' entry, so there is no first-class 'geminiCli' provider distinct from Antigravity CLI.
featureNotes.agents.pi: Oh My Pi (OMP), the successor to Pi, is a first-class provider (`omp`); plain 'Pi' is not listed separately in the provider table.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: docs/core-concepts/architecture: 'the abstract BaseProvider interface means any CLI tool that runs in a terminal can be orchestrated', this is a developer-facing extension point (write a Python provider class), not a no-code 'point at an arbitrary command' adapter like some competitors ship.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: CAO itself has no worktree concept. The bundled AI-DLC portfolio example (examples/aidlc-portfolio) layers isolated Git worktrees on top of CAO sessions, but that isolation is the child AI-DLC workflow's job, not a CAO feature.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Not a default/built-in feature. The bundled Kubernetes example (examples/cao-clusters/kubernetes/eks) runs each elastic worker as its own disposable pod via a broker, but this is an optional reference deployment, not something `cao launch` does locally.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Terminal-level, not file/agent-state: when a `handoff` completes the worker terminal is deleted, but its scrollback and metadata are saved to `~/.aws/cli-agent-orchestrator/logs/terminal/` and `cao terminal restore <id>` recreates the window with that scrollback for debugging.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: The Web UI ships a session/terminal dashboard and a Flows list (scheduled flows, next run time, enable/disable), but neither is a queue or kanban board of tasks feeding agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: No push/desktop alert is documented. IDLE/PROCESSING/WAITING_USER_ANSWER/COMPLETED/ERROR status is visible in the Web UI and CLI, and the plugin system's control plane explicitly supports 'outbound event streaming (Discord, Slack, webhooks, audit logs)' for a needs-you signal, but that requires configuring or writing an event plugin rather than being on by default.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Not a dedicated collaboration feature, but an inherent property of the transport: any user with host access can `tmux attach` to the same session, and the Web UI's PTY WebSocket (`/terminals/{id}/ws`) can be opened by more than one browser client at once, the docs even flag it as unauthenticated by default if bound beyond localhost.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Extends CAO itself: per docs/plugins.md, an 'event plugin' is a Python package (installed via the `cao.plugins` entry-point group) that runs inside the `cao-server` process, subclasses `CaoPlugin`, and reacts to server lifecycle events (`post_send_message`, `post_create_session`, `post_create_terminal`), it can also add new MCP tools to CAO's own MCP servers by overriding `on_mcp_server(mcp)`. This is enabled by default (unlike the separate, gated, agent-side 'Agent Plugins 1.0.0' skills+MCP bundle system the docs explicitly warn not to confuse it with), so third-party code genuinely extends the app's own process and server-side MCP surface, not just the agents it runs.

github.description: Multi-agent orchestration for AI coding CLIs — Claude Code, Kiro, Codex, and more, coordinated in isolated tmux sessions

top.title: Show HN: Version 1.0 of agent-of-empires CLI agent orchestration tool

activity.changelogCadence: CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section is updated with nearly every merged PR; tagged releases roughly every 1-2 weeks (4 in the last 90 days)

editorial.reachRationale: 72 contributors and 244 commits in the last 90 days show a genuinely active outside-AWS GitHub community past hobby scale, and PyPI downloads (1,248/month) confirm real external installs of the CLI. Discounted: 1,350 stars (attention, not use,) and any AWS/Amazon-wide social presence, there is no product-specific X or Discord account, and Hacker News searches under disambiguated queries surface no thread about this tool specifically, so reach reads as established (real, growing use) rather than major.
editorial.polishRationale: My call: it looks hastily assembled rather than refined. The docs are broad (a Docusaurus site, i18n, a blog, two interactive courses) and the web UI ships inside the Python wheel, but pyproject.toml self-classifies as Beta as of September 2026, the changelog shows security hardening landing (an unauthenticated-by-default WebSocket PTY, a token-in-logs leak fixed within the period observed), and the Agent Plugins surface is built but gated off by default.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes well past a tmux wrapper with handoff/assign/send_message orchestration patterns, a five-scope persistent memory system with BM25/hybrid search and self-healing lint, an opt-in self-learning loop that promotes retrospective lessons into agent profile files, cron-like scheduled Flows with gating scripts, a fine-grained role/allowedTools permission system, two purpose-built MCP servers plus an MCP Apps host-rendered fleet UI, OTel telemetry export, and a documented Kubernetes elastic-worker architecture for disposable fleets.
editorial.feelRationale: The primary interface is tmux itself (native, low-latency terminal multiplexing CAO delegates to rather than reimplements) fronted by an event-driven FastAPI backend (pub/sub bus, debounced status detection over a rolling 8KB buffer) and a React/TypeScript/Vite web dashboard, none of this is Electron or a heavy web app. No independent user reports of lag or slowness were found (a web search for 'CAO slow OR fast OR laggy tmux' returned only project announcements and docs, no performance commentary), so the score rests on architecture rather than field reports.

tools.name: Cline Kanban
tools.tagline: A replacement for your IDE better suited for running many agents in parallel and reviewing diffs.
tools.valueProp: Cline Kanban turns local CLI agent work into linked cards that can start the next task after a predecessor finishes. Each card gets an ephemeral worktree, live agent TUI, line-level diff comments, and an agent-assisted commit or PR.

pricing.notes: Kanban is a free Apache-2.0 local app. Agent provider costs or subscriptions are separate; no Kanban plan or team billing is documented.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Local Node.js server opened in a browser; no released native desktop app.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Local Node.js server opened in a browser; no released native desktop app.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Local Node.js server opened in a browser; no released native desktop app.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: Mobile-responsive browser UI only, per v0.1.60 changelog.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Mobile-responsive browser UI only, per v0.1.60 changelog.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Run Kanban on a server you control and access via SSH tunnel, Tailscale, or browser; the agent runs on that server.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Each started card gets an ephemeral managed git worktree; gitignored files such as node_modules are symlinked from the main checkout.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Open PR creates a new branch at shipping time; starting a card creates a worktree but does not document an automatically named branch.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Diff viewer scopes changes to message ranges; docs do not describe restoring files to a prior checkpoint.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Sidebar agent can create, link, and start board tasks through injected instructions; this is board orchestration, not general nested agent sessions.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Linked cards auto-start when predecessors complete; auto-commit and auto-PR are optional settings.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Changelog documents browser notifications with the latest agent message, but does not clearly limit them to blocked-on-input events.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: A server can be exposed to collaborators, but docs describe no named users, roles or presence.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial: Kanban lets users configure Script Shortcuts that run commands from its navbar and exposes board task control to its sidebar agent; it has no documented third-party code loader for new Kanban panels, agent runtimes, or lifecycle hooks. The mechanism is described in github.com/cline/kanban README sections 2 and 5 and docs.cline.bot/kanban/core-workflow; agent-side MCP setup does not count.

github.description: Launch a local web app that runs CLI agents in parallel

top.title: Cline Kanban

activity.changelogCadence: irregular: 2 releases in 12 weeks; last two were 6 days apart

editorial.reachRationale: Kanban itself has 4,314 npm downloads/month, 1,337 GitHub stars, 19 contributors and only a small product-specific HN response, consistent with emerging use. Cline’s 23,627-member Discord and 80,414-follower X account can bring discovery, but they serve the larger Cline product and cannot be attributed to Kanban users.
editorial.polishRationale: The README and docs explicitly call Kanban a research preview, and the latest v0.1.70 release fixed a large-board freeze; the web app nevertheless covers the core task flow across platforms.
editorial.depthRationale: Linked card automation, managed worktrees, live agent TUI, message-range diff checkpoints, inline review comments, agent-assisted commits/PRs and conflict handling reach beyond a simple session dashboard.
editorial.feelRationale: The board is a React/Vite web app with xterm.js (web-ui/package.json). Changelog v0.1.70 fixes a freeze when clearing completed tasks on large boards, and v0.1.57 reduces project-switch latency; those are concrete rough edges but not evidence of persistent broad UI slowness.

tools.name: CloudCLI
tools.tagline: Code from anywhere, even your phone
tools.valueProp: CloudCLI puts existing CLI sessions in the same plugin-enabled web UI whether you self-host it or rent a persistent cloud environment. Its hosted environment lets a phone-started session continue in VS Code over SSH.

pricing.notes: Self-hosted UI is free; hosted CloudCLI Cloud starts at €7/month, with Growth €20/month and Team €39/month. AI subscriptions or API keys are separate.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Optional Electron desktop companion; the server also runs via Node.js.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Optional Electron desktop companion; the server also runs via Node.js.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Node.js web server; no Linux desktop companion is listed on the download page.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: The cloudcli command starts the server or experimental sandbox; agent steering is mainly through web UI or REST API.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: Responsive web/PWA access only; docs say a native app is in development, as of September 2026.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Responsive web/PWA access only; docs say a native app is in development, as of September 2026.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Docs describe project directories, branches and cloud containers, but no CloudCLI-managed Git worktree per task.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Managed cloud environments use isolated containers; self-hosted Docker sandbox mode is marked experimental.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Built-in Tasks tab and optional TaskMaster integration, but no documented first-party Kanban flow for feeding agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Hosted API and n8n integration can trigger runs; scheduling is shown through a third-party CloudCLI Scheduler plugin.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Team plan shares a specific cloud environment with teammates; the owner controls access.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: True: third-party TypeScript code extends CloudCLI UI itself with custom top-level tabs and optional Node.js backend servers, using context events and RPC/WebSocket APIs. Documented at https://cloudcli.ai/docs/plugins/plugin-overview and https://cloudcli.ai/docs/plugins/getting-started; plugins cannot modify built-in tabs or agent chat.

github.description: Use Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, and Codex on mobile and web with CloudCLI (aka Claude Code UI). CloudCLI is a free open source webui/GUI that helps you manage your Claude Code session and projects remotely.

top.title: Show HN: CloudCLI-Web/Mobile UI for Claude Code,Codex and Gemini(8.2k stars)

editorial.reachRationale: 9,490 npm downloads/month, 4,666 downloads of the last five release assets, 701 product Discord members, and nine listed community plugins indicate an established product-specific user base. The 13,826 GitHub stars show attention but are discounted as usage evidence, and the hosted tier has no disclosed user count.
editorial.polishRationale: A stable 1.37 release line, desktop installers, mobile layout, coherent docs and a mature plugin guide; the latest changelog lists chat and session fixes.
editorial.depthRationale: Multi-agent session history, shell/files/Git diff review, cloud containers, team sharing, API automation and real UI plugins, but no managed worktrees or integrated PR review flow.
editorial.feelRationale: The main interface is a React/Vite web app with an optional Electron desktop companion (repo package.json and README). The changelog notes transcript performance and bandwidth fixes, but no reliable evidence establishes consistently fast or slow UI response; scored as a typical web app.

tools.name: Cloudroom
tools.tagline: Cloud Agents should be open source.
tools.valueProp: Cloudroom runs several coding harnesses in local threads or separate cloud sandboxes, with one desktop chat for each. Its Teleport feature moves a running thread between Mac and cloud while preserving the conversation.

pricing.notes: Free: 100 cloud agents and 25 cloud-compute hours per month; unlimited local agents. Pro $50, Super $150, Ultra $500 monthly. Model subscriptions or API keys are separate.

featureNotes.platforms.linux: Linux x64 AppImage is explicitly alpha; macOS is the primary download (docs/get-started).
featureNotes.platforms.web: The mobile browser app at /mobile offers phone access, but is not a general desktop web app. Docs/faq says Cloud threads work with Mac off, while the /mobile page says Mac must be awake; actual offline behavior is unresolved.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Cloudroom Core can run on a user-owned Linux machine and connect to the desktop app by URL and token (core README and docs/setup.md).
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Cursor is Local-only (docs/harnesses).
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Docs/local-threads says Local Worktree creates a new folder and Git branch and Cloudroom removes it after its last thread is deleted; Cloud threads instead use separate sandboxes and branches.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Each Cloud thread gets its own Linux sandbox; docs/cloud-threads says child threads can share the parent sandbox.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Cloud threads receive their own branch; Local Worktree creates a branch when chosen, while plain Local shares the project folder.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Git diff and Review are in the Local side panel only; docs/cloud-threads explicitly excludes Cloud threads.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Docs/cloud-threads says Open pull request in a Cloud thread menu has the agent open a PR from that branch.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Docs/subagents says the lead can check, message, stop and archive its child threads, and Cloudroom messages it when a child finishes.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: The Apache-2.0 desktop app runs Local without an account and can connect to a user-run Core by URL/token; the hosted Cloud sandbox service itself is not published for self-hosting (GUI/core READMEs).
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Third-party code can extend the app itself: the GUI repo ships a plugin SDK and loader, plus a documented composer plugin that adds actions, menu commands, banners, and rich-text behavior (gui/packages/plugin-sdk/README.md and gui/examples/plugins/composer-customization/README.md). This is app-level code, not agent skills or MCP.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: The bundled room-cli can start, message and inspect Cloudroom threads; the self-hosted Core documents an HTTP API (docs/get-started and core docs/api.md).
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: The privacy policy documents Settings → “Share usage data and setup errors” and room-cli settings general telemetryEnabled false; it also lists separate switches for title renaming and agent feedback.

github.description: Desktop app for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. Start an agent on your Mac and move it to the cloud mid-task.

editorial.reachRationale: The GUI repo has 125 stars, one contributor and hundreds of application downloads across recent tagged releases; update-manifest requests dominate its larger asset-download total. The product is public but early beta, so these signals support emerging reach rather than established use.
editorial.polishRationale: First-party docs cover installation, limits, Teleport and recovery; Mac downloads, a Linux alpha and a detailed daily changelog show a maintained product, while the beta label and documented Linux/phone limits cap the score.
editorial.depthRationale: My call: deep, but short of platform for a beta created in September 2026. Beyond parallel chats it has managed worktrees, separate cloud sandboxes, live Teleport, diff review, PR handoff, scheduled cloud agents, app-level plugins and steerable cross-harness child threads. Much of it is unproven in wide use.
editorial.feelRationale: Cloudroom's repo (davidondrej/cloudroom-gui) is tagged electron and desktop-app on GitHub and is mostly TypeScript/JavaScript, confirming a standard Electron shell; no reports of lag or praise for speed were found.

tools.name: cmux
tools.tagline: The terminal built for multitasking, organization, and programmability.
tools.valueProp: A terminal, not an orchestrator: a native Ghostty-based Mac app that adds notification rings, a scriptable browser pane and a socket API. No worktrees or PR flow of its own; the paid tier adds cloud VMs and an iPhone mirror.

maker.name: Manaflow, Inc.
maker.funding: YC S24 (as Manaflow; pivoted from an LLM-agent spreadsheet to cmux)

pricing.notes: Terminal is free and GPL; local agents run on your own keys. Pro $50/mo ($40/mo annual): Cloud agents on up to 50 vendor-hosted Cloud VMs (24 GB RAM / 6 vCPU shared), the iOS app, email support, no metering. Team $60/user/mo ($48 annual) adds centralised billing and priority support. Enterprise (contact sales): self-hosted or air-gapped Cloud execution, SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC 2, SLA. A one-off Stripe 'Founder's Edition' grants early access to cmux AI, iOS, Cloud VMs and voice mode.

featureNotes.platforms.windows: Only 'cmux TUI', the Rust terminal multiplexer (curl installer or `npx cmux`), ships for Windows x64 (Arm via emulation). The GUI app is macOS only.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: cmux TUI runs on x64/Arm64 Linux. A separate nightly-only 'cmux Browser' Linux build (Chromium tabs + workspaces + terminal surfaces) comes from the manaflow-ai/cmux-v2 repo. The Ghostty GUI app is macOS only.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: TestFlight beta ('cmux BETA'), gated behind Founder's Edition or the Pro plan. Mirrors Mac terminals over your own Tailscale/local network; Lock Screen notification replies.
featureNotes.platforms.macos: Native Swift + AppKit on libghostty; macOS 14+, Apple Silicon and Intel. DMG with Sparkle auto-update or Homebrew tap manaflow-ai/cmux.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: cmux TUI is a separate Rust multiplexer (macOS/Linux/Windows) with headless sessions, attach, SSH machine rail and a JSON-lines control socket.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: `cmux ssh user@host` uploads a cmuxd-remote relay daemon: browser panes route through the remote network, remote agents notify the local sidebar, mosh transport. `cmux ssh-tmux` mirrors remote tmux (beta). TUI attaches to headless sessions over SSH.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Pro/Team only: persistent vendor-hosted Linux 'Cloud VMs' (up to 50, 24 GB RAM / 6 vCPU shared) that agents clone repos and open PRs on. Free tier has none.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Only on Enterprise (contact sales): self-hosted or air-gapped Cloud execution and networking. No public server component to run yourself; the SSH relay daemon runs on hosts you own but is not a server.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Named on homepage/README and in the session-resume integration list; no dedicated docs page.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Named only in the session-resume hook list ('Copilot'); no dedicated docs page.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: 'Cursor CLI' in the resume list; Cursor approvals surface as Needs-input notifications (0.64.23).
featureNotes.agents.amp: First-class since 0.64.23: auto-resume, completion notifications, Vault history, managed `amp` shim.
featureNotes.agents.pi: Named for notifications (hooks/OSC), Vault indexing and fork-from-checkpoint; oh-my-pi integration page.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: It is a terminal: any CLI works. Notification rings need the agent to emit OSC 9/99/777 or call `cmux notify` from a hook.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: 'cmux AI' is listed only as a Founder's Edition early-access item; no user-facing docs describe a built-in agent.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: cmux does not create or manage worktrees. The custom-commands docs ship a 'Worktree Agents' cmux.json example whose shell command runs `git worktree add` then launches Codex and Claude in it; their blog argues the agent should manage worktrees.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Pro Cloud VMs are isolated remote Linux machines but persistent ('pets, not cattle'), not per-task sandboxes. No local container isolation.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: A WebKit diff viewer pane exists (referenced in the MDM policy docs and 0.64.24 release notes) but has no docs page; no review-and-comment flow.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: The sidebar shows linked PR status/number per workspace; PRs are opened by the agent, not by cmux.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Vault (0.64.23) records checkpoints of Claude Code, Codex, Pi and Grok sessions and can fork from one (`cmux fork`). Session restore rebuilds layout and resumes agent sessions; it does not snapshot files or process state.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: None. The 'Task Manager' is a CPU/RAM process monitor (`cmux top`), not a task queue.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: No orchestrator of its own. Any agent can create workspaces, split panes, send input and read screens via the CLI/socket (skills ship for this). `cmux claude-teams` and oh-my-opencode/codex/pi render their teammates as native splits.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Event-triggered rule engine in ~/.cmuxterm/automations.json with notify, RPC, run and webhook actions (0.64.23). No scheduled runs documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Notification rings, sidebar badges, macOS banners, custom shell command, notification hooks, iOS push forwarding, and inline replies from the banner or Lock Screen. Fires on OSC 9/99/777 or `cmux notify`.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Only as a primitive: `cmux send --surface <id>` / socket `surface.send_text` lets one session type into another. No inbox or message channel.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: 'Voice mode' appears only as a Founder's Edition early-access item.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Accounts exist for Cloud VMs, the iOS pairing and billing; Team plan is per-user seats. The terminal itself needs no sign-in.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: GPL-3.0-or-later per LICENSE and README; GitHub shows NOASSERTION because the LICENSE file prepends a Manaflow dual-licensing notice. Cloud VM backend is not open.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Terminal, SSH and the iOS terminal stream need no vendor server. iOS sign-in, pairing metadata and forwarded notification text go through cmux servers; Cloud VMs are vendor-hosted unless Enterprise self-hosts.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: `app.sendAnonymousTelemetry` defaults to true (PostHog, Sentry, remote feature flags); toggle in Settings > App or force off via the MDM key DisableTelemetry.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Config-only, not a code plugin system: per cmux.com/docs/custom-commands, `.cmux/cmux.json` (or `~/.config/cmux/cmux.json`) defines an `actions` registry mapping IDs to shell-command behavior that cmux surfaces in its own Command Palette, tab bar and keyboard shortcuts, plus reusable `commands`/workspace layouts. No mechanism loads third-party code to add new panels, views or providers to cmux itself; the skills collection and notification-hook shell commands extend the agent/notifications, not the app's own surface.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: CLI plus a JSON-RPC Unix socket covering workspaces, splits, input, screen reads, sidebar status, notifications and the browser; TUI has typed bindings for TS/Python/Go/Java/Rust. No MCP server documented.

github.description: Open source Ghostty-based macOS terminal with vertical tabs and notifications for AI coding agents. Built for multitasking, organization, and programmability.

top.title: Show HN: cmux - Ghostty-based terminal with vertical tabs and notifications

editorial.reachRationale: Strong product-specific signals: 380,702 release-asset downloads, 32k npm downloads/month, a 198-point Show HN with 77 comments, and a 165-contributor base together support a real, established user base past the early-adopter stage; discounted the 27k stars somewhat since a viral Ghostty-based launch inflates GitHub attention faster than use.
editorial.polishRationale: A native Swift/AppKit app on libghostty with a 25-page docs site, MDM policy keys, localisation in nine languages, Sparkle updates, a Homebrew tap and a release roughly every week (three changelog entries in four days), plus 27k stars and a 165-contributor repo (created January 2026). Held back because much of the surface is flagged beta (iOS on TestFlight, remote tmux, TextBox, Linux as a nightly-only separate repo), several shipped features (automations, Vault checkpoints, the diff viewer) exist only in release notes, and 5k open issues signal churn.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes past a tmux wrapper with notification rings and inline replies, a scriptable browser pane, an SSH relay daemon, Vault session search with fork-from-checkpoint, an automations rule engine and Cloud VMs, but by design it has no task board, no worktree or branch management, no PR or merge flow and no agent of its own. The README calls it 'a primitive, not a solution'.
editorial.feelRationale: Native Swift/AppKit app with GPU-accelerated libghostty rendering, explicitly built (per the README's origin story) to avoid the Electron/Tauri jank the maker found in competing orchestrators, and praised by users as feeling 'like switching to a rocket' from Warp. Held back by GitHub records a closed issue for a ~2s terminal-pane load delay after drag-and-drop, and Reddit threads report the app freezing after ~24 hours of use and input lag while Codex is running.

tools.name: Codeg
tools.tagline: Run every coding agent together, and keep the work moving on every screen.
tools.valueProp: Aggregation first: it imports the on-disk session history of fifteen agents into one searchable store, so a Codex run can read last week’s Claude Code transcript. Ships as desktop, server or Docker with iOS and Android clients, but access is a single shared token.

maker.name: XinTaoFei (xintaofei)
