maker.funding: No company or investors disclosed; README and docs carry paid sponsor placements from API-relay and cloud vendors (Compshare/UCloud, OneHop, APIMart and others)

pricing.notes: Free and Apache-2.0 with no account, plans or paid tier. Codeg ships no model; each agent signs in with your own subscription, provider API key or custom endpoint.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Tauri/WebKit app, Apple Silicon and Intel .dmg, signed and notarized by Apple.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: x64 and arm64 installers; not Authenticode-signed, so SmartScreen shows an unknown-publisher notice. Server self-update is disabled on Windows.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: x64 AppImage plus .deb/.rpm for x64 and arm64; needs WebKitGTK (libwebkit2gtk-4.1).
featureNotes.platforms.ios: App Store app 'Codeg Client' (id6785199071), SwiftUI, requires iOS 26+. Docs label it a 'current test release' whose features and distribution may change. It is a client only: agents and files stay on your desktop or server.
featureNotes.platforms.android: APK from GitHub releases (xintaofei/codeg-android), Jetpack Compose, Android 12+; no Play Store listing. Same 'test release' caveat and client-only role as iOS.
featureNotes.platforms.web: Same UI served by the desktop app's Settings → Web Service or by codeg-server/Docker, guarded by an access token; side panels become drawers on narrow screens.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: codeg-server is a headless server binary configured by environment variables, not a CLI for starting or steering agents. Chat-channel slash commands are the closest thing.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Run codeg-server or the Docker image on a machine you own and reach it from any browser or the mobile apps; the desktop app can also attach to a remote workspace and send custom HTTP headers (e.g. Cloudflare Access) since 0.28.2. No relay: you expose it yourself over LAN, VPN, tunnel or reverse proxy.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Docs: 'there's no Codeg account, no cloud in the middle'. Codeg provisions no compute.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: codeg-server plus codeg-mcp companion: one-line installer for Linux/macOS/Windows, signed tarballs, multi-arch image on ghcr.io and Docker Hub, Compose example, self-update with rollback under --supervise.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Anthropic's claude CLI does not speak ACP, so Codeg installs the @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp adapter (maintained by the ACP org), which reuses your ~/.claude login and settings.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Runs through the @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp adapter rather than the codex CLI; ChatGPT login happens inside Codeg. CODEX_PATH can point the adapter at your own codex binary.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Vendor CLI run over its own ACP support; Google login is completed by running gemini in a terminal once.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Not on the fifteen-agent roster; would need registering as a custom ACP agent.
featureNotes.agents.opencode: Downloaded as a bundled binary; per-tool permissions exposed from OpenCode's own schema.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Bundled cursor-agent binary; official subscription via cursor-agent login or a Cursor API key for headless machines.
featureNotes.agents.pi: On the roster, but Pi ignores MCP servers so it can be delegated to yet cannot lead a delegation. Repository .pi/extensions run at startup; since 0.25 trust is prompted per workspace.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Custom agents must speak ACP: pick one from the public ACP registry or paste its distribution JSON and Codeg installs it and records its sessions. An arbitrary non-ACP command is not supported.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Docs: 'Codeg ships no model of its own.' Every agent brings its own credentials.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: To-do tasks each get a worktree <project>-task-<id> created by Codeg, pinned to HEAD at launch, reused across retries; the branch selector also creates ad-hoc worktrees with a fresh conversation rooted in them.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: The Docker image containerises the server, not individual tasks. Agent settings say 'Codeg adds no sandbox itself'; the optional 'let the agent handle files and commands' switch defers to whatever sandbox the agent configures.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Task branches are named task/<id>; the agent is instructed to commit there and never touch the base branch.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Live diffs beside the conversation, a Changes tab with commit/pull/push/stash, and a review column on the task board where you read the diff before accepting.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Only for tasks started from the Repository panel: delivering a reviewed task opens a pull request for an issue-derived task (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo) or pushes onto the existing head branch for a PR-derived one. No generic 'open PR' action for ordinary conversations is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Three-pane merge editor with per-hunk accept for any conflicting merge, rebase or pull; accepting a task pulls the base branch into its worktree, resolves conflicts there, and verifies the merge with git before marking it done.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: No agent-state or file checkpoints. The only rollbacks documented are server self-update rollback and undo of configuration-snapshot imports (0.30.10).
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Split View: right-click a tab to split right or down into any number of groups, each with its own tab strip; layout and drafts persist per workspace.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: To-dos board (To do / In progress / Needs you / Done) with per-folder concurrency limits, scheduling, an init command per worktree, and an optional auto-land rule that is off by default.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Delegation ships off and is enabled in Settings → General. Thirteen of fifteen agents can lead (they must accept MCP tools over ACP); OpenClaw and Pi can only be workers. Hand-off is non-blocking and each sub-agent is its own live session shown as a card.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Saved composer setups run headlessly on a cron schedule or on demand, starting a session or (since 0.23) queueing a to-do; seven built-in templates.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: OS notifications (on by default) for turn complete, permission request, agent question, agent error, background task and work task; plus pushes into Telegram, Lark (Feishu) or WeChat with /approve and /deny from chat.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: One-way: a lead hands a self-contained task to a sub-agent and reads its answer back, and any agent can @-mention and read another agent's stored session. Sub-agents start cold and there is no peer messaging between running sessions.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: No dictation or voice mode appears anywhere in the README or docs.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Installation docs pitch codeg-server for 'headless or team use', but auth is one shared bearer token with no user accounts, roles or per-person settings; notifications and sounds are stored per browser, not per user.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Anyone holding the token sees and can steer the same conversations on that server; no presence, roles or per-user history.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: No plans, billing or admin of any kind.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Apache-2.0 on the desktop app, server and both mobile clients (xintaofei/codeg, codeg-ios, codeg-android).
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Docs: 'There is no server component you don't run yourself.' No relay; mobile clients connect directly to your host over whatever network path you expose.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Per agent: official subscription reused from the CLI's own login, a provider API key/custom endpoint, or a saved Model Provider (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini).
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Docs: 'no analytics, telemetry, or tracking of any kind'; network is used only for agent calls, git remotes, forge API, update checks, agent installs and chat channels.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: No plugin API for Codeg itself. Appearance settings allow colour-token overrides, portable theme JSON and a sandboxed custom stylesheet (docs.codeg.app/reference/settings/appearance), which restyle the existing UI but cannot add panels, commands or providers. ACP agents, skills and the MCP registry extend the agents Codeg runs, not Codeg.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: A token-guarded HTTP/WebSocket API exists (consumed by the open-source mobile clients; POST /api/health is the only endpoint documented) plus a codeg://session/<id> URL scheme on desktop. The built-in codeg-mcp server hands delegation tools to agents; it is not an external control surface.

github.description: Collaborative multi-agent AI coding workspace: aggregate sessions from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Grok Build, etc. Desktop app, self-hosted server, or Docker.

top.title: Show HN: VDP – open-source unstructured visual data ETL

editorial.reachRationale: Decent release-asset downloads (32,940) and active commit cadence show ongoing use, but there's no npm/brew distribution, no Discord or X account, and no legible HN reception in English-language channels (the tool's community appears to live on WeChat/LinuxDO), so visible reach stays limited.
editorial.polishRationale: Notarized macOS builds, signed release artefacts for every platform, a self-updating server with rollback, an App Store iOS client and docs plus README in ten languages; held back by an unsigned Windows installer, mobile clients labelled test releases as of September 2026 with the Android build APK-only, release notes that read like patch streams (57 releases in 90 days), and the fact that this rating comes from docs and release notes rather than hands-on use.
editorial.depthRationale: Beyond parallel sessions it documents a worktree-per-task board with a mandatory review gate and git-verified merges, cross-vendor delegation through its own MCP companion, cron automations, Telegram/Lark/WeChat approval loops, a GitHub/GitLab/Gitea panel that turns issues into tasks and delivers PRs, a three-pane merge editor, token-usage reporting and Office-document editing; few tools in the set go that far. Rated from docs and release notes, not hands-on use.
editorial.feelRationale: Tauri app (src-tauri directory; docs describe the desktop app and codeg-server sharing one Rust core) with a webview renderer rather than a GPU-native one; settings expose a hardware-acceleration toggle to work around black-screen/rendering glitches on some AMD, Intel and Nvidia setups, but an HN/Reddit/GitHub search turned up no maker claims or user reports about general speed or lag.

tools.name: Coder Agents
tools.tagline: Coder Agents is a chat interface and API for delegating development work and research to coding agents in your Coder deployment.
tools.valueProp: Coder Agents runs its own agent loop in a self-hosted Coder control plane and provisions governed workspaces only when a task needs compute. Unlike Xum, it is a multi-user chat and API built into an existing Coder deployment.

pricing.notes: Community AGPL deployment includes up to five concurrent Coder Agents at no charge; more queue. AI Premium adds unlimited concurrent agents with purchased Agent Time; infrastructure and model provider costs are separate.

featureNotes.platforms.cli: Coder CLI and Chats API can initiate/steer chats; the primary interface is web.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Coder Agents provisions separate Coder workspaces from templates; docs do not say it creates or manages Git worktrees.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: An agent workspace can use Docker, Kubernetes or VM infrastructure according to the selected Terraform template; a container is not guaranteed.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: The agent can push commits and create PRs through configured git credentials; no dedicated in-chat PR creation control is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Chats API supports triggers from CI/CD and webhooks; no built-in scheduler is documented.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Chats can be shared for live read-only viewing; only the owner can steer the agent.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Coder Community core is AGPL-3.0, including a five-concurrent-agent pool; Premium/AI Premium entitlements and enterprise capabilities are commercial.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: The agent loop, chat history and tools run in the Coder deployment; AI Premium Agent Time usage is reported to Coder billing servers.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Admins configure their own provider keys or self-hosted model endpoints; it does not use a developer Claude Code/Codex subscription.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Config-only extension of the Agents surface: Terraform workspace templates define agent compute, and admins configure models/system prompts. /platform-controls and /extending-agents document these; skills and MCP tools extend the agent only, with no documented loader for third-party chat panels, commands or agent runtime code.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: The Chats REST API creates and steers agent chats; /tasks-to-chats-migration documents its endpoints.

github.description: Secure environments for developers and their agents

activity.changelogCadence: weekly: 2 mainline releases in 3 weeks, with frequent patch releases

editorial.reachRationale: The parent Coder repo has 16,722 stars and 277 contributors, and its company Discord has 4,224 members, but those signals predate and span much more than Coder Agents. No product-specific adoption count was found; the feature is established enough to ship in GA yet its own reach remains emerging.
editorial.polishRationale: The feature is called generally available, has detailed administration docs and browser push alerts; product-specific usage remains hard to assess from the parent repo.
editorial.depthRationale: Template-based workspace provisioning, centralized model and access policy, subagents, persistent chat, read-only live sharing, in-chat diffs and a Chats API support a full organization workflow.
editorial.feelRationale: Coder Agents is a web chat backed by a Go control plane and remote workspaces. The getting-started docs identify workspace provisioning as the main startup latency and suggest prebuilt workspaces; no measured chat UI latency supports a higher or lower score than typical web-app responsiveness.

tools.name: Codex
tools.tagline: The same powerful coding agent, built into ChatGPT.
tools.valueProp: The model vendor’s own multiplexer, folded into the ChatGPT desktop app: local worktree threads, hosted cloud tasks, SSH hosts, a phone remote and scheduled runs under one login. Only OpenAI models and only its own agent; the CLI is open, the rest is not.

maker.name: OpenAI
maker.funding: Privately held, venture- and strategic-investor backed

pricing.notes: Codex is bundled with ChatGPT plans and shares one usage allowance with ChatGPT Work. Individual: Free $0 (limited Codex access), Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo (Codex on web, CLI, IDE extension and iOS, cloud integrations, GPT-5.6 family, credits top-up), Pro from $100/mo (5x or 20x Plus limits). Business $20/user/mo billed annually for 2+ users ($25 monthly): desktop and mobile apps, larger cloud VMs, SAML SSO, MFA, admin controls. Enterprise & Edu: contact sales, SCIM, RBAC, Compliance API audit logs, data residency, credit- or USD-based usage billing. Alternatively an OpenAI API key at API rates for CLI/SDK/IDE only, with no cloud features. Plus and Pro can buy extra credits; Voice in the desktop app costs $0.05/min from the same budget. The Feb 2026 app launch temporarily included Codex on Free and Go.

featureNotes.platforms.windows: Codex app for Windows shipped 2026-03-04 (update note on the launch post); Remote hosts and the Windows sandbox are documented for the ChatGPT desktop app on Windows.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: ChatGPT desktop app for Linux is a preview (announced 2026-08-12): .deb for Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 and Debian 13, .rpm for Fedora 43/44, install script for Arch, x64 and ARM64. Some features, including Computer Use, are not available on Linux as of September 2026. Codex CLI itself runs natively on Linux.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: The ChatGPT iOS app carries Codex: Remote (start, steer, approve and review tasks on a paired Mac or PC) and Codex cloud tasks. The changelog has dedicated 'ChatGPT for iOS' Codex entries (newest 2026-09-08) and the pricing page lists Codex 'on iOS' for Plus.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Remote connections docs say you can control a host 'from ChatGPT on iOS or Android' and event-triggered scheduled tasks work on mobile, but the pricing page lists Codex 'on iOS' only and the changelog has no Android-specific Codex entries; cloud-task UI parity on Android is unverified.
featureNotes.platforms.web: Codex cloud at chatgpt.com/codex: chats list, environments, code and security reviews, PR creation. ChatGPT web also hosts scheduled tasks and event triggers.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: Codex CLI is a full-screen terminal UI (agents overview, /agent thread switching, /voice, /hooks, /plugins); `codex exec` is the non-interactive mode.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Two paths: (1) Remote pairs your phone or another desktop with a Mac or Windows PC you own through QR-code pairing and an OpenAI relay ('A secure relay layer keeps trusted machines reachable'); the host must stay awake and signed in. (2) The desktop app can add projects on an SSH host from ~/.ssh/config and starts the remote Codex app server over SSH; chats run commands on the remote filesystem.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Codex cloud runs each task in an isolated environment on OpenAI-managed infrastructure (openai/codex-universal base image), configured per repository with setup scripts, env vars and secrets; GitHub and GitLab (beta). Business plans get larger VMs. Requires ChatGPT sign-in, not an API key.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: No self-hostable relay or cloud. The open-source app server (JSON-RPC) is a local process that talks to OpenAI's backend; the Remote relay and Codex cloud are OpenAI-hosted only.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Not supported as a harness. The app and CLI can /import instructions, settings, skills, plugins, projects and recent chats from Claude Code, Claude Cowork or Cursor, and keep them in sync, but they do not run those agents.
featureNotes.agents.codex: This is the Codex agent itself; the app, CLI, IDE extension and cloud all run the same OpenAI Codex harness with OpenAI models (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna).
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: No generic adapter for third-party agents. Extensibility is via skills, plugins, MCP servers and hooks around the Codex agent, not by swapping the agent.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Codex is OpenAI's own agent loop; model choice is limited to OpenAI models, optionally served through Amazon Bedrock (AWS credentials from configured commands since CLI 0.155.0).
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Cloud tasks run in isolated OpenAI-managed environments. Local runs are sandboxed with platform-native enforcement (macOS Seatbelt, Linux/WSL2 bubblewrap, native Windows sandbox) rather than containers; network access is off by default and gated by approvals.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Managed worktrees start on a detached HEAD from the chosen branch; you convert to a branch on demand with 'Create branch here' (default prefix codex/). Cloud tasks show codex/<slug> branches in the task list. No automatic per-task branch naming for local worktrees.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Launch post: review the agent's changes in the thread, comment on the diff, or open it in your editor. The IDE extension shows per-file diffs with Undo; Remote shows diffs on the phone; cloud tasks show summary and diff before you open a PR.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Cloud tasks: 'open a pull request when the work is ready'. Local worktrees: 'commit your changes, push your branch to your remote repository, and open a pull request on GitHub' from the worktree chat header.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Handoff performs the Git operations needed to move a chat and its code between a worktree and the local checkout, and copies .worktreeinclude files; no documented merge-conflict resolution flow.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Codex saves a snapshot of a managed worktree before deleting it and offers to restore it when the chat is reopened; the IDE extension has per-edit Undo. Docs otherwise advise creating Git checkpoints yourself before and after a task.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Launch post: agents run in separate threads organized by projects with built-in worktrees; homepage: 'agents work in parallel across projects'. Codex cloud runs tasks in parallel environments.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Activity view lists chats that are unread, running or waiting for input; Scheduled lists automation runs whose results land in a review queue; cloud has a task list with status. No kanban and no queue that feeds idle agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Subagent workflows are enabled by default: the main agent spawns parallel subagents (custom [agents] roles with their own model and reasoning effort, max_concurrent_threads_per_session) and collects their results; the app surfaces each subagent thread and the CLI has /agent. The Ultra intelligence level delegates proactively.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Scheduled tasks run on a schedule in the local project, on a dedicated background worktree, or in the cloud (web tasks cannot touch local folders). On web and mobile, tasks can also trigger from Gmail, Slack or GitHub pull-request events (since 2026-08-25). Managed via the desktop app or web only, not CLI or IDE.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Desktop settings for turn-completion, permission and question notifications; the Activity bell shows chats 'waiting for your response'; floating Pets show Running / Needs input / Ready / Blocked; mobile Remote gets 'notified when ChatGPT completes a task or needs your attention', with push, email or SMS channels on web; CLI `notify` runs an external program on turn completion.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Subagents return summaries to the parent thread only; no documented agent-to-agent or thread-to-thread messaging.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Voice in the desktop app (GPT-Live, $0.05/min from the Codex budget; 1.25 credits/min on credit-billed plans; not available with an API key). Codex CLI 0.155.0 added experimental /voice behind /experimental.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: ChatGPT Business and Enterprise workspaces with SAML SSO, SCIM, RBAC, groups and provisioning, managed configuration, plugin controls and Compliance API audit events.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Read-only snapshot links of a local Codex thread (macOS, since 2026-08-20; workspace links limited to the workspace, known secret patterns redacted). Cloud environments can be shared with the workspace. No live co-steering of one agent by two people.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Business $20/user/mo (annual, 2+ users) and Enterprise/Edu with workspace credit pools, overage limits, usage insights and an Analytics API.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Only the Codex CLI, SDK, app server, skills, plugins and the codex-universal cloud image are open (Apache-2.0, openai/codex, 125k stars). The docs' open-source page lists the IDE extension and Codex cloud as 'Not open source'; the desktop app (the multiplexer surface scored here) and the Remote relay are closed.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Every surface needs OpenAI's backend for models and, for Remote and cloud, OpenAI's relay and infrastructure.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: OpenAI is both the tool vendor and the model vendor: you sign in with a ChatGPT plan (usage included, credits for overage) or an OpenAI API key (API rates). There is no way to bring another vendor's subscription; the only alternative provider is Amazon Bedrock serving OpenAI models.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Config reference documents `analytics.enabled` (boolean, 'When unset, the client default applies') and an `otel` exporter table; both are user-level keys that project configs cannot override. Training defaults follow the ChatGPT or API account settings.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Agent-side only, nothing extends Codex's own interface. Per learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins, a Codex/ChatGPT plugin bundles skills, MCP servers, browser extensions and hooks that run inside the Codex/ChatGPT agent loop (e.g. "Installed 119 of 29 available plugins" in the CLI plugin browser), none of it adds a panel, view, command, provider/runtime or UI component to Codex itself, and the docs state plainly "Plugins aren't available in the IDE extension." No separate mechanism exists for extending the Codex app/CLI/IDE surface with third-party code.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Codex SDK (TypeScript and Python), `codex exec` for CI, and the Codex app server JSON-RPC protocol (experimental, not for production). Codex can consume external MCP servers, but hosting Codex as an MCP server (`codex mcp-server`) was deprecated 2026-08-24 and removed 2026-09-05.

github.description: Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal

top.title: The Codex App

editorial.reachRationale: npm @openai/codex ~80M/month and brew cask 96k installs/30d are the highest product-specific install numbers in the set, plus a 805-point HN launch; Discord (856k) and X (428k) are OpenAI-wide and were discounted but weren't needed to justify the score.
editorial.polishRationale: My call from hands-on use: solid, but buggier than many of the native Rust tools here. The changelog ships 17 dated entries a month across app, CLI and iOS, and installers cover macOS, Windows, Linux (preview), npm and Homebrew. But the app has become the general ChatGPT desktop app, so the coding command centre lives inside a much larger product, and the docs mix ChatGPT Work and Codex terms.
editorial.depthRationale: Beyond parallel threads and managed worktrees it has Handoff between worktree and local checkout, a cloud tier with per-repo environments and GitHub/GitLab/Linear/Slack triggers, scheduled and event-triggered automations with a review queue, subagents with custom roles, hooks, a plugin marketplace, SSH-host projects, a phone remote with approvals and diffs, voice, and enterprise admin surfaces (SCIM, RBAC, Compliance API, MDM-managed config). Judged from docs and changelog, not hands-on use.
editorial.feelRationale: My call from hands-on use: a bit laggy. The CLI core is Rust, but the desktop app ships inside the general-purpose ChatGPT app (Pets, Appshots, document artifacts), and switching and scrolling there feel slower than in the native Rust tools.

tools.name: CodexMonitor
tools.tagline: Monitor your Codex situation.
tools.valueProp: A native Tauri command center dedicated to one agent only: Codex. One shared codex app-server, worktree-per-branch agents, a built-in git/GitHub dock and Whisper dictation, with an optional self-hosted Tailscale daemon for driving it from iOS. No multi-agent support, no plugin system, no vendor server anywhere.

pricing.notes: No pricing page, no in-app purchase, no subscription anywhere in the README or marketing site; 'Get the app' links straight to the GitHub releases page. Fully free, open-source (MIT), BYO Codex/OpenAI account.

featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: README: 'Worktree and clone agents for isolated work; worktrees live under the app data directory (legacy .codex-worktrees supported)'; the Tauri IPC surface exposes dedicated add_worktree/remove_worktree/rename_worktree/apply_worktree_changes commands, and the backend has a shared src-tauri/src/shared/workspaces_core/ module for it, a first-party, managed worktree-per-agent flow, not a manual convention.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Nothing for the app itself: a full recursive tree listing plus a GitHub code search of Dimillian/CodexMonitor for 'plugin'/'extension' return zero hits for any CodexMonitor extension mechanism (the only match is Tauri's own unrelated `.vscode/extensions.json` and its bundled `tauri-plugin-*` dependencies, which CodexMonitor consumes, not exposes). The README documents no SDK, extensions folder or plugin manifest. The 'Skills' picker and MCP-server status the UI surfaces are read-only views into the Codex CLI's own skills/MCP configuration under $CODEX_HOME, agent-side, not a CodexMonitor-native way for third parties to add panels or commands to the app.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: README section 'iOS Support (WIP)': mobile layout runs and remote-backend mode works, but terminal and dictation are unavailable on mobile, there is no App Store listing, and setup requires a manual Xcode/TestFlight build script plus a Tailscale-connected desktop daemon, real but unfinished and not casually installable.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: The remote/mobile path is a daemon you run yourself (`codex_monitor_daemon` / `codex_monitor_daemonctl`, JSON-RPC over a Tailscale tailnet with a shared token), documented in docs/mobile-ios-tailscale-blueprint.md and the README's 'Headless Daemon Management' section, there is no vendor-hosted backend at all.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: The UI is a resizable sidebar/dashboard/thread layout ('Command center layout: Threads, reviews, and activity stacked into one view') with recent-activity lists per workspace; neither the README nor the marketing site describes a kanban/queue board of sessions.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: No telemetry, analytics, or crash-reporting SDK (Sentry, PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel) appears anywhere in the ~1,000-file repository tree; the app appears to ship with no telemetry to opt out of.

github.description: An app to monitor the (Codex) situation

top.title: Codex Monitor

editorial.reachRationale: 47,476 downloads across its last 5 GitHub release assets, 4,337 stars, 417 forks and 76 contributors for a single-purpose macOS-first niche tool, plus unprompted public praise from notable accounts including OpenAI researcher @tszzl ('needs to use @Dimillian's CodexMonitor'), real, measured adoption past hobby scale. Did not count the maker's personal X account (61.9k followers, @Dimillian) toward reach since it is a general-purpose indie-dev account covering several unrelated apps, not a CodexMonitor-specific channel; the low-engagement 2-point HN thread was similarly discounted.
editorial.polishRationale: A native Tauri (Rust + web UI) app with macOS overlay title bar/vibrancy, toast-driven auto-updates, resizable multi-panel layout, Whisper dictation, and a working (if WIP) iOS build with its own Tailscale-based remote daemon and headless CLI. That is an unusually complete surface for a repo created January 2026 as a solo/small-team build, backed by 76 contributors and 47k+ release downloads. Held back by no commits or releases since v0.7.67 (2026-03-24), 94 open issues, and iOS lacks terminal/dictation and any App Store distribution.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes well past a terminal wrapper with worktree-per-branch isolation, live git diff/log/branch management, GitHub Issues/PR browsing with an 'Ask PR' composer, a prompt library, and a self-hosted remote daemon for mobile access, but it is deliberately single-agent (Codex only, no Claude Code/Gemini/other CLI support), has no task board, no automations, no PR-creation flow, and no plugin system.
editorial.feelRationale: Native Tauri app (Rust backend, OS-native webview) rather than Electron; a contemporaneous Reddit thread contrasts Tauri favourably against a '300MB monstrosity of the Electron app' for the same Codex use case, and a testimonial calls CodexMonitor 'the best performing tool like this that I've used.' Held back by: no first-party performance benchmarks or claims were found, and Tauri's webview-rendered frontend is not the same class as a fully native Swift/GPUI renderer.

tools.name: Conductor
tools.tagline: Run a team of coding agents in the cloud.
tools.valueProp: The polished closed-source Mac app: free local worktrees, plus a paid tier that moves agents into vendor-run sandboxes with shared multiplayer chats. No self-hosting and no attach-your-own-machine path.

maker.name: Melty Labs, Inc.
maker.funding: YC S24; seed-funded (docs FAQ: 'a small team running on seed funding')

pricing.notes: Free: local workspaces on your Mac, parallel agents, bring your own subscriptions/keys; Conductor does not bill or resell model usage. Pro $50/mo: Conductor Cloud with included workspace hours, Multiplayer with up to 5 Pro users, Conductor API, mobile app 'coming very soon'. Teams $60/user/mo (invite-only): live collaboration for any team size, admin portal, centralized billing. Enterprise: custom (DPA, SAML SSO, SCIM, SLA, purchase-order billing). Usage-based pricing for cloud compute is planned.

featureNotes.platforms.windows: Install page: 'Conductor is not available for Windows or Linux yet'; a waitlist form is linked.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Install page: 'Conductor is not available for Windows or Linux yet'; a waitlist form is linked.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: Homepage lists 'iOS SOON' and the pricing page says 'Conductor mobile app COMING VERY SOON'; not shipped as of 2026-09-14.
featureNotes.platforms.android: No Android mention anywhere on the site; only iOS is announced.
featureNotes.platforms.web: No browser client. Homepage lists the desktop app, mobile (soon) and the API as the ways to 'conduct'; app.conductor.build is used for account, billing and API keys.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: A `conductor` CLI (routines, models, workspaces, chats) is documented in the API docs and preinstalled inside cloud workspaces since 0.80.0; no public install instructions for running it on your Mac were found. It drives cloud workspaces only.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Cloud FAQ: 'Can I use my own cloud machines instead of Conductor's? Not yet, but we are building a self-hosted cloud offering' for Enterprise.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Pro, Teams or Enterprise plans only. Vercel Sandbox (Firecracker microVM) in us-east-1, 8 vCPU / 16 GB / 32 GB ephemeral NVMe, Amazon Linux 2023; sleeps after 4 h idle and hard-stops at 23 h 50 m. GitHub repositories only.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: No self-hostable component; the self-hosted cloud offering is described as in development.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: GitHub Copilot appears only as a model provider selectable through the OpenCode harness, not as a Copilot CLI harness.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: The harness set is fixed to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode. You can point the bundled harnesses at your own executable, but there is no generic 'run this command' adapter.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Cloud workspaces run in isolated Vercel microVM sandboxes (Pro+ only). Local workspaces run agents directly on your Mac with your user permissions and no sandbox (FAQ: 'Agents run directly on your system without sandboxing').
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: New workspace = new worktree + new branch from the configured base; the agent is instructed to rename the branch to match the task ('Branch rename preferences').
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: 'Resolve conflicts preferences' are sent when an agent helps with merge conflicts; the Checks tab gates merge readiness; Graphite and GitHub stacked PRs are supported.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Automatic per-turn snapshots stored as private Git refs; revert deletes later chat turns too. Supported for Claude Code and Codex only, not Cursor or OpenCode.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Workspaces can be created from GitHub or Linear issues and listed on Home with by-person/project filters, but there is no kanban or task queue that feeds agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Cloud workspaces only: agents get a preinstalled Conductor CLI and workspace-scoped API key to create workspaces, start chats, send follow-ups and monitor other sessions (0.80.0 release notes, API cookbook). Not available in local workspaces.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Routines (0.85.0) run a saved prompt in a fresh workspace on a cron schedule, from a GitHub Action, or via a webhook URL. Cloud-only, so Pro/Team plans only.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Release notes reference completion sounds (0.52.0, 0.83.0) and macOS notifications that open the relevant chat (0.83.0 fix), but no docs page describes when notifications fire or whether waiting-on-input is covered.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Multiple chats in one workspace share the branch and files, and `.context` holds notes and handoffs, but no agent-to-agent messaging is documented. Claude Code's own agent teams can be enabled via an env var; that is Claude's feature, not Conductor's.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Voice input in the composer exists per a 0.83.0 fix note ('Fixed voice input sometimes getting stuck after recording'); no docs page describes it.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Cloud organizations. Pro users can collaborate with up to 5 Pro users; Teams removes the cap and adds an admin portal for roles.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Multiplayer (cloud workspaces only): teammates open the same chat, see live agent output and typing presence, follow, reassign and share workspace links.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Privacy page documents PostHog analytics (feature events, model errors, crash stack traces, OS and IP) with no documented off switch. The 'Enterprise data privacy' setting only disables features that call external AI providers.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Nothing for Conductor itself: per docs/reference/harnesses, the app supports a fixed, closed set of four harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) with no mechanism to register a new custom harness/runtime, and docs/guides/providers confirms all 'provider' configuration is just credential/env-var setup for those four fixed harnesses, not a plugin loader. Remaining extension points (MCP servers, slash commands, skills, `.conductor/settings.toml`, conductor:// deep links) all configure the agents Conductor runs, not Conductor's own panels, views or commands.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: REST API (api.conductor.build/v0, OpenAPI spec, beta), hosted MCP server (api.conductor.build/mcp, OAuth) and a `conductor` CLI. All of them manage cloud workspaces only and require a Pro plan.

top.title: Show HN: Conductor, a Mac app that lets you run a bunch of Claude Codes at once

editorial.reachRationale: No GitHub signal (closed source), but a product-specific X account with 26,497 followers, a 1,896-member Discord, 232 brew cask installs/30d, and a well-received 228-point Show HN ('run a bunch of Claude Codes at once') together support a real, established community past the early-adopter stage.
editorial.polishRationale: Judged from docs and release notes, not hands-on: the changelog ships roughly twice a week with long fix lists, docs are thorough and consistent, there is a keyboard-shortcut reference, accessible colour options and SOC 2 Type II, but the API, MCP server and several UI features are flagged beta/experimental and Windows/Linux/mobile are absent.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes well past a session switcher: inline diff comments that become agent attachments, an agent Review action, a Checks tab (CI, deployments, review threads, todos) gating merge, per-turn checkpoints, workspaces from GitHub/Linear issues, Graphite stacks, cloud sandboxes, multiplayer, routines and a REST/MCP API. Judged from docs and release notes, not hands-on use.
editorial.feelRationale: A Tauri/WebKit shell (Homebrew cask installer served from crabnebula.app, a Tauri CDN, and `src-tauri/icons` in the docs), not Electron, but the maker's own changelog shows a recurring pattern of freezes, stalls and crashes, 'fixed terminal freeze for certain shell configurations,' 'fixed a rare crash when rendering chat messages,' 'fixed updates not installing when the app becomes unresponsive', and the most recent release (0.85.0, Sept 2026) headlines 'reduced freezes and stalls when streaming long chats, opening diffs, restoring terminal history, or attaching large files.'

tools.name: Cube
tools.tagline: A cloud computer for your coding agents.
tools.valueProp: Cube gives every agent a worktree on one persistent, user-sized Linux cloud computer. Its Mac app, phone browser, and ready-made SSH access reconnect to that same machine, with compute billed only while it runs.

pricing.notes: Prepaid usage credit: CPU and memory billed while the machine runs; persistent SSD billed even while paused. Eligible new accounts may claim starter credit after adding a payment method. Agent subscriptions/model usage are separate. Old monthly subscriptions remain only for legacy accounts.

featureNotes.platforms.web: Phone browser can check and continue cloud agent sessions; desktop setup and machine control require the macOS app.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: SSH provides shell access to the Cube machine, but no separate Cube session-control CLI is documented.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: The site lists many installable agents, but does not document an arbitrary custom command adapter.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Cube creates a separate Git worktree and branch for each task on the shared cloud machine.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: One persistent Linux machine hosts all agents; the site contrasts this with a per-task microVM model.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: No supported third-party code loader for Cube panels, commands, providers, or lifecycle hooks is documented in the homepage, parallel-agents page, release notes, or public release-only repository. Agent CLIs installed inside the cloud machine extend those agents, not Cube itself.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Documented SSH access reaches the cloud machine; no Cube-control API or MCP server is documented.

editorial.reachRationale: The product-specific X account has 1,286 followers, and the public desktop release assets total 555 zip downloads across 32 listed versions; GitHub has only a release feed, not a source community. The Discord invite returned no member count and the disambiguated HN query had no stories, so use looks early.
editorial.polishRationale: The Mac installer, browser session access, SSH, machine controls, and billing pages form a usable product, but the 0.16 release feed shows frequent fixes and the older comparison page describes obsolete plan pricing.
editorial.depthRationale: Cube manages persistent cloud compute, agent installation, per-task worktrees, grouped screens, SSH, phone continuity, port forwarding, and live resource usage; no documented task board or in-app PR workflow was found.
editorial.feelRationale: The official licenses page names Electron, React, and xterm.js for the desktop interface. Recent release notes mention faster reconnects and fixes for terminal restoration, but no measured UI latency or product-specific user speed reports were found; 3 reflects a typical Electron terminal app.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.tagline: Cursor is your coding agent for building ambitious software.
tools.valueProp: The only tool here that runs no third-party harness: editor, agents window, CLI, web, iOS and Slack all drive Cursor’s own agent on Cursor-billed tokens. In exchange it owns the whole stack, down to cloud subagents and its own git host.

maker.name: Anysphere, Inc.
maker.funding: Acquired by SpaceX: the 2026-08-14 company post says 'Cursor has officially been acquired by SpaceX', completing a process that began with an April 2026 SpaceXAI partnership; the Terms of Service name Anysphere, Inc. as the vendor as of September 2026. Previously a VC-backed startup.

pricing.notes: Hobby $0: limited Agent requests, Composer, no cloud agents. Individual: Pro $20/mo, Pro+ $60/mo, Ultra $200/mo, each with two monthly usage pools (Cursor Models: Grok 4.6, Grok 4.5, Composer 2.5; Other Models at the model's API rate), on-demand usage billed in arrears, frontier models, MCP/skills/hooks, cloud agents, Bugbot on usage-based billing. Start (India only) INR 649/mo with the Cursor Models pool and cloud agents but no third-party models, Automations or SDK. Teams $40/user/mo Standard or $120/user/mo Premium (5x agent limits): central billing, team marketplace, cloud agents and automations with shared context, Bugbot, analytics, team-wide Privacy Mode, SAML/OIDC SSO. Enterprise custom: pooled usage, invoice/PO, SCIM, repo/model/MCP access controls, audit logs, service accounts, AI code tracking API. Cloud agents need a paid plan and are charged at API pricing for the selected model; Teams and Enterprise pay a $0.25 per million token Cursor Token Rate on third-party and BYOK usage; self-hosted Team Pools require Enterprise; Projects are not available on Enterprise; US data residency adds 10%.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Native .dmg, macOS 12 Monterey or later, Apple Silicon and Intel; Homebrew-core cask `cursor`.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Native .exe installer, Windows 10 or later; the CLI has a native PowerShell installer (`irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' | iex`) as well as WSL.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Signed apt (Debian/Ubuntu) and yum (RHEL/Fedora) repositories for amd64 and arm64, plus a portable AppImage.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: Native App Store app (id6767085653) for iPhone and iPad on iOS/iPadOS 26.0 or later: start and follow cloud, pool and My Machines agents, review and merge PRs, Remote Control of a desktop session, push notifications and Live Activities. Needs a plan with cloud agents (Start, Pro, Pro+, Ultra, Teams, Enterprise) and non-legacy Privacy Mode.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Docs: 'Android is planned.' The suggested path is cursor.com/agents in Chrome installed as a PWA, which counts as web here.
featureNotes.platforms.web: cursor.com/agents starts and manages cloud agents from any device (also the Android PWA path); cursor.com/dashboard holds environments, secrets, integrations, self-hosted pools and admin; Origin repos and PRs live at cursor.com/codebase.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: `agent` (curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash): interactive Agent/Plan/Ask modes, `-p` headless print mode for CI, `agent persist` detachable sessions, `& prompt` hand-off to a cloud agent, `agent worker start` to register the machine as a self-hosted worker, and `agent acp` for ACP clients.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: The CLI is an interactive single-conversation terminal program with slash commands, a status line and approval pagers; it is not a multi-session full-screen multiplexer. The Agents Window is an Electron desktop surface, not a TUI.
featureNotes.execution.local: The IDE, the Agents Window and the CLI run agents on your machine, optionally in per-agent git worktrees; the CLI has a sandbox mode for command execution.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Three paths. My Machines: `agent worker start` on any laptop, devbox or VM you own opens an outbound-only HTTPS connection and executes tool calls there (personal login, no Enterprise needed). Team Pools: named worker fleets (Enterprise plan, service-account keys, Kubernetes/partner-host templates). Remote SSH workspaces are also supported in the IDE and Agents Window. In every case the agent loop and inference stay in Cursor's cloud.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Cursor-hosted isolated Ubuntu VMs per agent with cloned repos, Dockerfile or snapshot environments, prebuilt Builds, secrets, network allowlists, Tailscale/PrivateLink/Cloudflare Tunnel options, computer use and remote desktop control. 'You can run as many agents as you want in parallel.' Paid plans only.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Only the tool-execution worker (`agent worker start`, `agent worker controller`) runs on your hardware; the agent loop, orchestration, inference and dashboard remain in Cursor's cloud and workers need outbound access to api2.cursor.sh. There is no self-hosted control plane.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Not runnable inside Cursor. The only Claude reference is compatibility: subagent definitions in `.claude/agents/` and `~/.claude/agents/` are read alongside `.cursor/agents/`.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Not runnable inside Cursor; `.codex/agents/` subagent files are read for compatibility only.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Cursor's own agent is the only harness, across the IDE, Agents Window, CLI, web, iOS, Slack, GitHub/Linear mentions, SDK and cloud agents.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: No adapter for third-party agents. The relationship runs the other way: the Cursor CLI exposes an ACP server (`agent acp`) so other clients can host Cursor's agent.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Cursor Agent with model routing across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, SpaceXAI (Grok 4.6, Grok 4.5), Meta and Cursor's own Composer 2.5; Auto mode uses Cursor Router on Teams and Enterprise. Built-in Explore, Bash and Browser subagents.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Agents Window creates a separate git checkout when you start or move an agent into a worktree; `.cursor/worktrees.json` runs setup commands (Unix/Windows variants) on creation; Cursor 3.5+ discovers existing worktrees and auto-cleans old ones up to a machine-wide cap. Also available from the IDE via Worktree Skills and from the CLI.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Every cloud agent, cloud subagent and Project runs in its own isolated VM (Cursor-hosted, or your worker for self-hosted). Locally the CLI offers a sandbox mode with network controls; the IDE has run modes but no container per task.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Cloud agents 'work on a separate branch, then push changes to your repo'; Slack's `autopr` option and the dashboard base-branch setting control PR behaviour. Local agents get a separate worktree when you use worktrees; no automatic branch naming for plain local sessions is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Agents Window 'new diffs view' to review and commit changes and manage PRs without leaving Cursor; Agent Review runs a Quick or Deep AI review on local changes (auto after commits or `/agent-review`); the iOS app shows full diffs, commits and checks.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Cloud agents open merge-ready PRs with screenshot/video artifacts on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Azure DevOps or Origin; automations have a PR-creation tool enabled by default; the Agents Window and iOS app manage PRs in-app.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: PRs can be merged (squash), marked ready, branch-updated and auto-merged from the iOS app and Origin, and cloud agents auto-subscribe to their PRs to fix CI and address review comments. No dedicated merge-conflict resolution feature is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Agent creates checkpoints before significant changes; click any checkpoint in the chat timeline to preview and restore files. Stored locally, separate from git, and restoring does not remove messages.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Agents Window is multi-workspace and 'works well when you want to run and manage many agents in parallel'; cloud agents are unlimited in parallel; the Cloud Agents dashboard, Slack `list my agents` and the iOS inbox (up to eight Live Activities) list running agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: No kanban or drag-to-queue board. Projects (beta, Sep 2026) give a coordinator agent that plans, delegates and tracks tasks across agents, and the dashboard lists runs; Cursor's cookbook ships a sample 'kanban board for cloud agents' built on the SDK rather than a product feature.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Custom and built-in subagents run foreground or background with their own context; `/in-cloud` hands a task to a cloud subagent on its own VM and branch, and `/autopilot` puts a PR on one; Projects coordinators create and manage as many agents as the work needs.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Cloud-agent Automations with cron schedules and triggers from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Slack, Linear, Sentry, PagerDuty and webhooks, plus marketplace templates; Subscriptions let a running agent wait on PR activity, CI, Slack replies or timers; Projects can watch channels and schedules.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Native OS notifications 'when an agent run finishes or when input is required' since Cursor 1.5 (Settings); iOS push notification per finished turn with Live Activities; Slack completion notifications. Nothing is documented for the CLI.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Parent agents receive subagent results and `cursor/task` completions; Projects coordinators direct their delegated agents and you can open and talk to any of them. No peer-to-peer messaging between independent sessions is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Documented only for the iOS app ('dictate instructions to agents for hands-free edits with live transcription'); no desktop or CLI voice input page was found.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Teams (one team per account) and Enterprise Organizations with multiple teams and per-team roles, SSO, SCIM, domain join, admin dashboard, Admin and Analytics APIs.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Send an agent's URL and teammates on the same Cursor team with repo access can open the run, conversation, changes and artifacts read-only; a team admin can enable 'team follow-ups' (service accounts only, or all) so they can steer it. Slack threads act as shared control surfaces for cloud agents.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Teams $40 or $120 per user per month with central billing, usage analytics, spend limits and SSO; Enterprise adds pooled usage, invoicing, SCIM, billing groups and audit logs.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Proprietary; the Terms prohibit reverse engineering. Only reference templates (e.g. anysphere/k8s-workers) and the cookbook are public.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: The agent loop, inference and orchestration always run in Cursor's cloud; even BYOK requests 'will still go through our backend', and self-hosted workers need outbound access to api2.cursor.sh.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Custom API keys are supported (docs 'custom API keys' section; the Cursor Token Rate applies to 'BYOK usage'), but requests transit Cursor's backend, Teams and Enterprise pay $0.25 per million tokens on top, and cloud agents are billed at API pricing through Cursor. Cursor primarily resells tokens; no Claude or ChatGPT subscription login.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Privacy Mode (any plan, on by default and enforceable for Enterprise) stops training and applies ZDR with providers, and the Terms forbid training without explicit agreement; no page read documents an off switch for product usage telemetry itself.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial: Cursor is a VS Code fork and installs third-party editor extensions from Open VSX (cursor.com/help/customization/extensions), which can add panels, views and commands to the editor but cannot reach the agent and background-agent surfaces; the extension API stops at the editor. Cursor Plugins and the Agent Plugins standard (cursor.com/docs/plugins) bundle rules, skills, subagents, hooks and MCP servers for the agent and do not count.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Cloud Agents REST API (agents, runs, artifacts, self-hosted pools and workers), `@cursor/sdk` (TypeScript) and `cursor-sdk` (Python) with local and cloud runtimes plus an SDK Bridge for other languages, Origin API, Admin/Analytics/AI-code-tracking APIs, a built-in Cursor Cloud MCP diagnostics server, and `agent acp`.

top.title: Cursor IDE support hallucinates lockout policy, causes user cancellations

editorial.reachRationale: @cursor/sdk npm at ~2.26M/month, a 39k-member product Discord, 482k X followers on the product's own @cursor_ai handle, and 692 HN stories place it as a default choice alongside Claude Code and Codex; GitHub stars aren't available (closed source) so this rests on the install and community numbers, not stars.
editorial.polishRationale: Judged from docs and the changelog rather than hands-on: signed installers on all three desktop OSes, a shipped App Store app, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/42001 and AIUC-1, MDM guides, docs in six languages and a weekly dated changelog; but much of the multiplexer surface is mid-rollout (Projects beta, Origin 'early beta', /goal and steering 'rolling out', Remote Control needing 3.9.8+), Android is 'planned', Projects are excluded from Enterprise, and the rename from Background Agents to Cloud Agents leaves stale terms in older changelog entries.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes far past a session switcher: Local worktree agents, a diffs view and AI Agent Review, unlimited parallel cloud VMs with computer use and remote desktop control, cloud subagents on their own VMs, Projects coordinators, event-driven Subscriptions and Automations across GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Slack, Linear, Sentry and PagerDuty, self-hosted worker pools with Kubernetes templates, a native iOS app with Remote Control of a desktop session, REST API plus TypeScript and Python SDKs, and its own git host. Judged from docs and the changelog, not hands-on use.
editorial.feelRationale: Cursor is an Electron-based VS Code fork (a third-party integration note confirms 'Cursor is Electron so you get CDP access'), and independent reports describe real sluggishness rather than isolated gripes: a Cursor forum thread on the app 'becoming ridiculously slow after a few hours' points to extensionHost/ptyHost lag, a Reddit thread calls it 'ridiculously slow and error-prone,' and separate troubleshooting posts cover high GPU usage/UI freezing and slowness on large projects.

tools.name: DeepSeek Harness
tools.tagline: Everything is a plugin.
tools.valueProp: DeepSeek's own open-source agent runtime, not a UI for orchestrating other coding-agent CLIs: models, tools, sessions, sandboxes, scheduling and even the UI are all swappable Cordis plugins. It has no worktree, PR, branch or task-board flow of its own; wrapper products like iPolloWork embed it as one interchangeable engine.

maker.name: DeepSeek AI (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd.)

pricing.notes: Harness itself is free and MIT-licensed. Settings → Models takes a DeepSeek API key, or you add other built-in providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Moonshot/Kimi, Zai/GLM) or a custom OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic-Messages endpoint with your own key; the privacy policy confirms 'custom model services' send your input directly to that model provider and DSH does not process it server-side.

featureNotes.platforms.tui: The CLI reference lists `dsh --profile tui --resume <id>` only as an illustrative example ('assuming the tui profile is installed'); no TUI app, package or docs page confirms a terminal UI ships by default alongside the Web and Desktop profiles.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: No git integration of any kind is documented: the full docs sitemap (guide + reference subsystems) has no git, worktree, branch or PR page. 'Workspace' means a registered project directory grouping sessions, not a git worktree, confirmed by the Workspaces subsystem reference, which stores a canonical directory path and an ordered session list with no git operations.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: The Process Sandbox subsystem ships Linux bwrap/Landlock, macOS Seatbelt and a Windows ACL restricted-token backend for filesystem-effect confinement (read-only / workspace-write / danger-full-access). Its own reference explicitly calls containers, microVMs and remote execution 'sibling implementations of whole capability seams, not providers of ctx.sandbox', i.e. describable as a future plugin, not something that ships.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: The Sessions subsystem reference says a tool result's `meta` payload can carry a presentation extra, citing dsh-tool-fs attaching 'its result-time contextual diff', file edits render an inline diff in the session transcript, not a separate review queue.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Sessions are an append-only event log that supports resume, fork, search and replay of the whole conversation/tool-call history (Trajectory view), which behaves like a checkpoint/rollback of agent state, but nothing describes snapshotting or restoring workspace files themselves.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: A workspace holds an ordered list of multiple sessions (Workspaces subsystem reference), and the Desktop app's quit-confirmation logic explicitly inspects 'active tasks' across 'sessions loaded during this run', 'running agents including subagents and approval waits, queued messages, running or stopping jobs', confirming several sessions can be running in the background at once. No first-party page shows a grid/dashboard for watching them side by side; it is background-capable multi-session chat, not a multiplexer view.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Standard mode's capability list names 'subagents' explicitly, and session events record 'subagent scheduling'; this is one agent delegating bounded work to sub-agents inside its own run, not a user spawning independent top-level agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Two documented mechanisms: session-local scheduled reminders (guide/schedule) and an opt-in overlay that creates new review Sessions from GitHub pull-request webhooks (guide/github-review).
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: No docs page or README section describes a needs-you push/desktop alert; the Desktop-quit dialog surfaces pending work only when you try to quit, which is not confirmed to be a proactive notification channel.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Extends the app itself, not just the agent: per docs (develop/basic, "Your first plugin"), a Harness plugin is a TypeScript module/object/class that registers against a Cordis `ctx` and can add or replace tools, LLM provider adapters, sandboxes, storage, scheduling, and session/event hooks; the homepage states models, tools, skills, sessions, sandboxes, storage, loops, scheduling and "the UI" are all plugins. Verified concretely in the repo: `packages/client/ui-slots` (README) is a typed slot registry that "lets web client plugins define and compose typed UI regions" (sidebars, panels, settings screens) in the dsh web client itself, and `packages/client` ships dozens of `ui-*` packages (ui-sidebar, ui-settings-plugins, ui-plugin-manager, etc.) built on it. Plugins are packaged as npm bundles (`dsh.bundle` manifest) installed into a profile with `dsh plugin add`; distribution is decentralized via the `dsh-plugin` GitHub topic. This is DeepSeek Harness's reference case for the top of the scale: the runtime, including its own UI, is genuinely swappable/extensible via third-party plugins.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: The CLI resolves a per-profile 'telemetry switch' at boot (apps/cli README), a documented on/off setting rather than an always-on collector; separately, the privacy policy says 'custom model services' traffic is not processed on DeepSeek's servers at all.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: `dsh --profile sdk` serves a JSON-RPC stdio API and `dsh --profile acp` serves the Agent Client Protocol for automation clients; DSH is also documented as an MCP *client* (guide/mcp-memory connects third-party memory MCP servers), not confirmed as an MCP *server* itself.

github.description: DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin.

top.title: DeepSeek Harness developer preview

activity.changelogCadence: near-daily (22 GitHub releases in the repo's first six weeks after its August 2026 creation)

editorial.reachRationale: Product-specific signals are enormous for a repo created August 2026: 1.55M npm downloads/month for @deepseek-ai/dsh, a 747-point/314-comment Show-HN-style launch, and a real third-party ecosystem (awesome-plugin lists, independent desktop wrappers like dsh-desktop and deepseek-harness-desktop each with thousands of stars). Discounted the 236k GitHub stars as viral-launch attention, and discounted that DeepSeek is a top-tier AI lab (company-level halo) since Harness is a side runtime, not DeepSeek's main product (the models are). Not rated dominant: it launched in August 2026 as a developer preview tied specifically to running DeepSeek-family models, not a cross-industry default the way Claude Code or Codex are.
editorial.polishRationale: Despite an explicit 'developer preview, THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES' warning, the shipped surface is unusually mature: signed, auto-updating Electron desktop builds for macOS/Windows/Linux with native menus, tray, multi-locale UI, plus an extensively documented plugin/config/session architecture. Held back by the dev-preview status itself and, as of September 2026, zero packaged release assets (installers are not attached to GitHub releases).
editorial.depthRationale: Goes well past a tmux wrapper with a real plugin system, subagent delegation, scheduled and webhook-triggered automations, and full session replay/fork/trajectory review, but has no git worktree/branch/PR flow and no task board.
editorial.feelRationale: Implementation is a local Node/Cordis server with an Electron 'thin wrapper' shell around the same Web UI (apps/desktop README), a standard web-rendered app, not a native/GPU-rendered one, so not rated higher. Reddit and a GitHub Discussions thread report the *agent* getting slower over long sessions from token/cache overhead, which Feel leaves out (that is agent speed, not UI responsiveness); no reports of UI-specific jank, slow session switching or scrollback lag were found, but the product is too new for a confident higher score.

tools.name: Devin
tools.tagline: Devin, the AI software engineer
tools.valueProp: The vendor’s agent is the fleet: Devin sessions run on Cognition’s VMs and are steered from the web, Slack, Teams, a CLI and a kanban board, with coordinator Devins spawning child Devins. No bring-your-own-key path.

maker.name: Cognition AI, Inc.
maker.funding: Series E: $2B+ at a $48B valuation (Sep 2026, Reuters); Series D: $1B+ at $26B post-money led by Lux, General Catalyst and 8VC (May 2026, TechCrunch); $400M at $10.2B (Sep 2025). Acquired Windsurf in July 2025.

pricing.notes: Free $0: light agent quota, limited models, unlimited Tab/inline edits, Devin Review and DeepWiki. Pro $20/mo: daily+weekly quota shared across Devin Cloud, Devin CLI and Devin Desktop, frontier models, up to 10 concurrent sessions, extra usage at API pricing. Max $200/mo: much larger weekly quota, no daily cap. Teams $80/mo minimum: $40/mo per full seat (Pro-equivalent quota + Desktop access) or free flex seats drawing on shared on-demand credits, up to 200 members, unlimited concurrent sessions, admin dashboard, centralized billing. Enterprise: custom, SAML/OIDC SSO, SCIM, IP access lists, audit logs, dedicated single-tenant VPC deployment via AWS PrivateLink, customer-managed keys. On-demand credits roll over; Automations and Devin Review draw from them. Cognition meters and bills all model usage; no BYO keys.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Devin Desktop (the renamed Windsurf IDE) ships Apple Silicon and Intel .dmg/.zip builds; the Devin CLI installs via curl script or `brew install --cask devin-cli`.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Devin Desktop x64 and arm64 installers (user and system); Devin CLI has a Windows installer and PowerShell script and also runs under WSL.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Devin Desktop x64 .tar.gz and .deb, plus apt/rpm instructions; glibc >= 2.28. Devin CLI via the curl installer.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: No iOS app. The web app's Desktop tab works as a remote desktop on iPad and other touch devices (Sept 9, 2026 release notes); the iOS pages in the docs are about Devin building iOS apps on macOS VMs.
featureNotes.platforms.android: No Android app; the docs' Android page covers Devin running an Android emulator inside its own session.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: Devin CLI (Rust) runs the Devin Local harness in your terminal with /model, /handoff to Devin Cloud, /fork, /revert, /share, subagents, --sandbox and a `devin -p` single-turn mode for scripts; `devin worker start` turns a machine into an Outposts worker.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: The CLI is an interactive full-screen terminal chat (model picker, slash commands, /resume for past sessions), not a tmux-style multiplexer of many sessions.
featureNotes.execution.local: Devin Local in Devin Desktop and Devin CLI run on your machine with your files, shell and credentials; optional OS-level sandbox with filesystem and network rules.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Devin Outposts (Pro, Max, Teams; off by default on Dedicated Tenant): install the Devin CLI on your own VM, container, Kubernetes cluster or 'a Mac Mini on your desk', run `devin worker start --outpost=<name>`, and cloud sessions execute their commands and file edits there over an outbound HTTPS connection. Inference and planning stay in Cognition's cloud. Devin Desktop can also connect to agents over SSH from the location selector (v3.10.23).
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Devin Cloud: each session runs on its own isolated VM (Ubuntu, Windows or macOS) with shell, embedded IDE, browser and desktop; sessions sleep and wake. Enterprise can have a customer-dedicated single-tenant VPC hosted by Cognition.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Enterprise deployment docs: Devin's 'brain' is 'a stateless, cloud-based service ... always residing in Cognition's Cloud'. Outposts workers and the open-source devin-outpost-k8s operator are clients of that cloud, not a server you run.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Devin Desktop only, Pro/Max/Teams (Enterprise gated by admin): the ACP page lists 'Claude Agent, Anthropic's coding agent' as an example ACP agent you can plug in. You install the binary yourself and add it to a local or team ACP registry.json; Devin Desktop does not download agents. The separate open-source Devin Handoff plugin lets Claude Code, Codex or Cursor hand a task off to a Devin Cloud session.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Devin Desktop only, via ACP registry config; listed by name as an example ACP agent. Binary must be preinstalled.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Devin Desktop only, via ACP registry config; listed by name as an example ACP agent. Binary must be preinstalled.
featureNotes.agents.opencode: Devin Desktop only, via ACP; the docs include a full sample registry entry for OpenCode (`opencode acp`). Binary must be preinstalled.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Not listed among ACP example agents. Cursor appears only as a source agent for the Devin Handoff plugin (hand a task off to Devin Cloud).
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Devin Desktop only: any agent that implements the Agent Client Protocol (JSON-RPC over stdio) can be added to `~/.windsurf/acp/registry.json` or a team registry, including in-house agents. Session modes and terminal capabilities are not supported. Not available in the web app or Devin Cloud.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Devin is the product: the cloud Devin agent, the Devin Local harness (Desktop and CLI), Cognition's own SWE-2 model, Fusion (frontier lead model plus SWE-2 sidekick) and the Adaptive model router.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Devin Desktop: the agent location picker offers Local, Worktree and Cloud; 'New worktree' creates a fresh git worktree for the session and a Merge action brings changes back. Cloud sessions instead get their own VM.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Every Devin Cloud session runs on its own isolated VM; Outposts sessions run wherever your worker does (docs recommend a dedicated machine or container, with an official `devin-cli` Docker image); Devin Local/CLI has an opt-in OS-level sandbox that enterprises can enforce.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Cloud sessions push their own branches and open PRs, and managed-Devin/workflow examples put each child 'on its own branch', but no automatic branch naming policy is documented. Desktop worktree sessions create a worktree; branch naming is not described.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Session Changes and PR tabs open file diffs in the embedded editor; Devin Review adds AI-organised diffs and findings on every PR (also at devinreview.com); Devin Desktop is a full IDE with a diff view and a Quick Review subagent.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Sessions open PRs on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps, follow review comments and CI results, and can split work into stacked PRs.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Desktop worktree sessions have a Merge button; cloud coordinator sessions 'resolve conflicts' between managed Devins; Devin follows PR review feedback and CI 'to get each PR approved and merged'.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Devin CLI/Devin Local only: /fork branches a session from any step and /revert rolls files and conversation back to a step; Desktop can Duplicate a session. No checkpoint/restore is documented for Devin Cloud sessions.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Pro/Max allow up to 10 concurrent cloud sessions, Teams/Enterprise unlimited. Devin Desktop's Agent Command Center shows local and cloud agents on one Kanban board; the web sidebar groups sessions by PR status or repo.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Agent Command Center is a Kanban board grouped by status (running, waiting for review, waiting for CI, done) with Board and List views; Linear and Jira tickets can be assigned to Devin; Outposts are literally session queues.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Managed Devins: a coordinator session spins up child sessions (each on its own VM), messages them, monitors ACU spend, sleeps or terminates them. Dynamic Workflows: Devin writes and runs a Python script (agent(), pipeline(), parallel()) that orchestrates a team of Devins, resumable by run ID. Triage Devin spawns child sub-devins; Devin Local/CLI has foreground/background subagents.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Automations page: triggers from Slack, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira, Pylon, PagerDuty, cron/one-time schedules and webhooks; actions start a session, message a session, run a persistent Triage Devin or email you. Manageable via Terraform provider and API.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Devin Desktop sends one native OS notification per session when an agent finishes or needs input (`devin.agentNotifications`, covers Devin Local and ACP agents). Devin Cloud: Slack DM notifications on status updates, in-thread questions in Slack/Teams, email on automation runs.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Coordinator sessions send follow-up instructions to child sessions; the Devin MCP server and API let any session or MCP client message running sessions; Desktop Spaces 'share context between agents'.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Voice mode in the web app: start a call from the composer, hold Space to talk, Devin speaks back; moved to a live speech model on Sept 16, 2026. Slack-connected sessions show who was on the call.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Organizations with Member, Admin and DeepWiki Only roles on Teams (up to 200 members); Enterprise adds custom roles, enterprise accounts spanning several organizations, SSO and SCIM.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Sessions are org-visible and multi-participant: the MCP docs note 'other users can still interact with your sessions', chat shows avatars 'once someone else joins', teammates answer Devin's questions, and sessions sync bidirectionally with Slack threads, Slack code channels and Teams chats. As of September 2026, Devin Local in Desktop did not support conversation sharing.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Teams plan with full/flex seats, shared on-demand credits, admin dashboard; Enterprise contracts with centralized enterprise admin controls.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: No; the agent loop always runs in Cognition's cloud even with Outposts or a dedicated VPC.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Enterprise FAQ: 'Devin is a compound AI system and does not currently support third-party LLM API keys.' All plans meter usage through Cognition. The only BYO path is third-party ACP agents in Devin Desktop, where 'billing is directly between you and the third-party agent provider'.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Paid plans can opt out of model training on the Data Controls settings page (Teams: admin only; Enterprise: never trained without written consent). No off switch for product analytics is documented; Devin Desktop reports agent usage and lines-of-code analytics to team admins.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial: Devin Desktop is a VS Code fork with Open VSX editor extensions (docs.devin.ai/desktop/recommended-extensions), which add panels, views and commands to the editor but cannot touch the Devin session and fleet surfaces themselves. The Plugin marketplace (skills, rules, hooks, MCP servers, subagents) and Claude Code plugins in the CLI are agent-side and do not count.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: REST API (v1 sessions with idempotency keys, v2 enterprise, v3 organizations/automations/outposts), an official Devin MCP server for managing sessions, playbooks, knowledge and schedules from any MCP client, a DeepWiki MCP, and a Terraform provider.

top.title: Cognition (Devin AI) to Acquire Windsurf

editorial.reachRationale: A clear major-tier case: a 103k-member product-named Discord ('Devin') and Cognition's well-documented scale (up to a $48B valuation) support a name most practitioners know, though the 633 brew installs/30d for devin-cli is modest and the 183k X followers (@cognition, company-wide) were discounted.
editorial.polishRationale: Judged from docs and release notes rather than hands-on: documentation is very thorough and cadenced (cloud release notes weekly, Desktop builds several times a week, SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SCIM), but the product was mid-rebrand as of September 2026 (Windsurf paths and 'Cascade' still littered Desktop docs and config locations), Devin Local lagged Cascade on memories, workflows and conversation sharing, ACP agents are Desktop-only and need hand-written registry files, and the docs landing page itself warns that 'documentation may be out of date'.
editorial.depthRationale: Nothing else in the set goes this far past a session switcher: a Kanban command center over local and cloud agents, coordinator sessions that spawn and message child Devins, Python dynamic workflows with resumable runs, event-driven automations from nine trigger sources, Devin Review on every PR, stacked PRs, Slack/Teams-synced sessions, voice calls, an MCP server and three API versions, and Outposts for running on your own hardware. Judged from docs and release notes rather than hands-on.
