featureNotes.platforms.ios: Phone access is the responsive web app at app.humanlayer.com; no store app is documented.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Phone access is the responsive web app at app.humanlayer.com; no store app is documented.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: @humanlayer/cli: `humanlayer login`, `daemon launch`, `agents auth codex`, `automation run`.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Remote daemon on a cloud VM, workstation, container or private-network host you provide, authenticated with `humanlayer login` or a short-lived launch token; sessions are driven from the desktop or web app via the HumanLayer API.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Homepage says 'spin up cloud daemons for long-running work', but the docs only describe daemons on hosts you provide; no vendor-provisioned sandbox is documented.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Enterprise tier lists 'On-Prem & Private VPC' with no public documentation; Starter and Pro sync through HumanLayer Cloud.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Default agent; Claude via Anthropic API or AWS Bedrock, inherits ~/.claude/settings.json.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Codex CLI via `humanlayer agents auth codex`, or a custom Responses endpoint (Azure AI Foundry, OpenAI) through CODELAYER_CODEX_* env vars.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Homepage FAQ lists 'Copilot' among supported agents/models; there is no docs page for it and it is unclear whether this means Copilot CLI.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Fold, HumanLayer's own coding agent (github.com/humanlayer/fold), is available behind Settings > Experiments > Use Fold Coding Agent and adds Grok models.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Task worktrees created from .humanlayer/workspace.json (source ref, setup commands, copyGlobs, multi-repo), with Now/Later/Never timing per task; an agent can write the config for you.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: You may run a daemon inside your own container (credential-persistence docs exist), but there is no per-task sandbox.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Worktree target ~/.humanlayer/worktrees/<slug>/{repo} and branch named from the task slug.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Diffs tab and diff viewer with review-scope filtering, sort by latest agent change and J/K navigation of changed files.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Ask the session agent to open a draft PR from the GitHub tab or diff view; `/rpi:describe-pr` opens or updates the PR at the end of a workflow.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: GitHub tab can merge, close, convert to draft, update branch and enable auto-merge (release 0.172.0) but only after enabling 'GitHub PR Tab' under Settings > Experiments; no conflict resolution is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Their 'checkpoints' are human review points between workflow phases and artifacts are versioned; there is no file or agent-state snapshot and rollback.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Tasks list grouping sessions, artifacts and worktrees; release notes mention Kanban shortcuts and research/design/implementation work views.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: The UI shows Claude Code's own subagent tool calls and RPI skills delegate to Claude Code/Codex sub-agents, but no HumanLayer-level agent-spawns-agent control is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: `humanlayer automation run` starts an ephemeral daemon inside a CI job, cron machine or script with a personal access token; GitHub Actions example with schedule trigger documented. Release 0.166.0 called the GitHub Actions path experimental.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Slack automations post on artifact events (design discussion, PRD, TDD, outline, comment created) and the app routes in-app notifications through workspace tabs; no documented alert for an agent waiting on input.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Sessions in a task share synced artifacts and later agents read reviewer comments, but there is no direct session-to-session messaging.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Live multiplayer response drafts with shared text, named cursors and presence (0.175.0); teammates can send messages to a running session from the web app; tasks are shared at task level.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Per-user Pro pricing, native user administration, organization admins, Enterprise SSO/SAML and audit logs.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Homepage FAQ: 'Not yet, but we'll be open-sourcing some of the building blocks'. The humanlayer/humanlayer repo is Apache-2.0 but its README says the code is deprecated; only the RPI skills are open source.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Only via the Enterprise on-prem/private VPC offer; every other tier routes sessions and sync through the HumanLayer API.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Claude, Codex and other subscriptions or API keys; 'no separate HumanLayer per-token bill'.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Privacy policy documents PostHog analytics, feature flags and session replay; only web session replay has a documented off switch (Cookie Settings). No app-level telemetry opt-out is documented.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Agent-side only, and not shipped as of September 2026: the FAQ says HumanLayer is 'actively working on ways for you to bring your own skills and workflows.' As of September 2026, the only 'skills' were HumanLayer's own built-in RPI skills surfaced via slash-command autocomplete; there is no mechanism, documented or otherwise, for third-party code to change HumanLayer's own interface or core. See https://docs.humanlayer.com FAQ.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Personal access tokens and the CLI's `automation run` drive the HumanLayer API from scripts, but there is no public API reference or MCP server.

github.description: The best way to get AI coding agents to solve hard problems in complex codebases.

top.title: Launch HN: Human Layer (YC F24) – Human-in-the-Loop API for AI Systems

editorial.reachRationale: As of September 2026 the original GitHub repo was a deprecated issue tracker (0 commits in 90 days) for what has since become a closed-source, renamed product; npm downloads for @humanlayer/cli (~24.7k/month) and a 2,726-member Discord showed it was alive, but the top HN result (354 points) is for the earlier, different human-in-the-loop SDK product, and X activity had been quiet since July 2026, so it read as still finding its audience.
editorial.polishRationale: Release notes ship every one to three days with structured highlights, docs follow a tutorial/guide/explanation/reference split, SOC 2 Type II, a Homebrew cask and keybinding settings, but the desktop app is Apple-silicon-only, the browser app lacks workspace management and a terminal, several headline features sit behind Settings > Experiments (GitHub PR tab, Fold agent, Projects V2), the docs carried CODELAYER_* env vars and a legacy Riptide.app path as of September 2026, pricing exists only as a homepage section, and the flagship GitHub repo is a deprecated shell. Judged from docs and release notes, not hands-on.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes far past a session switcher. Tasks bundle sessions, worktrees and versioned artifacts; a phased workflow (Oneshot, RPI, PRD-Oriented, Freeform) with human review gates; inline comments on design docs that later sessions read; GitHub/Linear/Jira issue import and Slack event automations; a GitHub tab that shows checks, hands failing CI to the agent and merges PRs; remote daemons; an ephemeral-daemon CLI for CI runs; Advanced Metrics for token spend; live co-authored prompts. Judged from docs and release notes, not hands-on.
editorial.feelRationale: The desktop app is Tauri-based (release notes reference 'Tauri builds' and a fixed bug where Tauri's WebKit localStorage WAL could grow to multiple gigabytes) with a small Rust footprint alongside TS/Go per gh api languages; release notes repeatedly target UI speed specifically - 'faster stream initialization', large sessions 'open faster', and task launches made 'instant' - evidencing known rough edges that were actively chased down and fixed.

tools.name: Intent
tools.tagline: Large-scale agent coordination for developers.
tools.valueProp: A living spec that both humans and agents keep reading from and writing to for the life of a task, so it stays the plan and the audit trail instead of a one-time brief that goes stale. Built-in browser verification attaches screenshots and console output straight into that spec as evidence, and a remote workspace's live browser session can be handed off between your own devices mid-task.

maker.name: Augment Code
maker.funding: $252M total raised, incl. $227M Series B (Apr 2024) at a $977M post-money valuation; Sutter Hill Ventures, Index Ventures, Innovation Endeavors, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Meritech Capital.

pricing.notes: Intent itself is a free download with no account or paid tier of its own (docs: "Intent is a free desktop app"). It needs at least one configured agent provider: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi run on your own subscriptions or keys, unmetered by Intent. Its recommended/built-in provider, Augment's own Auggie, instead draws down Augment's own paid usage credits (Standard $20/mo, Business $100/mo, Enterprise custom, per augmentcode.com/pricing) "at the same rate as our Auggie CLI" per the launch post, so cost depends entirely on which provider you pick.

featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial: no skills/plugin marketplace, but `intentd` (the local-first Rust daemon that owns Intent's whole domain model, workspaces, notes, tasks, agents, git, terminals, files, events) exposes a documented JSON-RPC 2.0 API over Unix-domain-socket and WSS/TLS transports with roughly 140 methods across many namespaces, explicitly designed so 'a desktop UI, a CLI, or an' external client can drive the same state, a control protocol that can operate Intent from outside, matching the config/scripting-protocol bar for partial. Documented in packages/intentd/README.md in github.com/intent-hq/intent; no evidence of a way to add new panels/commands to Intent's own UI.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Download link is labelled "Windows (Alpha)" on the docs install page.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Download link is labelled "Linux (Alpha)" on the docs install page.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: intentd ships a CLI (serve/call/status/stop/doctor/settings/import/mcp-bridge), but it manages the daemon/updates rather than steering agents; the end-user surface is the desktop app.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: The Changes panel shows PR status, CI checks and merge-queue state, but no first-party documentation describes automated conflict resolution.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: A work-in-progress snapshot is captured specifically when transferring a workspace between devices; no general per-turn checkpoint/rollback of agent edits is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: The global sidebar groups workspaces by status (In Progress, Needs Attention, PR Open, Completed) and Task Notes track sub-work inside a spec, but there is no dedicated kanban/queue board feeding agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Hooks and PR monitors wake an agent on a meaningful repo event (new CI result, PR comment) instead of polling, which is event-triggered but not a user-scheduled/cron automation system.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Coordinator, Implementor and Verifier agents exchange structured task delegation and reports within a workspace; there is no documented free-form messaging between arbitrary agent sessions.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: intentd (the daemon) is explicitly designed to run headless on a machine you own, but multi-device remote pairing is described as going through "a bundled secure tunnel" (via Tailscale's tailcat) whose infrastructure dependency is not documented.

github.description: Monorepo for the Intent platform — tracks intentd, cloudlands-fe, and ios as submodules; docs, CI, and release orchestration

top.title: Intent – The developer workspace for agent orchestration – Augment Code

editorial.reachRationale: Intent launched into public beta 2026-02-10 (Augment's own X post); the company account is discounted since Intent is one of several Augment products. Product-specific signals were small as of September 2026: 213 GitHub stars on the umbrella repo, only 4 Hacker News stories with a 5-point top submission, and community discussion limited to Augment's own r/AugmentCodeAI subreddit, a Medium writeup and a Product Hunt listing, real early usage rather than a known quantity.
editorial.polishRationale: Near-daily shipped releases with detailed notes, a searchable/rebindable keyboard-shortcut system, math rendering, and dedicated settings for animation and window translucency show real production investment, but it was labelled public beta as of September 2026, with Windows/Linux marked Alpha at that point, and the changelog repeatedly adds workarounds for the app itself (a long-task watchdog, renderer-hang capture and recovery) rather than only new features.
editorial.depthRationale: A Coordinator delegates to Implementor and Verifier specialists against a living spec that both sides edit; in-app git (worktrees, branch-per-task, diff review, PR creation and monitoring), a built-in browser that captures before/after screenshots as verification evidence, MCP support, and multi-device workspace transfer to/from a self-hostable remote daemon (intentd) go well past a session switcher.
editorial.feelRationale: Electron + SvelteKit frontend (cloudlands-fe repo) talking to a local Rust daemon, not a native UI. The maker's own changelog repeatedly ships fixes for stalls and hangs ("long-task watchdog and renderer hang capture," "recovery when things stall," reduced "renderer churn"), and independent reports agree: a Reddit thread titled "Why is Intent so slow?" and a Medium review ("Intent's interface is smooth, but long threads introduce noticeable lag").

tools.name: iPolloWork
tools.tagline: Next-gen agentic AI work assistant.
tools.valueProp: Treats code as one of several editable outputs: the same session can produce code, decks, videos, web pages and design files that stay editable after generation. Wraps OpenCode by default, DeepSeek Harness as a peer, and Codex only through MCP, under a source-available licence.

pricing.notes: Free for individual personal use and internal use by fewer than three total users under the 'iPolloWork Source Available License 1.0'; any use by three+ users, resale, SaaS or white-label distribution requires prior written authorization (contact sales). The public pricing.html page is unfinished Webflow template boilerplate (placeholder 'Quadra' copy, no real tiers or numbers).

featureNotes.platforms.tui: ipollowork-orchestrator CLI ships a default TUI status/pairing view (disable with --no-tui); it is an operator console for the host process, not a full terminal work surface like a tmux-style multiplexer.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Codex is reached only through the ipollowork-ui-mcp control surface, an MCP integration rather than a native engine adapter, the README explicitly says this 'is not claiming a native Codex engine adapter'.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: DeepSeek Harness subagents can be delegated bounded work from a session, but this is DSH's own subagent model surfaced through iPolloWork, not agents spawning/steering other agents natively inside the product.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Docs organize work by 'session' (task/owner/repo/permission boundary), not a kanban board or queue; no board/queue UI is described anywhere in the docs, FAQ or README.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Enterprise page offers team workspaces, RBAC and 'Contact Sales', but no public plan/pricing tiers exist (the pricing.html page is unfinished placeholder content).
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Extends iPolloWork's own UI: a plugin package (`ipollowork.plugin.json`, schemaVersion 2) can ship a `contributions` array with types `workspace-app` (adds a new app/panel into the workspace surface) and `settings-page` (adds a page into Settings), backed by MCP-Apps `ui://` HTML resources, the working `workspace-canvas` example plugin does exactly this. This is a real, documented package format (source.format `ipollowork-extension-manifest`) with install/validate/update/rollback/uninstall lifecycle, distinct from and beyond the agent-side Skill/Hook/MCP bundles that also ship in the same package. Documented in docs/plugin-packages.md and examples/plugin-packages/workspace-canvas in github.com/Devin-AXIS/iPolloWork.

github.description: Enterprise-grade, local-first Agent Workbench for people and agent teams. A unified multi-engine workspace for Codex Harness, DeepSeek Harness, and OpenCode, with unified plugins and Skills, multi-agent projects and tasks, and editable code, documents, presentations, design, and video.

activity.changelogCadence: near-daily (37 releases in the trailing 90 days)

editorial.reachRationale: Product-specific signals are early-stage: no Discord, zero Hacker News stories for the product, and no registry download numbers (npm packages return null). The product's own X account (8.3K followers) and a GitHub Trendshift badge show real attention, but stars (6.7K, discounted) and a repo created in August 2025 aren't enough to call it an established community as of September 2026.
editorial.polishRationale: Docs and README read as professionally maintained with a coherent architecture (Electron shell, local server, sidecar boundary, self-hosted topology). Polish is pulled down by the public marketing site: the pricing page is literally unfinished Webflow template placeholder copy ('Quadra', 'No items found') sitting next to otherwise polished docs.
editorial.depthRationale: It ships beyond code into design/video/PPT surfaces with a plugin/Skills system and enterprise deployment docs.
editorial.feelRationale: Standard Electron desktop shell with a React/Vite frontend per the README's architecture section; no first-party performance claims (native/GPU-rendered, etc.) and no user reports of jank or speed were found in a search for 'iPolloWork slow OR fast OR laggy'.

tools.name: Jean
tools.tagline: A dev environment for AI agents.
tools.valueProp: Jean puts local and self-hosted remote projects in one desktop sidebar, with each agent task in a managed worktree. Its project canvas ties sessions to GitHub, Linear, Sentry, review, and merge workflows.

pricing.notes: Jean is free and open source with no paid tiers; users bring subscriptions or API access for supported coding agents.

featureNotes.platforms.windows: Desktop builds exist, but the README says Windows is not fully tested.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Desktop builds exist, but the README says Linux is community tested; the headless server is supported on Linux amd64/arm64.
featureNotes.platforms.ios: Phone access uses the browser UI; no native iOS app is documented.
featureNotes.platforms.android: Phone access uses the browser UI; no native Android app is documented.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: jean-server launches a server; docs do not describe a CLI for starting or steering agents.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Yes: README and Projects, Worktrees, Sessions docs say Jean creates, archives, restores and deletes worktrees, with branch and path tracked per task.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: The published Docker image packages jean-server; docs do not describe containers per agent task.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: The project canvas has Issues, PRs, and Mr. Robot filters feeding worktrees, but no general Kanban board is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Jean displays reports from subagents spawned by a backend; docs do not describe Jean itself spawning or steering them.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Mr. Robot beta polls GitHub issues and creates worktrees/plans; optional auto-execution is limited to this issue sweep.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Desktop and Web Access can show the same sessions through a token-protected server; separate user accounts or permissions are not documented.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: No Jean app extension loader is documented. Opinionated Plugins installs RTK and Caveman for the CLI agents, while Magic Prompts only edits built-in workflow templates and model choices; see /docs/manage/opinionated-plugins and /docs/manage/magic-prompts.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Repository implements a Jean MCP server under jean-core/src/chat/jean_mcp.rs and jean-core/src/jean_mcp_core.rs; Web Access also exposes authenticated HTTP endpoints.

github.description: A dev environment for AI agents.

top.title: Show HN: Supervisor IDE – Command center for coding agents in complex projects

activity.changelogCadence: 19 releases in 90 days, including 8 from September 21–29, 2026

editorial.reachRationale: The last five release assets have 21,005 downloads and the repo has 54 contributors, evidence of early adoption. I discounted 1,306 stars as attention, and the linked Discord belongs to coolLabs rather than Jean specifically.
editorial.polishRationale: Jean has a stable 1.0.7 release, documented desktop and server installs, recovery, and mobile browser layouts; Windows and Linux desktop builds needed testing as of October 2026, and releases around that time included many fixes.
editorial.depthRationale: Managed worktrees, issue sweeps, GitHub/Linear/Sentry intake, in-app review and merge, checkpoints, and local plus remote server aggregation go well beyond a terminal wrapper.
editorial.feelRationale: Jean's README states its stack as Tauri v2, Rust, React 19 and xterm.js, and GitHub confirms a TypeScript/Rust split, a native Tauri shell rather than Electron; no jank was reported, so it scores above the plain-Electron baseline.

tools.name: JetBrains Air
tools.tagline: JetBrains Air is one system for building software with agents.
tools.valueProp: The only tool here embedded in a full IDE: JetBrains's own code intelligence (symbol resolution, navigation, refactors) feeds whichever agent you pick, and each task runs in one of four selectable environments, local workspace, a managed git worktree, a Docker container, or JetBrains's cloud, chosen per task, not per app. A companion governance product tracks policy, access and spend across every agent and vendor an org uses, not only JetBrains's own.

maker.name: JetBrains s.r.o.
maker.funding: Independent, privately held software company founded 2000, profitable on products like IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm; no external venture funding is disclosed for Air specifically.

pricing.notes: AI Free: 3 AI credits/30 days, for IDE completion plus occasional agent use. AI Pro: $100/yr (~$8.33/mo equivalent), 10 credits/30 days, anytime top-ups. AI Ultimate: $300/yr, 35 credits/30 days. AI Enterprise: $720/yr, maximum credits plus SSO/SCIM, audit logs and on-premises/hybrid deployment options (contact sales). 1 AI credit = USD 1.00, credits valid 12 months. Air also runs local tasks on a BYOK Claude/OpenAI/Gemini subscription or API key with no JetBrains AI subscription required; cloud tasks, automations and org governance always draw JetBrains AI credits, even when a BYOK/ACP agent is selected.

featureNotes.platforms.cli: Air Gateway (formerly JetBrains Central CLI) is a separate early-access CLI that unifies account/billing access for terminal agents like Claude Code and Codex; it is a credential and quota gateway, not the Air task/session UI itself.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Named on the homepage and connected via the ACP registry (an `acp.json` entry, e.g. `Copilot --acp`), not one of the four first-class provider accounts (Claude Agent, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Junie) listed in Supported agents.
featureNotes.agents.opencode: Named in the July 2026 "What's new" post as a newly supported ACP agent; connected via `acp.json`, not a first-class provider account.
featureNotes.agents.pi: Named in the July 2026 "What's new" post as a newly supported ACP agent; connected via `acp.json`, not a first-class provider account.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Documented one-click "Merge" of a finished cloud task's branch into your working branch (from the IntelliJ AI Assistant cloud-task flow); no documented conflict-resolution assistance beyond that.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: The desktop app lists tasks and automations per project in Tasks/Automations panels (a queue view), but no drag-and-drop kanban board is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Automation runs email the owner and can POST to a webhook on failure; no documented push/desktop alert for an interactive task that is blocked waiting on your input.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Air Teams gives a team shared access to the same cloud environment/project ("Run shared projects... invite others and manage access from one place"); not confirmed as two people concurrently steering the identical live agent session.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial: the only documented extension point for Air itself is config-level agent registration, adding an entry to `acp.json` (an `agent_servers` block naming the launch command) to plug in a new ACP-compatible agent, as shown in the Goose/Copilot example. No docs describe adding new panels, views, commands or providers via code; this is distinct from IntelliJ's general-purpose platform plugin SDK, which extends the IDE, not Air specifically. Documented at https://www.jetbrains.com/help/air/select-agents-and-models.html.

editorial.reachRationale: Established rather than major: the standalone plugin has modest concrete numbers for a product that was alpha as of September 2026 (6,795 Marketplace downloads/14 ratings, 49 Homebrew-cask installs/30d, 3,151 X followers, a 74-point/114-comment HN launch thread), so those alone would read as emerging. Weighed up because Air ships from JetBrains, a 26-year incumbent IDE vendor bundling it directly into IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm and the rest of its IntelliJ-platform line (already used by a large share of professional developers), with a public preview running since March 2026 and steady monthly feature releases since. JetBrains's company-wide follower counts and IDE user base were not used directly, per the rule against crediting vendor-wide reach to one product.
editorial.polishRationale: Consistent, well-documented UI (Chat, Files, Changes, History, Search, Terminal tools) across a genuinely multi-surface product, but several core pieces were labelled EAP or alpha as of September 2026 (cloud tasks, automations, the IDE plugin itself was 'Air Alpha') and a Marketplace reviewer reported the advertised Claude Code ACP flow did not work in chat sessions at that time.
editorial.depthRationale: Four distinct run environments (local, managed worktree, Docker container, cloud) selectable per task, before/after history snapshots with rollback, in-app diff review and PR creation, scheduled/event-triggered automations, and an org-wide governance layer for access, cost and audit across every connected vendor, well beyond a tmux wrapper, though there is no task board, subagents or cross-agent messaging documented.
editorial.feelRationale: Built on the JVM-based IntelliJ platform (a standalone Air.app plus an IntelliJ-IDE plugin), not a lightweight native or GPU-rendered shell. JetBrains's own YouTrack tracker has first-party-acknowledged reports of sluggishness: AIR-3185 'The AI agent is very slow' and AIR-3625 'AIR is slow to start and behave (3+ GB of fsdaemon in RAM) on IJ monorepo'; a targeted search surfaced no counterbalancing 'fast/instant' claims from JetBrains or users.

tools.name: Jules
tools.tagline: An Autonomous Coding Agent
tools.valueProp: Google runs each GitHub task in a separate cloud VM and lets one account launch up to 60 at once. Jules Tools adds a terminal dashboard and the REST API exposes session control.

pricing.notes: Free: 15 tasks/day and 3 concurrent. Google AI Pro: 100/day and 15 concurrent. Google AI Ultra: 300/day and 60 concurrent; paid upgrades required individual Google Accounts as of September 2026.

featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Jules clones each task into a separate cloud VM and publishes a branch; it does not create or manage local Git worktrees.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Config/control only: the documented REST API and Jules Tools CLI can create, list, message, approve and inspect Jules sessions from outside, but cannot load third-party code into its dashboard, commands or runtime. See Jules API Reference and Jules Tools Reference; agent-side MCP service integrations do not count.

top.title: Jules, our asynchronous coding agent

activity.changelogCadence: roughly biweekly: 5 dated entries from Jan 26 to Mar 9, 2026

editorial.reachRationale: Jules-specific evidence includes more than 140k public commits by its August 2025 GA announcement, 8,243 monthly Jules Tools downloads, 32,140 followers on @julesagent and a 339-point HN story. These show broad recognition; Google-wide audience numbers were not counted.
editorial.polishRationale: A documented web dashboard, terminal dashboard, guided plan and diff review, notifications and paid tiers, with a stale FAQ that called the product beta as of September 2026.
editorial.depthRationale: Separate VMs, up to 60 concurrent tasks, scheduled tasks, GitHub issue/PR flows, CI auto-fixing and a session API go well beyond a simple session list, while team administration and merge assistance are not documented.
editorial.feelRationale: The multiplexer uses a browser dashboard and a terminal dashboard; the docs describe no low-latency rendering architecture or session-switching measurements, and the environment snapshot claim concerns agent startup rather than interface speed. A typical web-interface middle score is the evidence-supported middle.

tools.name: Kilo Code
tools.tagline: One open agent for every developer workflow
tools.valueProp: Agent Manager is a panel inside the Kilo extension, not a separate app: parallel worktree sessions all run Kilo’s own agent loop against any of 500-plus models, with an in-panel GitHub PR review-and-merge flow and a shared message board between sessions. It orchestrates itself, not other vendors’ CLIs.

maker.name: Kilo Code
maker.funding: $8M seed (announced 2025-12-10), led by Cota Capital with participation from Breakers, General Catalyst, Quiet Capital and Tokyo Black. Founder Scott Breitenother (previously founded Brooklyn Data).

pricing.notes: Platform plan is free for individuals (open source VS Code, JetBrains and CLI extensions); Teams $15/user/month adds usage analytics, shared BYOK, centralized billing; Enterprise is custom (SSO/OIDC/SCIM, audit logs, SLA), with a 14-day Enterprise trial for everyone. AI inference is priced separately from the platform: Auto Free/BYOK/local models at $0, pay-as-you-go Kilo Gateway at exact provider rates (500+ models, no markup), or Kilo Pass subscriptions from $19/mo for bonus credits. Cloud compute is billed per second on top: Cloud Agent (Docker) $0.60/hr, Code Review $0.33/hr; Gas Town (a partner-hosted third-party agent orchestrator by Steve Yegge) $1.20/hr.

featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Kilo does not wrap third-party CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) as harnesses; its CLI is itself a fork of OpenCode and its Agent Manager sessions all run Kilo's own agent loop against whichever LLM you configure (BYOK, Kilo Gateway, or local models). There is no documented adapter for driving an arbitrary external agent binary.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Docker-based isolation exists for the separate Cloud Agent product ($0.60/hr, app.kilo.ai/cloud), not for the primary local Agent Manager, which isolates sessions with git worktrees on the host filesystem instead.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Agent Manager's PR panel manages, reviews and merges an existing pull request (via `gh`) and can import one by URL, and a 'Push Pull Request Fixes' toggle pushes fix commits, but the docs read do not describe a one-click 'create PR' action distinct from the agent itself running `gh pr create` in its terminal.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: 'Sections' let you group worktrees into collapsible, color-coded folders in the sidebar for organization, and the `agent_manager` tool can batch-create multiple named tasks/worktrees at once, but there is no kanban board or queue that feeds agents work over time.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Scheduled triggers (cron expressions, up to 5 per instance) exist for KiloClaw and Cloud Agent sessions, and `kilo run --auto` supports unattended CI/CD runs; the local Agent Manager panel itself has no scheduling UI.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: The CLI has a documented `attention` setting for desktop/sound notifications when waiting on input; an open GitHub issue (#7529, 'Unified Notification System for Agent Manager and VS Code Extension') states there is 'no consistent notification' when an Agent Manager session needs input, indicating the VS Code panel's own notifications were not unified as of September 2026.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Sessions can be shared via a read-only link (with an option to fork into your own copy) and resumed across devices, but this is asynchronous sharing, not two people live-steering the same running session together.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: No self-hostable Kilo Gateway/backend was found in the bounded docs read; BYOK and local models avoid a vendor model-proxy, but account, sync and Cloud Agent features depend on Kilo's own servers.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Extends Kilo itself: TypeScript/JS plugins (typed via `@kilocode/plugin`) loaded from a config `plugin` array, a `plugin/` directory, `kilo plugin install`, or the Marketplace, can add custom tools, intercept tool calls, register auth/model providers, register `experimental_workspace` adaptors (custom workspace targets), mutate chat params/headers, and customize compaction; npm plugins can also ship a separate TUI entry (`exports["./tui"]`) or theme package (`oc-themes`). Published via the Kilo Marketplace (`PLUGIN.yaml` under kilo-marketplace). Documented in full at https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/extending/plugins.

github.description: Kilo is the all-in-one agentic engineering platform. Build, ship, and iterate faster with the most popular open source coding agent.

top.title: Stop selling “unlimited”, when you mean “until we change our minds”

editorial.reachRationale: Reach reflects the parent extension's real user base: 27,421 GitHub stars, 1,245 contributors and an unusually high commit velocity (2,274 commits/30d), a 15,318-member product Discord, a 29,242-follower product X account, and an npm CLI package with over 119k monthly downloads together show a real, active community past the early-adopter stage. Discounted the homepage's self-reported '5M+ Kilo Coders' and '10T+ tokens processed every month' as unverified marketing superlatives, and kept this at established rather than major because Kilo competes directly with several similarly-sized open-source VS Code/JetBrains AI agent extensions (Cline, Roo Code, Continue) in the same niche rather than standing out as a name most practitioners outside that niche would know.
editorial.polishRationale: Judged from docs, not hands-on: documentation is unusually thorough down to badge-color priority tables and keyboard-shortcut references, and the release cadence is very fast (98 releases/90d with detailed changesets), but an open GitHub issue describes the Agent Manager's own notification system as inconsistent.
editorial.depthRationale: Parallel worktree-isolated sessions with per-worktree setup/run scripts and env-file copying, an in-panel GitHub PR review/merge flow with inline comments and conflict-aware merge controls, checkpoints with restore, task subagents plus a Kilo Swarm message board for cross-agent coordination, cron-based scheduled triggers (KiloClaw/Cloud Agent), a separate Cloud Agent and Code Review product, and a marketplace for agents/skills/MCP servers/plugins make this one of the broadest feature sets in this dataset. Judged from docs, not hands-on.
editorial.feelRationale: A VS Code/JetBrains extension (webview-based panel, not a native or GPU-rendered app), so the architecture caps it at 'fine' by default. A targeted search found mixed signals: a GitHub issue reporting 'severe performance degradation, extremely slow API calls' and a Reddit thread asking 'why is Kilo Code so slow' (largely attributed to upstream model/API latency rather than the UI itself), against a third-party comparison calling it 'fast and lightweight' versus Cursor. No consistent, UI-specific jank complaints distinct from model latency were found, so scored as a typical, unremarkable extension rather than notably slow or fast.

tools.name: Maestro
tools.tagline: Run AI coding agents autonomously for days.
tools.valueProp: An Electron cockpit for a fleet of CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot CLI), each in its own worktree. Auto Run drives markdown playbooks for hours unattended, Cue chains agents on events, and a moderator agent runs group chats between them. Free, AGPL, real plugin system, phone check-in.

pricing.notes: Free and open source (AGPL-3.0); no Maestro account, license check, or paid tier. Users bring their own Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode/Copilot CLI subscriptions; Maestro is a pass-through orchestrator.

featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Right-click any agent -> 'Create worktree sub-agent' spins up a git worktree on its own branch and directory; Auto Run can dispatch straight into a new worktree, and `maestro-cli auto-run --worktree --branch <name>` does the same headlessly (docs.runmaestro.ai/git-worktrees). Confirmed as the isolation mechanism, not just tolerated.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Extends Maestro itself via a genuine tiered plugin system, not a skills folder: plugins are folders under `<userData>/plugins/` with a signed `plugin.json` manifest. Tier 0 contributes data only (themes, prompts, settings, command macros, cue triggers); tier 1 runs sandboxed code in its own Electron `utilityProcess` behind a default-deny `PermissionBroker`; tier 2 adds sandboxed UI panels/modals/commands via a locked-down iframe (subject to a `PROTECTED_UI_SURFACES` denylist). Built/signed via `maestro plugin init/validate/sign/pack` and distributed as `.tgz` packages through Settings -> Plugins. Documented in CLAUDE-PLUGINS.md and docs/agent-guides/PLUGIN-DEVELOPMENT.md in github.com/RunMaestro/Maestro, distinct from the separate markdown-only 'Playbook Exchange'.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Git integration includes an in-app diff viewer, commit log and branch display alongside worktree actions (docs.runmaestro.ai/git-worktrees, README 'Git Integration').
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Dedicated 'Create Pull Request' flow (right-click worktree, branch-pill menu, or Cmd+K) opens a modal with source/target branch and an auto-generated title/description, using an installed+authenticated `gh` CLI; works for any agent on a branch, not just worktrees (docs.runmaestro.ai/git-worktrees).
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Group Chat lets you appoint one agent as moderator, which routes the question to other agents, pushes back on thin answers, and synthesizes a result across as many rounds as needed (docs.runmaestro.ai/agent-collaboration); 'Symphony' separately runs a scripted multi-agent pipeline that opens its own PR.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Cross-Agent Mentions: typing `@another-agent` in any chat forwards a slice of the transcript, runs it as a background process on that agent's own project/context, and streams the reply back inline with attribution; works across providers and across local/SSH-remote agents (docs.runmaestro.ai/agent-collaboration).
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: README lists 'Speakable Notifications - Audio alerts with text-to-speech announcements when agents complete tasks': one-way TTS output, not two-way dictation/voice control, so marked partial rather than true.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Desktop completion alerts plus text-to-speech 'Speakable Notifications'; the RC-only 'Pianola' Encore feature is a manager agent that watches selected agents for stalled questions and escalates unanswered ones to you.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: 'SSH Remote Execution' (movement #12, docs.runmaestro.ai/ssh-remote-execution) orchestrates agents on remote hosts/build machines/GPU boxes over SSH from the same local fleet view; playbooks can import directly to the remote host.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Built-in local web server (docs.runmaestro.ai/remote-control) serves the mobile-optimized UI over LAN via QR code, or over the internet through a self-run Cloudflare Tunnel; token-authenticated, off by default, no Maestro-run service involved.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: runmaestro.ai/privacy: no telemetry by default beyond opt-in crash reports and an 'Encore' usage-stats feature; a documented settings table turns off every network call Maestro makes on its own (updates, crash reports, usage stats, leaderboard, web interface, WakaTime), leaving it fully offline apart from your chosen AI provider.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Competitive battle-cards (runmaestro.ai/battle-cards, first-party self-comparison) explicitly mark 'Any-CLI-agent drop-in' as not shipped; supported agents are a fixed, named list (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot CLI beta; Gemini CLI listed only as planned).
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Battle-cards explicitly mark 'Container isolation per agent' and 'Cloud sandboxes' as not shipped, unlike Conductor/Amp/Cursor/Devin/Sculptor; isolation is worktrees on your own machine, not containers.

github.description: Agent Orchestration Command Center

top.title: Maestro – Run AI coding agents autonomously for days

editorial.reachRationale: Real, product-specific usage past hobby scale: 3,358 stars, 56 contributors, 682 commits/90d and weekly releases (created 2025-11-23, already on v0.17.5), plus a public leaderboard of named users who have logged 40-90+ days of cumulative autonomous runtime and a genuinely positive r/ClaudeAI reception. Discounted stars as attention rather than use, and discounted its modest X following (222) and small HN showing (7 points) which suggest it's known within the coding-agent niche rather than broadly.
editorial.polishRationale: Signed installers on all three desktop OSes, a full separate docs site, a public self-authored competitive comparison, heavy commit velocity (682/90d) with weekly releases, and a gamified public leaderboard show real production discipline; short of the top tier because several headline 'Encore' features (Concerto, Coworking, Groups+, Pianola) are release-candidate-only or opt-in, Gemini CLI support remained 'planned' rather than shipped as of September 2026.
editorial.depthRationale: Goes well past a session switcher: event-driven Maestro Cue automations chained from file changes, timers, GitHub activity or another agent finishing; a scripted Symphony pipeline that opens its own draft PRs; two distinct cross-agent collaboration modes (inline @mentions and a moderated multi-round Group Chat); SSH remote execution onto other machines; a full headless CLI for cron/CI; a tiered, signed, sandboxed third-party plugin system; and usage-dashboard/document-graph analytics on top of worktrees, in-app diffs and PR creation.
editorial.feelRationale: Electron app (TypeScript is 99% of the repo's languages per GitHub, and the plugin sandbox is built on Electron's `utilityProcess`), not a native/GPU-rendered stack. A targeted search turned up no user reports of lag or jank, and no maker performance claims either, so it lands as a typical, unremarkable Electron app rather than notably fast or notably slow.

tools.name: Mission Control
tools.tagline: Run every AI agent from one control plane.
tools.valueProp: A protocol-first dispatcher, not an editor: agents self-register over a REST heartbeat API and claim tasks from a queue, so any framework or script can take part without a bundled harness. Ships its own review gate, RBAC and audit trails, with no worktrees, diff review or PR flow of its own.

pricing.notes: Open source, MIT-licensed, self-hosted for free; homepage explicitly notes 'Self-host free. No account. No forced product telemetry.' No paid tier, plan or hosted offering for Mission Control itself. The maintainer (nyk) separately sells a fixed-scope 'Agent OS Setup' consulting package ($5K-$12K, 2-4 weeks) covering the wider agent operating stack, of which Mission Control is one component, that is consulting, not a Mission Control pricing tier.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: No native or Electron app; it is a self-hosted Next.js web app reached through a browser. The deployment guide lists macOS only as a build/host prerequisite (Xcode CLT for compiling better-sqlite3), not as a shipped client.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Same as macOS: no client app, only a browser UI and CLI. install.ps1 exists for running the server on Windows, not a packaged app.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Same: server can run on Linux (apt build deps documented, Docker image compiles for linux/x64), but there is no dedicated Linux client, only the web UI.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: CHANGELOG (#766) documents opt-in sandbox flags for host CLI dispatch: an `allowedTools` allowlist, a clamped `--max-budget-usd`, and a workspace-scoped `cwd` escape-protected via `MC_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, lightweight guardrails, not per-task Docker/microVM isolation. Mission Control itself can also run inside Docker (hardened Compose overlay), but that isolates the control plane, not individual agent tasks.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: No pull-request creation was found. The Automate capability list on the homepage advertises 'Bidirectional GitHub Issues sync', which is issue sync, not PR creation.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Homepage Run-layer copy for the task board: 'Six-stage flow with priorities, comments, projects, and sub-agent spawning'; no dedicated docs page elaborates on the mechanism.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Agents and humans can @mention each other on tasks/comments (task-board mention menu, changelog: 'Notification system with @mentions'), and heartbeat responses surface those mentions as work items, but this is asynchronous task-comment messaging, not a live agent-to-agent chat channel.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: RBAC roles (viewer/operator/admin) and a shared task board exist, and the memory/session panels are viewable by any authorized user, but no page describes two people watching or steering the same live agent session simultaneously.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: No billing surface of any kind; Mission Control is free, self-hosted software with no accounts tier or org billing.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Homepage: 'Self-host free. No account. No forced product telemetry.' No analytics/telemetry SDK (e.g. PostHog, Segment) appears in package.json dependencies, and .env.example has no telemetry toggle, read as telemetry being genuinely absent/off by default rather than opt-out of something shipped.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial: not a code-plugin system, but Mission Control ships a first-party control surface for driving itself from outside, `scripts/mc-cli.cjs` plus a REST API (with an `openapi.json`) that can create/control agents, tasks, cron jobs and memory entries, i.e. a scripting/control protocol over the app rather than a UI/panel plugin API. This is distinct from the separate agent-side Skills Hub (installs markdown skill files with a security scanner), which shapes agent behaviour, not Mission Control's own UI or server, and does not count. Documented in docs/cli-agent-control.md in github.com/builderz-labs/mission-control.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: REST API documented via an OpenAPI spec (served at /api/docs, interactive reference at /docs), a first-party MCP server (scripts/mc-mcp-server.cjs), a CLI (scripts/mc-cli.cjs) and a TUI (scripts/mc-tui.cjs).

github.description: Self-hosted control plane for AI agents: dispatch tasks, review runs, track spend, and operate OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, and other runtimes.

activity.changelogCadence: irregular, roughly every 2-4 weeks between dated entries (unreleased commits land continuously; CHANGELOG.md is bumped per version, not per PR)

editorial.reachRationale: 6,269 GitHub stars and 53 contributors on a repo created in February 2026 show real GitHub-level attention and community contribution, but there is no npm/PyPI/Homebrew distribution to measure installs, no Discord (community lives on Telegram instead), no product-specific X account, and no confirmed Show HN or launch thread for this project, HN queries either return nothing or collide with an unrelated, identically named MeisnerDan/mission-control repo (see research.notes), so reach rests on GitHub attention alone.
editorial.polishRationale: The project itself is labelled alpha software ('APIs, schemas, and configuration may change between releases'), a release shortly before the September 2026 research pass patched 13 dependency vulnerabilities including 9 in Next.js, and CHANGELOG entries describe an approval-rules engine that was scoped then deferred, signs of a serious codebase that was still settling as of September 2026 rather than a finished product.
editorial.depthRationale: Beyond dispatch and a task board it ships an automated quality gate (Aegis review with a 3-retry cycle), model-tier routing by task complexity, cron-scheduled recurring tasks, a four-layer agent eval framework (output/trace/component/drift), a full security-event and audit system with posture scoring and per-agent trust scores, a memory/knowledge-graph browser, a Skills Hub with a security scanner, and REST/MCP/CLI/TUI surfaces backed by an OpenAPI contract-parity CI check.
editorial.feelRationale: Standard Next.js 16 / React 19 web app (Tailwind, Zustand, Recharts, reagraph for the memory graph) rendered in the browser, not a native or GPU-rendered client; live terminal panes use xterm.js over node-pty, a common but not especially fast stack. No maker performance claims and no user reports of speed or jank were found (a targeted web search returned only setup guides and comparison blog posts, no sentiment on responsiveness), so this reads as an ordinary web app with no evidence pushing it above or below that baseline.

tools.name: Monocode
tools.tagline: A GUI for your coding agents
tools.valueProp: The one with the fullest issue-tracker inbox: GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Jira and Linear issues and pull requests land in one queue, and failed CI checks route straight to an agent for repair. A lead agent can coordinate up to four workers in the same checkout, and the app itself has no server, relay or account of any kind.

pricing.notes: Free, open-source (MIT) desktop app distributed as direct downloads (DMG/AppImage/deb/NSIS) from usemono.dev and GitHub Releases; no purchase flow, accounts or tiers. Requires your own paid or free CLI subscriptions/logins for whichever agents you use. README: "MonoCode does not sell tokens."

featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Not among the ten harnesses MonoCode ships adapters for (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, Pi, omp, fx, Hermes Agent); Google's own agent here is Antigravity, not Gemini CLI.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Not in the supported-harness list; GitHub only appears as an Inbox source (issues/PRs/checks), not as an agent harness.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: The harness set is fixed to ten named providers; CONTRIBUTING.md was pausing new-provider PRs as of September 2026 ('a new adapter would copy whatever is there today') and there is no generic 'run this command' adapter.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: v0.1.51: 'Git worktrees provide independent working copies for parallel sessions,' with a Settings → Worktrees manager listing branch, status, unpublished commits and associated sessions.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: v0.1.0 release notes: 'Git surface: staged and unstaged diffs, commit, push, pull, branch switching, and pull request creation.'
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Git surface covers stage/commit/push/pull/branch switching and stash-or-commit prompts on checkout conflicts (v0.1.11), and GitHub PRs can be merged/closed/reopened from the Inbox, but no in-app merge-conflict resolution UI was found across the full changelog.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: v0.1.0 security notes describe `harness_exec` running a fixed CLI allowlist inside a CSP-restricted webview, not containers or VMs; orchestration workers use private scratch directories with restrictive Unix permissions, not sandboxes.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: 'Agent orchestration v1' (v0.1.46): a lead agent coordinates up to four workers in the same checkout, assigns tasks, reviews results, and can redirect workers mid-turn.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: v0.1.52: hourly/daily/weekday/weekly schedules, 'Run now', and event triggers from GitHub/GitLab/Linear/Azure DevOps Inbox activity, with starter templates and run history.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Scoped to Agent orchestration: a lead agent's worker approvals and questions are routed through the lead, and the lead reviews/redirects worker results (v0.1.46), but this is lead/worker coordination within one orchestration run, not general agent-to-agent messaging.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Sessions live in a sidebar with folders, pins and filters (provider/status/time), not a kanban board or queue that feeds agents.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: No analytics/telemetry SDK, tracking pixel or MonoCode-run server is mentioned anywhere in the README, CONTRIBUTING, or the full CHANGELOG; the v0.1.0 security notes and the Linear-integration security note both state user data is 'never sent to MonoCode servers.' No dedicated privacy settings page was found, so this is inferred from the consistent absence of any telemetry description rather than an explicit opt-out toggle.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Agent-side only: Settings -> Skills discovers and manages SKILL.md files (MonoCode, project, personal, and harness folders) for the wrapped agent CLIs, this extends the agents MonoCode runs, not MonoCode's own interface or core. No plugin/extension API, SDK, or manifest for third-party code to change MonoCode itself was found in the README, CHANGELOG, or product site.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: MonoCode handles MCP elicitation/confirmations inside agent sessions (e.g. Codex) but does not expose its own API or MCP server for external control.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: No server or relay component of any kind; MonoCode is a fully local desktop app (v0.1.0 security notes describe only local CLI execution and webview CSP, no backend).
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Trivially true rather than actively supported: there is no vendor server in the path to begin with (no mobile client, no relay, no cloud compute), so there is nothing to self-host or depend on.

github.description: A GUI for your coding agents

top.title: MonoCode: GUI for Coding Agents

editorial.reachRationale: A single-maintainer project with a repo created in August 2026, no npm/brew/Discord/X presence and a 3-point HN mention; release-asset downloads are only in the hundreds, consistent with a personal project that was just getting started as of September 2026.
editorial.polishRationale: The CHANGELOG.md shows meticulous, near-daily craftsmanship (reduced-motion-aware animations, keyboard-accessible pickers, light/dark parity, a signed in-app updater), but the maker's own README said, as of September 2026, "This is very early and you should expect bugs," it is solo-maintained, and as of September 2026 there was no long track record of stability.
editorial.depthRationale: Goes far past a session switcher: managed worktrees with a dedicated Settings panel, session checkpoints with undo, a lead-and-up-to-four-workers orchestration mode, scheduled/event-triggered automations with templates, and an Inbox that unifies GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Jira and Linear issues/PRs and routes failed CI checks to an agent for repair.
editorial.feelRationale: Tauri desktop app (Rust backend, TypeScript/system-WebView frontend per GitHub language stats and README build instructions) rather than a GPU-rendered custom renderer, so it's lighter than Electron but not native-fast by design; README calls the project 'very early' with bugs expected, and no maker performance claims or user reports on speed/lag turned up in search (the 'Mono' name collides with MonoDevelop, drowning out results).

tools.name: Multica
tools.tagline: Your next 10 hires won't be human.
tools.valueProp: The issue tracker where agents are assignees: pick Claude Code, Codex or 24 other CLIs from the same dropdown as a colleague, and trigger runs from Slack, Lark or cron. It stays out of your git flow beyond a branch per issue, and its licence forbids hosting it for others.

pricing.notes: Self-hosting is free (Docker Compose or Helm) and agents run on the CLIs and subscriptions you already have; Multica ships no model. Multica Cloud exists (email or Google sign-in, 'Start free trial', 'Talk to sales' with a business-email-only form) but publishes no pricing page or tier table as of 2026-09-18; /pricing is a 404. The licence's hosted-service clause means only Multica may run it as a service for third parties. Vendor-hosted cloud runtimes are on a waitlist.

featureNotes.platforms.ios: Expo/React Native iPhone client in apps/mobile; not on the App Store, you build and sign it yourself from source (free Apple ID signing expires every 7 days). Docs: 'There is no Android client yet.'
featureNotes.platforms.cli: The `multica` CLI (curl installer, Homebrew tap multica-ai/tap, PowerShell) both runs the daemon and manages issues, agents, squads, autopilots and runtimes; JSON output for scripts.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Install the CLI on any server or dev box and run `multica setup`; the daemon registers that machine as a runtime. Download page: 'Same commands work over SSH.'
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Download page lists 'Cloud runtime (waitlist)': 'We'll host the runtime for you. Not live yet.' As of September 2026, agent execution was only on machines you connect.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Go backend + Next.js web + PostgreSQL 17 via Docker Compose or Helm; each user still runs the daemon on their own machine. Self-hosted GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/Forgejo integration requires creating your own app.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Custom runtime profiles let you point at a wrapper or pinned executable, but the command must speak one of the protocol families Multica already supports (Claude Code-style, Codex-style, ACP, etc.); it is not an arbitrary-command adapter.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: README: 'Multica does not ship a model. It drives the agent CLIs you already have installed and authenticated.' The daemon refuses to start until at least one supported tool is detected.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Not in the 26-tool list; Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) is supported instead.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: GitHub-repository resources use worktree mode by default: each run gets its own git worktree in the runtime's workspace directory, so runs on one repo execute concurrently. Local-directory resources default to in-place (one run at a time) with opt-in worktree mode.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Worktree mode leaves one branch per issue named `agent/<agent>/<issue>` (chats get `agent/<agent>/chat-<session>`); follow-up comments check the same branch out again. Uncommitted agent work is committed before the worktree is removed.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Docs tell you to review the agent's branch with `git log` / `git diff`; the linked-PR card shows added/deleted line counts and links out to GitHub. No diff viewer in the product.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: GitHub integration 'never pushes commits, comments, or status checks'; PRs that agents or people open are auto-linked to issues by branch name or title and can move the issue to Done on merge. No PR button of its own.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: The PR card mirrors GitHub's mergeability (mergeable / conflicting / blocked / behind) and CI status. In worktree mode, when your edits collide with the agent's the next run starts on a conflicted worktree and the agent is told to resolve it. Docs: 'Multica never merges it for you.'
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Security model doc: 'Multica makes no filesystem-sandbox guarantee'; runs execute with the daemon user's full permissions and Codex/Claude Code are launched with sandbox and permission prompts disabled. It recommends you put the daemon in a dedicated user, container or VM.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Retries keep the previous run's files and session; there is no snapshot/rollback of agent state or files.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Default caps: 20 concurrent runs per daemon, 6 per agent, adjustable. The board and each issue's execution log show every active run.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Issues page offers list, board, table, Gantt and swimlane views with custom statuses; assigning an issue to an agent enqueues a run.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Squads: a leader agent receives the issue and delegates by @-mentioning member agents or humans, which starts their runs; it is re-triggered by their replies. Parent issues with staged sub-issues wake the parent's agent when a stage completes.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Autopilots run a runbook on a 5-field cron schedule or from a webhook URL (with idempotency keys and GitHub/GitLab event filters), either creating an issue or running directly.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Inbox collects assignments, mentions, run failures and blocked issues; toggleable per group, with system/browser desktop banners. Agent work can also be followed in Slack, Lark, DingTalk, WeCom and Telegram.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Agents post comments and @-mention other agents in issue threads, which triggers those agents; squad members reply back to the leader.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Runs live on the issue: any member can watch the streaming transcript and add instructions in the same comment thread to join the run already going.
featureNotes.collaboration.teamBilling: Workspaces with owner/admin/member roles, per-agent access scopes and a sales contact form exist; no public plan or billing page.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: LICENSE is the full Apache-2.0 text plus 'Part I' conditions: no hosted service to third parties (even free) or commercial embedding without a commercial licence, and Multica branding in the UI cannot be removed. Internal use and modification are allowed. Not OSI-approved.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Web, desktop, CLI and the iOS build can all point at a self-hosted API; no vendor relay. Chat-channel bots and Git-host apps are ones you register yourself.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: Self-hosted server sends one anonymous daily snapshot to telemetry.multica.ai (release, bucketed counts); off with DO_NOT_TRACK=1. Separate PostHog analytics off with ANALYTICS_DISABLED. Documented in SELF_HOSTING.md and the v0.4.44 changelog.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial: no third-party code-plugin API, but Multica's daemon supports 'Custom runtime profiles', a documented, config-level way to register a new AI-coding-tool runtime (command, args, environment) beyond the built-in ones, so the daemon can discover and drive it like any other tool. This is a narrow, config-only extension point for Multica's own runtime/provider layer, distinct from the separate agent-side Skills system (shared SKILL.md bundles injected into each wrapped tool), which does not count. Documented at https://multica.ai/docs/daemon-runtimes#custom-runtime-profiles.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: REST API used by the CLI, with personal access tokens and run-scoped tokens; the multica-cli repo ships a skill so Claude Code/Codex/Cursor can drive it. Multica passes MCP servers to agents but does not expose an MCP server of its own.

github.description: Make humans and AI agents work as one team — open-source and self-hostable.

top.title: Multica: Orchestrating business agents like a real leadership team

tools.authorNote: A completely different mental model than everything else on the list. Instead of centering on chat sessions, Multica centers on tasks in a Kanban board. Agents with different tools, personalities and profiles pick up those tasks, work on them, and hand work off to each other. Like Amp, it’s worth having just to experience it even if it doesn’t end up becoming your daily driver.

editorial.reachRationale: An exceptionally large contributor base (309) and 1.1M+ release-asset downloads over the last five releases are strong product-specific usage signals, but they sit oddly next to a stale product X account (last post in June 2026, 3,349 followers) and a nearly invisible HN reception (2 points); credited the download/contributor evidence first while discounting the 50k stars, landing at established rather than higher.
editorial.polishRationale: Signed installers for six desktop targets with auto-update, a dated changelog written in plain language for every release (62 in 90 days), consistent and thorough English docs with translations, and a security-model page that states its limits honestly. Held back by the iOS client being build-it-yourself, the cloud runtime being a waitlist, no pricing page, a marketing site that counts 26 tools while the docs table lists 25, and 1,600 open issues. Judged from docs, changelog and release assets, not hands-on use.
editorial.depthRationale: This is a full Linear-style tracker (projects, sub-issues with stages, custom statuses, five views, inbox, roles, per-agent access scopes) on top of the multiplexer, plus squads that route work through a leader agent, cron and webhook autopilots with delivery replay, skills injected into 25 different CLIs' native skill paths, MCP config pushed per agent, five chat-channel integrations, GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/Forgejo PR linking with CI and mergeability, and a scriptable CLI with JSON output. It has no diff review, PR creation or merge, and no sandboxing. Judged from docs, changelog and release assets, not hands-on use.
editorial.feelRationale: README states Desktop is 'Electron, sharing the web UI packages'; a GitHub issue (#4930, closed) documents long issue-detail pages becoming 'noticeably slow or heavy' to open, with the maker's own fix ideas including virtualized rendering and paginated comment loading -- evidence of a heavy tracker-style web app rather than a lightweight one.

tools.name: Munder Difflin
tools.tagline: Agent harness to run an office of your clones
tools.valueProp: A 2D office floor where every CLI agent is an avatar at a desk, coordinated by an orchestrator that routes and escalates between them. The free tier is a full local hive; as of September 2026, remote and cloud execution had not shipped (the maker's own label is “coming soon”).

pricing.notes: Free forever tier: unlimited local agents, twelve providers, MIT licensed, includes the Command Center and kanban. Pro is $150/year (launch price, normally $200) or $20/month for the "Pro workspace" (orchestrator, tasks, inbox, automations, memory in one window) plus Stapler (screenshot/voice/meeting capture into the orchestrator), one machine at a time. Teams is priced per call (30-min setup), adds E2E-encrypted cross-device orchestrator messaging, invite-code seats and an admin console. Sandboxes (cloud execution) and mobile remote control were announced but had not gone on sale as of September 2026.

featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: No extension mechanism of its own: Munder Difflin's 'MCP and skills' post explains each hive agent is a real `claude` CLI session, so MCP servers and skills are simply inherited from the user's existing Claude Code configuration rather than registered with or distributed through Munder Difflin itself. No plugins/, extensions/ or SDK directory exists in the repo, and the README's related items are unchecked roadmap boxes, not a shipped feature.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: The built-in Monaco IDE has CHANGES/HISTORY/COMPARE git rails with branch compare and a "guarded checkout", but there is no dedicated conflict-resolution UI.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: HIVE.md describes the GOD agent's task ledger (tasks.json) as "assign, track, retry, checkpoint", a work-item checkpoint for retrying tasks, not a file/session snapshot-and-rollback.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Deliberately not MCP: the blog (mcp-and-skills-in-a-hive) says the harness's own memory layer runs as a CLI "not MCP, by decision" so it doesn't consume an agent's MCP slot. No external API or MCP server for controlling the app itself was found.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: The GOD orchestrator ("Michael") is described in HIVE.md as "an ordinary claude process" running with a system prompt, not a separate proprietary agent loop.

github.description: an open-source alternative to the dots, bots and muses of the world, run an office of claude code/codex like agents on your laptop, sandboxes or anywhere, uses your existing subscriptions

top.title: Munder Difflin – Agent harness to run an office of your clones

editorial.reachRationale: Strong first-party install/attention signals, 99,355 release-asset downloads (matching the homepage's own "100K+ downloads" claim), 7,944 stars, 57 contributors, #1 GitHub Trending and #5 Product Hunt of the day, and a well-received 312-point/145-comment Show HN, support an established, past-early-adopter user base. Discounted the personal X account (211 followers, maker's own handle, not a product account) and the modest 298-member Discord; the repo was created in May 2026, which keeps this short of "major".
editorial.polishRationale: Signed/notarized macOS builds plus Windows and Linux, a weekly release cadence (20 releases in 90 days), 57 contributors, i18n into Simplified Chinese and Arabic with RTL layout, a documented design-token system (DESIGN.md), a one-click auto-updater, and heavy SEO/blog investment. Held back: the app carried a self-applied "status: pre-release" badge as of September 2026, 234 open issues against a fast-moving repo, and the site's own FAQ page ("there's no paid tier to unlock the core") contradicts the current homepage pricing (Free/Pro $150-a-year/Teams), showing the marketing surface hasn't caught up with the product.
editorial.depthRationale: Well past a tmux wrapper: per-agent git worktrees, a shared semantic memory palace, inter-agent mailboxes, a dependency-aware kanban fed by GitHub issues, Slack/webhook triggers that spawn ephemeral workers, per-agent token budgets with a steer-constrain-stop circuit breaker, a built-in Monaco IDE with git rails, a 227-entry skills catalog, and (Teams) end-to-end-encrypted cross-device orchestrator messaging. Held back: no PR-creation flow was found, merge help is limited to branch compare/guarded checkout, there's no API/MCP surface, and remote-machine execution, cloud sandboxes and mobile remote control had not shipped as of September 2026 (announced by the maker as "coming soon").
editorial.feelRationale: Electron + Pixi.js (office floor) + xterm.js/node-pty (real terminal panes), not a native or GPU-native stack. The maker has documented deliberate performance engineering for this (rendering-many-live-terminals-performance blog: pooled persistent terminals, visible-only rendering, bounded scrollback, per-session IPC, an optional WebGL xterm addon "when measurement says so"), and a targeted search turned up no third-party reports of lag or jank, but also no independent "feels instant" praise, typical well-optimised Electron, not a native-speed standout.

tools.name: Muse Code
tools.tagline: A coding agent for your most complex coding workstreams.
tools.valueProp: Meta’s own terminal agent: one binary fans a task out to as many as 64 co-trained agents per session, with a control room to watch them. It runs no other vendor’s agent or model, and the cheap tier is paid for by letting Meta train on your code.

maker.name: Meta (Meta Superintelligence Labs)
maker.funding: Meta Platforms, Inc.; product of Meta Superintelligence Labs

pricing.notes: The CLI is a free download but every token is billed by Meta; there is no bring-your-own-key path to another vendor. Two ways to pay: (1) pay-as-you-go through a Meta Model API key, Standard tier $1.25 in / $0.15 cached / $4.25 out per Mtok (not used for training) or Contributor tier $0.10 / $0.002 / $0.20 (your prompts and completions train Meta models; the ToS says not to submit confidential code to it); (2) Muse Code subscriptions, CLI-only, bought through Meta Accounts Center: Everyday Usage $5/mo (10-50 prompts every 5 hours, voice, web search), High Usage $15/mo (5x), Power Usage $50/mo (20x, early access to features). No free tier is documented for Muse Code itself. Web search grounding is $2.50 per 1,000 queries on pay-as-you-go.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Docs: workflows are unavailable in the public aarch64-apple-darwin (Apple silicon) package because it omits workflow-script-engine-v8; voice input is on by default on macOS.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Docs list Windows (irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex) with gaps: PowerShell replaces Bash, the sandbox may raise a UAC prompt, and voice input and session messaging are unavailable.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Docs and the out-of-beta post say macOS and Linux; the product homepage said 'Available for MacOS and Windows' as of September 2026. Linux sandbox needs a working bubblewrap and a non-musl build; voice is off by default.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: `muse exec "<prompt>"` runs headless for scripts and CI with JSONL output, exit codes and --max-model-steps; `muse serve` exposes the engine over stdio.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: `muse` opens a full-screen terminal UI with slash commands, /workflows, /subagents, /tasks, side chats, rewind and a live reasoning line.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: No daemon, relay or SSH attach feature. Session messaging is explicitly local-only ('does not provide cross-user or cross-machine transport'); `muse serve` speaks the session protocol over standard I/O only.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: Meta hosts the model, not the workspace. Agents always run where the binary is installed; CI is your own runner.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: `muse serve` is a local stdio host for the SDK, not a network server; there is no relay or server component to run.
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Muse Code does not run Claude Code. It can message local Claude Code sessions over the same Unix-socket peer messaging (1.2.1 changelog), reads CLAUDE.md, discovers ~/.claude/skills, and a bundled /migrate skill imports Claude Code memory notes and MCP servers.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Not run. `muse skills import --from codex` and /migrate import Codex skills, memory and MCP servers; $CODEX_HOME/skills is scanned by default.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: No adapter for third-party agents; every worker, reviewer, observer and workflow child is Muse Code's own loop on Muse Spark.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Its own harness co-trained with Muse Spark 1.2 / 1.3; default model muse-spark-1.2, switchable with /models. Reasoning-effort docs mention 'other providers' but no non-Meta provider is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: `muse -w` starts a session in a Muse Code-managed worktree from HEAD (removed on close when clean and pushed); subagents and workflow children can each request an isolated managed worktree, never as a silent fallback.
featureNotes.isolation.containers: Not a container per task. Every shell command runs in an OS sandbox on by default (Seatbelt on macOS, bundled bubblewrap on Linux, a Windows sandbox) that limits writes to the workspace plus temp and gates network per destination; MCP tools and hooks run outside it.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Worktrees are created from HEAD; no automatic branch naming is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Edits show as expandable tool rows in the transcript and the session protocol carries a patchSummary/patchRef per edit for clients to render; there is no dedicated diff or review pane.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: No PR feature. Docs: it 'won't commit, amend, or push your work unless you ask it to'.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Docs: 'Review and integrate each session's changes through your normal source-control workflow.'
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Rewind (double Esc or /rewind) and /fork branch the conversation from an earlier point using the append-only event log, and crashed sessions resume from it, but rewind 'does not restore, revert, or delete workspace files'.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Inside one session, /workflows and /subagents show every child agent's status, tokens and progress together (up to 8 concurrent by default, 64 max per tree; a workflow may spawn 1,000 children with 16 active). Independent top-level sessions are separate terminals with no combined view.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: No kanban or queue. /tasks is a drawer of one session's background commands and subagents; Alt+Enter queues a prompt for the next turn.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Lead session spawns bounded child agents that can spawn grandchildren; workflows add staged/parallel groups written as JavaScript and saved for reuse under .agents/workflows. Four background observer agents (memory, skill, goal, verification) run alongside the main agent by default.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: /loop schedules a recurring prompt or skill by interval or 5-field cron inside a live session (jobs expire after 7 days); `muse exec` runs one prompt headless in CI with --disable-approval or --yolo.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: No built-in desktop or push alert. A `Notification` hook event 'fires when the agent needs your approval, so a hook can alert you'; you wire the channel yourself.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Session messaging: named live sessions on the same macOS/Linux machine discover peers and send steer/queue/notify messages over a Unix socket, with recipient-side approval of unknown senders; 1.2.1 notes messaging local Claude Code sessions. Unavailable on Windows and in headless runs.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: Alt+V / Option+V dictation; on by default on macOS, off by default on Linux, unavailable on Windows.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Meta Model API accounts have teams with admins, shared API keys and per-team rate limits, and managed hooks/config planes exist for enterprise administrators; Muse Code sessions themselves are single-user and messaging is same-account only.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Docs: session messaging 'does not provide cross-user or cross-machine transport'; no shared or multiplayer session feature.
