editorial.polishRationale: Separate Stable/Beta channels, signed platform-specific installers, a searchable docs site, recovery guidance and detailed release notes support a fairly finished workflow despite the README early-stage caveat.
editorial.depthRationale: Task-owned worktrees, integrated browser and simulator previews, diff/PR review, provider handoffs, scheduled automations, checkpoints, a headless server and Agent Gateway reach well beyond terminal multiplexing.
editorial.feelRationale: Synara's repo (Emanuele-web04/synara) ships an electron/electron-updater desktop target (start:desktop, electron-dev scripts) over a mostly TypeScript/JavaScript codebase, a standard Electron shell; no user reports of lag or praise for speed were found.

tools.name: T3 Code
tools.tagline: The open-source control plane for coding agents.
tools.valueProp: The free one with every client: desktop, hosted web, App Store and Play Store, with no paid tier at all, and one prompt fans out to several models in parallel worktrees. No task board, no automations, no cloud compute.

pricing.notes: Free with no paid tier. Terms of Service: 'T3 Code is currently offered without a T3 Tools subscription fee unless we clearly state otherwise for a feature.' You install and sign in to the agent CLIs with your own Claude, OpenAI, Cursor, xAI, OpenCode or Google subscriptions or API keys; T3 does not resell tokens. The optional T3 Connect relay (mobile access without port forwarding, push notifications) needs a free T3 account. README: 'Wait, what are you selling me? Nothing.'

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Electron app; arm64 and x64 DMGs, Homebrew cask t3-code. The `t3` server CLI has no Intel Mac build (build from source).
featureNotes.platforms.linux: x86_64 AppImage from GitHub Releases; AUR packages t3code-bin and t3code-nightly-bin are maintained in-repo under packaging/aur. SnapShots need Wayland.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: x64 .exe and winget T3Tools.T3Code; agents can run inside a WSL distro. Windows cannot run the background service.
featureNotes.platforms.web: Two forms: `t3` starts a local server and opens a local web app; app.t3.codes is a hosted client that connects straight to your server over HTTPS (it does not proxy).
featureNotes.platforms.cli: `t3` starts, serves, pairs, connects and updates the server; `t3 app [path]` opens a new agent thread for a directory in the running desktop app. Not a full agent-steering CLI.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Four routes to a machine you own: LAN/tailnet pairing links, Tailscale HTTPS (`t3 serve --tailscale-serve`), desktop-managed SSH that installs and launches the server on the host, and the T3 Connect relay. Remote host must be Linux or Apple Silicon macOS for SSH-managed servers.
featureNotes.execution.cloudManaged: No vendor sandboxes; docs: 'T3 Code runs coding agents on your computer'.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: `t3 serve` / `t3 service install` runs the server on any Linux or macOS host you control; the relay source also lives in the repo (infra/relay).
featureNotes.agents.claudeCode: Multiple accounts via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR instances; OpenRouter and claude-code-router setups documented; auto-compact threshold setting.
featureNotes.agents.codex: Multiple accounts via CODEX_HOME shadow homes; async questions and app-access approvals surfaced.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Not listed. Google Antigravity (the official Antigravity ACP agent, signed in with Google, Gemini Enterprise, Gemini API key or Vertex) is supported instead.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Not first-party; the community fork zortos293/t3code-copilot adds it.
featureNotes.agents.opencode: Requires OpenCode 1.14.19+; can attach to an existing external OpenCode server by URL.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Cursor CLI (`cursor-agent`), including subscription limit reporting.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Providers are fixed adapters (Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity); binary path and env vars are configurable per instance but there is no generic command adapter.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Per-thread 'New worktree' option (not the default; a thread can also work in the project directory). Storage settings auto-remove T3-managed worktrees after inactivity, after merge, or when they have no commits.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: A worktree thread gets its own branch; branch names, commit messages and PR descriptions are generated by the selected provider.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Diff panel per thread plus a Pull requests page with comments, viewed-file marks and review actions; the mobile app shows PR status but not the diff.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Git actions commit, push and open PRs on GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps via each host's CLI or token.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Merge, auto-merge while checks run, revert PRs, and GitHub stack 'Merge stack' / 'Rebase stack' from the PR page. No local conflict-resolution UI is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Checkpoints use hidden git refs; 'Edit from here' rewinds the conversation and can 'Revert files too', only for threads in a worktree and only for providers that can rewind (Antigravity cannot).
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Thread sidebar with pinned/active/snoozed/settled sections; Cmd+Enter starts a thread in the background; Shift-click several models to send one prompt as separate threads and worktrees; auto balance places new threads across connected machines.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Threads settle automatically after inactivity or when their PR merges, but there is no board or queue feeding agents.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: The Agents view only inspects a provider's own subagent activity (Claude, Antigravity batches); T3 Code does not spawn or steer agents from an agent.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Push notifications and iOS Live Activities / Android ongoing activity when an agent finishes, fails, needs approval or asks for input, on mobile via T3 Connect only. Desktop alerts are not documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.voice: On-device dictation on iPhone with iOS 26+ inserts text into the composer; no voice on desktop or Android and it never submits a turn.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: A T3 account is one person's devices and environments; no orgs, seats or shared environments are documented.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Pairing, Tailscale and SSH routes need no vendor server; only the optional T3 Connect relay (Cloudflare tunnels, Clerk auth) and mobile push notifications go through T3 Tools infrastructure.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: PostHog product events are on by default (provider, model, permission mode, durations, token totals; no prompts or file contents). Disable with T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false on the server.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Config-only, not code-level: T3 Code has no plugin/extension SDK for adding a panel, view, provider or command to the app itself. A project's `t3.json` can declare named "actions" that Settings → Project imports and lets a user run/edit (docs/user/project-settings.md: "The Project category... holds the project's name, icon, actions, checkouts and removal... A project's t3.json actions can be imported there."); this is exactly the config-level 'custom command/action JSON that the app runs' bar for partial, not a third-party code-loading mechanism. Providers are a fixed, individually documented list (Claude, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode) with no generic/custom-provider hook.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: `t3 app <path>` opens a thread from a shell, and T3 exposes MCP tools to the agents it runs (link_pull_request, device_* tools); there is no documented public API or MCP server for driving T3 Code from outside.

top.title: T3 Code – a new OSS agentic coding app that wraps Codex

editorial.reachRationale: My call: 28k GitHub stars, 169k monthly npm downloads for the CLI and 143,866 release-asset downloads, with Theo Browne’s audience behind it. That is major-name reach, not the established middle, even if the Discord is his general server and the HN launch was quiet.
editorial.polishRationale: Seven months after the first commit it ships signed builds for macOS, Windows and Linux, App Store and Play Store apps, a hosted web client, winget/Homebrew/AUR packages, a background service with remote self-update, and roughly two stable releases a week on top of daily nightlies; the in-repo user docs are detailed and consistent with the product. Held back because the version was 0.0.x as of September 2026, the README says 'very very early, expect bugs', there are about 2,000 open issues, there is no docs site, and this is judged from docs and release notes rather than hands-on use.
editorial.depthRationale: Past a session switcher it has per-thread worktrees with auto-cleanup, checkpoint rewind with file restore, a PR review-and-merge surface across six git hosts including GitHub stacks, multi-model fan-out, load balancing of new threads across machines, a pooled subscription-limits dashboard, an embedded browser, iOS/Android simulator panels agents can drive, and SnapShots with accessibility data. It stops short because there is no task board, no scheduled or event-triggered runs, no agent-spawns-agent orchestration, no team features and no public API.
editorial.feelRationale: The desktop app is Electron-based (README) rather than a GPU-rendered native shell, but the maker set out to build 'something performant' and the X testimonials the homepage curates specifically praise speed - 'the first coding gui that didn't suck performance wise' and 'pretty awesome, really fast too' - with no jank or slowness complaints turning up in docs or social posts.

tools.name: Tembo
tools.tagline: Move coding agents to the cloud
tools.valueProp: Harness-agnostic cloud sessions: bring Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Amp, Pi, OpenCode or Tembo's own open-source fx agent, each running in its own VM, plus BYOK and a PR review workspace spanning GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket. Unlike Devin, the whole platform ships as a self-hostable single-instance release, not just cloud workers.

maker.name: Tembo, Inc.
maker.funding: $20M total, including a $14M Series A led by GreatPoint Ventures (Venrock, Grand Ventures, Wireframe Ventures, Defined Capital and Cintrifuse Capital also participated). Founded by Ry Walker (CEO, previously founded Astronomer.io), Darren Baldwin Jr. (CTO), Benjamin Akar (CPO) and Connor Paton (CGO).

pricing.notes: Free is a 14-day trial only (1 user, 1 repo, 1 project, open-source models plus OpenCode/Pi), not a permanent free tier. Pro $60/mo and Max $200/mo are usage allowances (Tembo Gateway tokens + VM compute) with overage billing, up to 5 or 10 users. Enterprise is custom. BYOK (including OpenRouter) and connected ChatGPT/Codex OAuth subscriptions make model inference $0 through Tembo, but VM compute draws from the plan's allowance. Compute is metered per-second by VM size ($0.1066-$2.9536/hour).

featureNotes.platforms.linux: Desktop download page lists the Linux build as an AppImage marked '(Beta)', versus a stable macOS .dmg.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: A `tembo` CLI exists, but it runs inside the session sandbox for the agent's own terminal operations (git, merge continuation, dependency installs); it is not a client a user installs to start or steer sessions from their own machine.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: No 'attach Tembo to a machine you own for a normal session' path is documented; every session (hosted or self-hosted) runs in a Tembo-provisioned VM sandbox, not your own already-running machine.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Self-hosted overview: the entire platform (web app, API, agent workers, cron, admin UI, Postgres, Redis) ships as a single-instance NixOS machine image you run in your own AWS/GCP/Azure/on-prem environment, with a web installer and pull-based updates.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Gemini models are selectable inside the Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and fx harnesses, but 'Gemini CLI' is not itself one of the six listed agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Amp, Pi/fx).
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: The agent harness list (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Amp, Pi, fx) is fixed in the docs; 'Custom agents' in the pricing table refers to user-authored automation instructions on top of those harnesses, not a generic arbitrary-binary adapter.
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Tembo built and open-sourced its own harness, fx ('a tiny, open, native coding agent with multi-provider model support', github.com/tembo/fx, Apache-2.0), offered alongside third-party harnesses in every session.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: No git-worktree management is documented anywhere in the docs, changelog or sandbox pages; isolation is one fresh ephemeral VM sandbox per session (repo cloned in, torn down after), not a worktree per task.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Not named as a discrete feature, but the core workflow (session -> Open PR) implies a branch per session; the review dashboard mockup shows agent-authored branches like `tembo/allow-tagged-bots`.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: The in-sandbox `tembo` CLI ships a `tembo merge --continue` command 'to finish a merge after you resolve conflicts and stage the resolutions' (built-in-skills-and-tools docs); no dedicated in-app conflict-resolution UI is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Pricing compares 'Pausable / resumable sessions' (VM snapshot/pause, no compute charge while stopped) and the changelog adds automatic task recovery after a sandbox crash; there is no documented step-level revert/fork like Devin's, so this is session-level pause/resume rather than a rollback feature.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Sessions live in a sortable, filterable list (by status, created/updated, archived) grouped into views like 'My sessions' and 'Team activity', not a kanban board.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Sessions have an explicit visibility toggle (workspace-wide vs private) and a 'Team visibility' activity feed so teammates can see what's running and comment via Slack/PR threads; no evidence of two people co-steering the same live turn simultaneously.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: The full stack, including the web control plane and agent workers, runs as a single customer-operated NixOS instance (self-hosted/overview); a Tembo license key and outbound HTTPS to Tembo's release endpoint are required for updates, with an air-gapped/manual-update option.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: BYOK (including OpenRouter) and connected ChatGPT/Codex OAuth subscriptions make Tembo Gateway model usage $0; VM compute is billed against your Tembo plan allowance either way.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: False: nothing lets third-party code extend Tembo's own panels, commands or providers. The only extension points found are agent-side: `.tembo.json` hooks run a fixed `setupScript`/`postClone` shell list before the agent starts (docs.tembo.io/features/hooks), and 'Third-party MCP servers and custom skills can add to' the agent's sandbox tools (built-in-skills-and-tools docs), both extend what the agent can do, not the Tembo application itself. No plugin/extension/SDK-for-the-app page exists in the docs index (docs.tembo.io/llms.txt); the public `sdk`/`sdk-python` GitHub repos and MCP server are API clients, not app plugins.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Public REST API covers sessions, agents, projects, sandboxes, PRs, repositories, queues and organizations (docs.tembo.io/api), plus a hosted Tembo MCP server for connecting AI clients to that same API.

top.title: Launch HN: Relace (YC W23) – Models for fast and reliable codegen

editorial.reachRationale: A weekly changelog and a handful of named customers on the homepage (Kernel, Tilt, Whop, Conduit, Collabrios) show real, active usage, but community signals are minimal: an X account with ~8.5k followers, a product Discord with only 9 members, and official SDK/MCP npm packages downloading in the low hundreds per month. HN queries return only name-collision noise (a similarly named 'Tambo' React UI toolkit, and unrelated launches) so no genuine public-launch discussion was found; the founders' prior company (Astronomer.io) was discounted as not being this product.
editorial.polishRationale: The docs and weekly changelog are detailed and consistent (themes, live PR checks, a real code editor for setup scripts), but the Linux desktop build is explicitly 'Beta', the macOS app is at an early v0.0.7, Kubernetes/GCP self-hosted deploys are 'early access', and pricing FAQ language ('coming soon...maybe' on an old npm package) suggests parts of the stack are young.
editorial.depthRationale: Beyond session-switching, Tembo has a cross-Git-provider (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket) review workspace with 'Tour Mode' grouping and chat-with-the-diff, event/schedule-driven automations across nine-plus integrations with reusable templates, a genuinely self-hostable single-instance platform (not just workers), and seven interchangeable agent harnesses including its own open-source fx. It falls short of the set's ceiling because it has no multi-agent orchestration: no coordinator/child sessions, no kanban task board, and no cross-agent messaging.
editorial.feelRationale: Tembo's desktop downloads are a macOS .dmg and a Linux AppImage alongside an identical web app at app.tembo.io, the standard packaging for a web-rendered client; the only speed claims found (fast to start, pausable, resumable) describe cloud session startup, not the interface itself.

tools.name: Tern
tools.tagline: A neoterminal for the Electron-weary.
tools.valueProp: Tern keeps terminal and agent panes alive in a daemon while Mac, iPhone and browser clients share one session. Its native blocks and Luau plugins put files, Git, notebooks and custom tools beside the shell.

pricing.notes: Tern is waitlist-gated in closed beta; no Tern-specific public price or plan was found on its product page or plugin docs.

featureNotes.platforms.ios: The product page shows a native iPhone client sharing the same live session, but access is closed beta via waitlist; no public App Store or TestFlight distribution was verified.
featureNotes.platforms.web: The product page demonstrates a browser client via tern web serve and WebGPU; this is a self-served browser tab, not a Stencil-managed cloud workspace.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: The product page documents tern split, run and capture; the SDK documents tern ctl for scripting windows and sessions.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: The product page documents tern remote serve on a server over QUIC, reached through Tailscale or Iroh; sessions stay on that machine.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: tern remote serve exposes the user-run session daemon; tern web serve exposes a browser client.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: SDK scripts/sessions.md documents agent-command <command> for future agent blocks; arbitrary CLI commands can run, but only omp receives the advertised native Surface Protocol treatment.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: No Tern-managed worktree creation or per-task assignment is documented: the product page lists Git blocks, while SDK scripts/git.md only documents folding/unfolding a worktrees section in Git Refs. Displaying existing worktrees does not meet the manage-them requirement.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: The product page shows Git graph, diffs and line staging; SDK scripts/git.md documents opening changed files as diffs.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: The advertised kanban block is a view over TODO.md; no task-to-agent dispatch is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: SDK scripts/terminal.md documents an attention inbox and a waiting alert, but these are script-driven states; automatic blocked-agent OS or push alerts were not verified.
featureNotes.openness.openSource: Stencil publishes an MIT-licensed Tern SDK and examples, but no main Tern app repository or product source was found among its public organization repositories.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: The session daemon can run on your own machine, but the product page requires a Stencil account and waitlist admission; no account-free end-to-end path is documented.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: True app-extending code: docs.stencil.so/tern/index.md documents Luau plugin.toml packages loaded by Tern, with host/window entry points for native blocks, command lenses, pane hooks, palette commands, key binds, routes, CSS and layout. This extends Tern itself, not agent skills or MCP.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: SDK scripts/index.md documents tern ctl and a local control endpoint for scripts to drive windows, panes and sessions; the product page also names tern split/run/capture.

tools.authorNote: A brand new, early-stage beta app by the guy who made OMP, the infamous pi fork. It's in early access, but quite polished and slick, and it feels pretty good to use.

editorial.reachRationale: Tern was waitlist-gated in closed beta as of October 2026. Stencil publishes a Tern-specific SDK with 64 GitHub stars and installable plugin examples, suggesting early developer attention; SDK stars are not product installs, and no public user or download count was found.
editorial.polishRationale: The product page shows a coherent native Mac, iPhone and browser experience, while extensive plugin and scripting docs cover concrete controls; closed-beta access prevents public hands-on verification.
editorial.depthRationale: Persistent sessions, remote hosts, native file/Git/database/notebook/board blocks, a control API and app-extending Luau plugins reach far beyond terminal splits, though no managed worktrees or task-to-agent dispatch is documented.
editorial.feelRationale: Stencil says Tern is Rust-native without bundled Chromium and reports a 151 ms cold launch to an interactive prompt (p95) on its product page. This supports a fast-feeling 4, but the benchmark is maker-reported and public access is waitlist-gated.

tools.name: Tortie
tools.tagline: A calm agent multiplexer with familiar IDE features.
tools.valueProp: Durability first: agents run in a private bundled tmux server, so quitting or crashing the app never kills a session, and a reboot replays scrollback with each agent’s resume command armed. Skips worktrees, queues and cloud on purpose; Apple-silicon only.

maker.name: Greg Ceccarelli (gregce)
maker.funding: none announced; solo side project by a SpecStory co-founder (README: 'I built it to scratch my own itch'), bundles SpecStory capture

pricing.notes: Free under Apache 2.0 with no paid tier. Tortie launches agent CLIs you already installed and signed into; optional Claude/Codex usage meters read your existing plan's quota. The only model calls it makes itself are the optional one-line Catch Me Up summary and the optional Architecture contract, both routed through an agent you pick.

featureNotes.platforms.macos: Apple silicon only, macOS 15.7.9 or later; signed DMG from GitHub releases, no Intel build.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: An optional `tortie` shell command exists but only opens a folder in the app; docs say it 'is not a remote-control API' and it cannot start or steer agents.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: Marked 'early'. Adds another Mac over SSH (Tailscale suggested); sessions run in that machine's own tmux, which must already be installed. Remote folders are read-only until you approve one write root per machine. Linux hosts untested.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: No server or relay component exists; remote access is direct SSH from the app.
featureNotes.agents.geminiCli: Launch and resume machinery exist but docs say the full resume round-trip is unproven, and Catch Me Up shows your asks but not Gemini's answers.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Not launchable. Docs list 'VS Code Copilot' only as a capture-only observer, alongside Cursor IDE.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Cursor CLI is launchable; docs note some attachment behaviour is inferred.
featureNotes.agents.pi: Launchable; safe resume depends on the original project directory. Its successor Oh My Pi resumes from any directory and joins Catch Me Up.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Add a CLI with a data-only `agents.json` row (command, args, resume shape); Tortie asks for confirmation before a new definition can start a process. No third-party code is loaded.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: PRODUCT.md calls a project tab 'worktree-aware, not worktree-required'; Tortie does not create or manage worktrees and its docs point you to an orchestrator for 'worktree assignment'.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Modified files open as a diff against HEAD by default (Pierre Diffs); a separate Redline view marks up prose files word by word with per-change accept and rewind.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: Git sidebar can publish, push and open commits on GitHub, and reads GitHub Actions runs via a read-only `gh` allowlist, but no PR creation is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Source control groups 'merge changes', and offers pull, sync and cherry-pick, but no conflict-resolution editor is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Checkpoints are for sessions, not files: bounded scrollback snapshots plus an armed resume command survive a reboot, and removed sessions stay recoverable for 90 days. Per-phrase rewind exists only in the Redline view for Markdown/text files.
featureNotes.orchestration.parallelSessions: Any number of named sessions per project tab; up to 6 can be arranged in one split.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: A menu-bar indicator lights only when a session is blocked on a person, and ⌘J opens a cross-project list of sessions waiting for input. No OS push/desktop notification is documented.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: No vendor server exists at all; updates come from GitHub releases and optional SpecStory Cloud sign-in is the only third-party service.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: No telemetry or privacy statement in the docs. The repo has no analytics dependency and no telemetry code in src; a repo research note (docs/research/37-telemetry.md) plans opt-in usage telemetry with a forced first-run choice, which had not shipped as of September 2026. Docs state usage meters and SpecStory capture send nothing unless switched on.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Config-only, not code-loading: docs/supported-agents#custom-agents states "Custom agents are data-only JSON definitions. They can describe a command, arguments, icon, activity behavior, and safe resume shape without loading third-party code into Tortie's own processes." A definition can only launch a new agent/command entry, not add a panel, view or provider elsewhere in the app. README confirms the same boundary explicitly: "It does not run third-party plugin code inside its own processes. Adding an agent is configuration, not code." The "plugins" the app surfaces in Session Tools (docs/agent-context-and-skills) are each agent's own skills/MCP servers/hooks, read-only and agent-side.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Docs: 'Tortie is not a general remote-control API.' It inspects agents' MCP servers but exposes none of its own.

github.description: A calm agent multiplexer with familiar IDE features, for macOS, with an iPhone app.

editorial.reachRationale: A textbook niche case: 81 stars, effectively a solo maintainer (2 contributors), no npm/PyPI/brew distribution, no Discord, zero HN stories, and a personal X account with under 1,000 followers, a personal project by design.
editorial.polishRationale: Signed, self-updating DMG; a marketing site with an in-browser live demo of the build; docs that state limits as plainly as features (each agent's resume status, remote 'early', 'saves have no undo'); a full Git sidebar with commit graph, file history and GitHub Actions runs; light/dark themes and custom fonts. Held back by Apple-silicon-only support, ~80 stars, and a 'Contributor entries: 1' project created in August 2026.
editorial.depthRationale: It goes well past a tmux wrapper on durability (private tmux server, reboot snapshots, armed resume commands), review (diff-vs-HEAD, prose Redline, Catch Me Up transcript reader) and agent introspection (Context view of skills/MCP/hooks, an Architecture map), but by design has no worktrees, task board, automations, PR creation, subagents or multi-user.
editorial.feelRationale: Electron (Monaco editor, xterm.js terminal, `src/renderer`), but the maker publishes an unusually detailed performance write-up with measured before/after numbers: warm startup (DOMContentLoaded) 29-44% faster, first terminal attachment 16-31% faster, and a Source Control view rewrite that cut renderer memory from 1.3-1.8GB to 90-135MB and eliminated long tasks in a 96,000-file stress test. Only minor, already-fixed rough edges turned up (e.g. a Redline redraw that 'used to feel slower').

tools.name: Traycer
tools.tagline: The <Nerve Center/> for Agentic Coding
tools.valueProp: Traycer keeps coding agents, planning artifacts, diffs, and team comments in one shared Task across desktop and mobile. It also lets agents coordinate across your own machines while retaining managed worktrees and model switching.

maker.name: Traycer
maker.funding: Investor-backed; investor names not established from the About Us page.

pricing.notes: Free includes unlimited sessions, remote hosts, mobile app, sync and individual sharing with your own agent subscriptions. Sync is $20/user/month or $16/user/month annually for team-wide sharing. Traycer inference credits are optional pay-as-you-go with a 20% markup; the pricing page also lists cloud sandboxes at additional cost.

featureNotes.platforms.ios: The iPhone and iPad app is distributed through TestFlight beta, not the App Store (install and mobile-app docs).
featureNotes.platforms.web: The web dashboard manages account, billing and teams; docs describe Desktop and mobile as the Task interfaces, not a browser workspace.
featureNotes.platforms.tui: The terminal agent interface runs a coding agent CLI in a terminal; Traycer does not document a full-screen Traycer TUI.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Traycer Host is installed and supervised on your own local or remote machine; the separate Traycer cloud handles sync and mobile relay (concepts/hosts; concepts/sync-and-offline).
featureNotes.agents.builtIn: Traycer Inference is an opt-in provider using Traycer credits; it is distinct from the external CLI agents.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Desktop docs enumerate supported coding-agent integrations and allow a custom binary path for an existing provider; the custom-CLI-agent integration is documented for the separate IDE extension.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: Traycer creates a new Git worktree and branch per selected workspace folder/run, lists and deletes managed worktrees, and offers Sweep and optional safe automatic cleanup (concepts/worktrees; settings/worktrees).
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: A new branch is created when a Task uses the New worktree run location; Local and Existing worktree modes do not create one.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: The Pull Requests panel follows PRs opened by an agent; docs do not describe a Traycer control to create a PR.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: Git Diff has a Merge Changes section for conflicts and Sweep detects merged branches; no in-app conflict resolver or merge action is documented.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: The review guide and Agents panel document per-turn and per-file undo; for an agent fork, the CLI copies a Chat agent from its latest checkpoint.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Tasks contain planning artifacts and tickets with status; the first screen is a workspace, and no automatic ticket-to-agent queue is documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Host notification hooks run a script or POST on selected events; scheduled wake-ups in the changelog belong to Claude background work rather than a general Traycer scheduler.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: Agent-to-agent messaging, transcript access and child creation depend on the user, Host and agent surface per the capability matrix.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Shared Tasks permit collaborative artifacts and comments; other people can view and clone shared agent chats, but cannot steer the same agent.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: The desktop app and Host are open-source, but docs say mobile reaches a Traycer relay and Tasks sync to Traycer cloud.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: The website privacy policy offers an analytics opt-out; release builds may enable Sentry/PostHog per README, and no desktop telemetry disable control was established.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Partial, config/hooks only for Traycer itself: Host notification hooks run a script or POST a URL, and the CLI can control agents and worktrees (settings/notifications; cli/commands). Settings/providers documents installable Plugins for coding agents only; no loader for third-party Traycer panels, commands, or runtimes is documented.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: The traycer CLI supports agent creation, messaging, transcripts, and worktree management, but agent commands need Traycer-provided Task/agent context.

activity.changelogCadence: frequent: desktop stable releases on Sep 9, Sep 28, Sep 29 and Oct 1, 2026 (plus release candidates)

editorial.reachRationale: Product-specific signals include 11,734 downloads across the latest five mixed-component GitHub releases, 1,011 monthly CLI npm downloads, and a 1,746-member Discord. The company site reports 550K tasks and large IDE-extension install counts, but those are self-reported and not desktop active users; 1,576 stars measure attention only.
editorial.polishRationale: Signed desktop builds for three OSes, mobile apps, extensive documentation, fine-grained settings, and a 1.x stable release series support a finished product; iOS was TestFlight as of October 2026 and the changelog continues to fix UI and Host issues.
editorial.depthRationale: Managed worktrees and cleanup, diff/PR review, per-turn undo, planning artifacts, remote Hosts, model routing, multi-agent messaging, mobile access, and team sharing go well beyond session switching.
editorial.feelRationale: The desktop uses an Electron/TypeScript renderer (repository desktop package and language breakdown). The v1.4.0 changelog claims quicker long chats and lower memory, while v1.2.0 documents earlier multi-gigabyte sessions and smoother streaming after fixes; independent latency evidence is unavailable, so this is a cautious midrange score.

tools.name: TUIOS
tools.tagline: A window manager for your terminal.
tools.valueProp: A Go window manager inside the terminal you already use: floating windows and tiling layouts, a daemon that composes one session from panes on several machines, and a JSON protocol to script it all. Agents are manifest-driven with worktree fan-out and inter-agent mail; a restart restores layout, not conversations.

maker.name: Gaurav Gosain
maker.funding: none announced; solo GitHub repo (21 contributors on top of the maintainer) with a Ko-fi donation link in the README

pricing.notes: Free and MIT-licensed with no paid tier. TUIOS launches agent CLIs you already installed and are signed into; it makes no model calls of its own (unlike some peers, it has no built-in summarizer).

featureNotes.platforms.windows: Pre-built binaries for Windows ship on the GitHub releases page alongside Linux, macOS and FreeBSD; the package-manager installs (Homebrew, AUR, Nix, install.sh) are Linux/macOS only.
featureNotes.platforms.web: A separate `tuios-web` binary serves the app over WebSocket/WebTransport to a browser. It has no login of its own; the docs say to put an authenticating proxy in front, or run `--insecure` on a trusted network.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: `tuios-web` (browser terminal) and `tuios ssh` (built-in SSH server with public-key auth) are both binaries you run yourself; no vendor server exists.
featureNotes.agents.anyCli: Add a manifest as a TOML file in `~/.config/tuios/harnesses/`: process-name/screen/title rules for state detection. With no manifest at all, any CLI still runs in a pane; it just won't report agent state.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: `tuios worktree new/ls/diff/rm` creates and removes the git worktree itself (under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/tuios/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>`) and the session inside it; branches are never deleted by the tool.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Each `worktree new` call creates one branch; `tuios fan N` creates N sibling branches (`stem`, `stem-2`, ...) from one prompt, each in its own worktree and session.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: `tuios worktree diff [--stat]` prints commits made on top of the base, uncommitted changes and untracked files as text in the terminal. There is no dedicated diff-viewer UI, comment thread or accept/reject flow.
featureNotes.isolation.checkpoints: Session resurrection after a daemon restart or reboot brings back window layout and working directories only; the docs state explicitly that running programs and scrollback do not come back, so an agent's conversation is not resumed.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: Any agent in a pane can call the same `tuios fan`, `worktree new` and messaging commands a person would, so an agent can spawn and message siblings through the control protocol/CLI. There is no distinct 'lead agent' orchestration role in the product itself.
featureNotes.orchestration.automations: Hooks run shell commands on nine events (window, workspace, session attach, agent state changes, etc.), configured per docs/HOOKS.md. No scheduled/cron-style runs are documented.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Desktop notification, a clickable dock message, sound/bell, and a configurable shell command, with per-state toggles, `suppress_focused` and `quiet_hours` (`[notifications.agent]`). Alerts are raised by an attached client, so a fully detached session tracks state without announcing it.
featureNotes.orchestration.crossAgentMessaging: `tuios send-agent-message`, `ask-agent` (types a question and waits for the pane to settle) and a per-session stash for shared files, with threads, an inbox per pane plus a `human` inbox, and rate limits/loop-refusal to stop accidental agent-to-agent loops. Messages are held in memory only and lost when the daemon stops.
featureNotes.collaboration.sharedSessions: Several terminal clients (local or over SSH) can attach to and mirror one daemon session at once, tmux-style; there are no per-user accounts or a separate cursor/selection per client.
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: No telemetry, analytics or crash-reporting code found in the repo tree (searched for telemetry/analytics/posthog/sentry paths) and no telemetry disclosure on the site or in the docs; `tuios update` only checks or updates when run by hand, with no documented automatic phone-home.
featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Extends the app itself, but only at the config/scripting tier, not by loading third-party code: (1) a documented, self-describing JSON control protocol (docs/control-protocol), line-delimited JSON over a Unix socket with 62 verbs that can create/close windows, split and retile, change options and themes live, read/write panes, and stream events, is exactly the 'scripting or control protocol that can drive the app from outside' bar for partial; (2) `[hooks]` (docs/hooks) run a shell command on daemon/client lifecycle events (new window, focus, workspace switch, agent state, attach/detach); (3) `[dock.custom.<name>]` (docs/configuration#custom-components) backs a dock cell with a shell command and on-click action; (4) TOML agent-harness manifests (`~/.config/tuios/harnesses/*.toml`) only add detection rules for the process-scanner, not new panels or commands. TUIOS's own comparison page states this plainly: "Extending: Hooks, dock components, control protocol. No plugins", contrasted explicitly with herdr's plugin directory (executable + manifest) and marketplace, and zellij's WebAssembly plugins, which TUIOS does not have.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: A line-delimited JSON control protocol on the daemon's Unix socket (self-describing via `list-verbs`, `list-verbs --json`) underlies every CLI command, plus a read-only `tuios mcp` MCP server scoped to the agent's own session by default.

github.description: A terminal window manager that knows what your agents are doing. Tiling panes, workspaces, sessions that survive restarts, and one Inbox for every coding agent.

top.title: (⌐■_■) TUIOS is an experimental terminal tiling multiplexer

activity.changelogCadence: irregular; the only tagged release (v0.7.0) is from March 2026, but a rolling 'since v0.7.0' changelog page on the site is updated alongside near-daily commits and dated blog posts (newest 22 Sept 2026)

editorial.reachRationale: Real but early-stage signals: 3.7k stars, 21 contributors, a Terminal Trove 'Tool of the Week' badge and multiple package-manager listings (Homebrew, AUR, Nix, Docker) show genuine adoption and outside contribution, discounted against distribution numbers that are small (31 Homebrew installs/30d, 6,524 total release-asset downloads) and a Show HN that drew only 5 points and 0 comments; no Discord and no product X account to weigh at all. TUIOS's own comparison page puts its closest peer, herdr, at roughly 10x its stars, contributors and installs, which is consistent with placing TUIOS a tier below herdr's 'established'.
editorial.polishRationale: An unusually complete docs site (20+ pages plus a from-tmux/from-zellij interactive tutorial that runs the real app in-browser), a public engineering blog with dated, specific postmortems, 342 built-in themes, shell completions, six install methods, a CLI-driven settings page, and a maker-written comparison page against six competitors that is candid about where TUIOS loses. Remaining rough edges: several shipped pieces are flagged experimental or beta in the docs themselves (sixel clipping, the OSC 66 text-sizing protocol, remote panes), the only tagged release dates to March 2026 even as main moves daily, and the browser terminal ships with no authentication of its own.
editorial.depthRationale: Well past a tmux wrapper, it creates and fans out git worktrees itself, gives agents a mailbox/ask/reply protocol with a human inbox and a file stash, federates sessions across machines (including panes and even a single session spanning several hosts), and exposes a self-describing JSON control protocol plus an MCP server. It stops short of PR creation, merge assistance, a task board, or resuming an agent's conversation after a restart (only layout and a fresh shell come back).
editorial.feelRationale: Pure Go TUI with event-driven rendering the docs describe as zero-CPU at idle, no Electron or web-view layer, and a public blog series of specific, measured performance fixes (a scrollback ring cut from 232MB to 2.2MB per pane, a resize-lag fix validated with Go benchmarks and pprof, frame-composition profiling). Held back because the distributed release binaries use TUIOS's own pure-Go terminal emulator by default (the faster libghostty-vt backend is opt-in and needs building from source with zig), and the docs themselves flag known rough edges in newer graphics protocols (sixel clipping, OSC 66 text sizing); no third-party performance complaints turned up in a search, but none praised it either.

tools.name: Vibe Kanban
tools.tagline: Your Engineering Bottleneck Has Shifted
tools.valueProp: The original kanban-for-agents: issues feed worktree workspaces, and inline diff comments plus a preview browser send review straight back to the agent. Its maker shut down in April 2026, so the hosted tier is gone and the app is community-maintained.

maker.name: bloop (BLOOP AI LIMITED)
maker.funding: VC-backed (investors thanked in the shutdown post); company shut down 2026-04-10, project handed to the community

pricing.notes: Free to run; you authenticate with each coding agent's own CLI login. The pricing page listed Free / Pro $30 per user per month (2-49 users, SLA, Discord support) / Enterprise (50+, SSO/SAML) as of September 2026, but the 2026-04-10 shutdown post says all subscriptions were terminated and refunded, and hosted remote services (issues, comments, projects, organisations) were removed 30 days later.

featureNotes.openness.pluginSystem: Config-level only, not code-loading: there is no plugin/extension SDK for adding a panel, view or command to Vibe Kanban itself. Per-project Setup, Dev Server and Cleanup Scripts (docs/core-features/creating-projects) are arbitrary shell commands the app itself runs at fixed lifecycle points around every agent execution ('Setup scripts will be run before the coding agent is executed'; cleanup scripts run after a coding agent finishes its turn, 'treat it like a git pre-commit hook'), a documented, narrow-scope hook mechanism, matching the config-level bar for partial. Settings → Agents (docs/settings/agent-configurations) similarly lets you define named configuration profiles with custom environment variables that point an existing built-in agent (e.g. Claude Code) at a third-party provider endpoint such as Z.ai or OpenRouter, a custom-provider-by-config extension point. By contrast, MCP server configuration (docs/settings/mcp-servers) explicitly 'update[s] the global configuration file of the coding agent' and is agent-side, not Vibe Kanban's own surface, and does not count.
featureNotes.platforms.macos: Tauri desktop app (.dmg, x64 and aarch64) in GitHub releases; the npx web app also runs on macOS.
featureNotes.platforms.windows: Tauri desktop app (.msi / setup.exe, x64 and arm64) in GitHub releases; the npx web app also runs on Windows.
featureNotes.platforms.linux: Tauri desktop app (.deb / .AppImage, amd64 and aarch64) in GitHub releases; the npx web app also runs on Linux.
featureNotes.platforms.web: `npx vibe-kanban` serves a local web UI; Remote Access lets a phone browser reach a paired host via cloud.vibekanban.com or a self-hosted relay.
featureNotes.platforms.cli: `npx vibe-kanban` only launches the server/UI and `--mcp` starts a stdio MCP server; there is no CLI for creating or steering agent runs.
featureNotes.execution.remoteOwn: README documents running on a remote server behind Cloudflare Tunnel/ngrok with 'Open in VS Code' generating ssh-remote URLs; Remote Access pairs a phone to a host through a relay that was vendor-hosted and sunset after the April 2026 shutdown, or self-hosted.
featureNotes.execution.selfHostServer: Docker Compose stack for 'Vibe Kanban Cloud' (remote server, relay, Postgres, ElectricSQL) with GitHub/Google OAuth or a single bootstrap admin login.
featureNotes.agents.copilotCli: Listed as 'GitHub Copilot CLI' on the supported agents page.
featureNotes.agents.cursorAgent: Listed as 'Cursor Agent CLI'.
featureNotes.isolation.worktrees: One git worktree per workspace under .vibe-kanban-workspaces, created automatically with setup scripts; cleaned up after completion.
featureNotes.isolation.branchPerTask: Working branch auto-named like vk/abc123-add-login-page from the target branch.
featureNotes.isolation.diffReview: Unified/side-by-side diff with inline comments that are batched and sent to the agent as the next message.
featureNotes.isolation.prCreation: GitHub PRs from the Git panel or command bar with AI-generated description and draft option; multi-repo workspaces create one PR per repo.
featureNotes.isolation.mergeAssist: 'Merge' pulls the target branch into the working branch, prompts to rebase when behind, and shows a conflict indicator; local merge of the workspace branch is also offered.
featureNotes.orchestration.taskBoard: Kanban issues, sub-issues, priorities and tags required signing in to Vibe Kanban Cloud; the hosted service was withdrawn after the April 2026 shutdown, so the board needs the self-hosted Docker stack. Without sign-in only workspaces are available.
featureNotes.orchestration.subagents: No orchestrator agent, but the local MCP server (`vibe-kanban --mcp`) exposes issue and workspace tools that agents running inside Vibe Kanban can call.
featureNotes.orchestration.notifications: Sound effects and browser push notifications when tasks complete, need attention or error.
featureNotes.collaboration.multiUser: Organisations with Admin/Member roles and email invites existed in Vibe Kanban Cloud; the hosted service is sunset, and the self-host guide's bootstrap login is a single shared credential unless you configure OAuth.
featureNotes.openness.selfHostable: Local app works without an account; the cloud/relay stack ships as Docker Compose. Analytics default to PostHog unless disabled.
featureNotes.openness.byoSubscription: Each agent page tells you to log in with the agent's own CLI first (e.g. `npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code`).
featureNotes.openness.telemetryOptOut: `analytics_enabled` config flag (defaults true) and PostHog is disabled entirely when POSTHOG_API_KEY is empty at build time.
featureNotes.openness.apiOrMcp: Local-only stdio MCP server for organisations, projects, issues, workspaces and task execution; a REST backend the frontend uses (origins gated by VK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS).
